title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄序
皇上紀元之歲爲萬曆癸酉維時
百度聿新諸司据法守正吏
治蒸蒸各臻于理乃秋八月
會天下當舉士于鄉先期應
天府臣循
制以請
===
上命臣應期臣洛文往典試事臣
應期伏自惟省臣嘗兩佐辟
廱忝預造士經學行能罔可
楷式恒日惴惴懼也不自意
過被
簡命膺校士之役夫以臣之寡昧
輒不自量曩忝與六館生徒
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄序
皇上紀元之歲，爲萬曆癸酉。維時百度聿新，諸司据法守正，吏治蒸蒸，各臻于理。乃秋八月，會天下當舉士于鄉，先期，應天府臣循制以請。上命臣應期、臣洛文往典試事。臣應期伏自惟省，臣嘗兩佐辟廱，忝預造士，經學行能，罔可楷式，恒日惴惴懼也。不自意過被簡命，膺校士之役。夫以臣之寡昧，輒不自量，曩忝與六館生徒
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

The first year of His Majesty's reign era was the guiyou year of Wanli (1573). At that time, all measures of governance were newly revitalized, the various offices adhered to the law and upheld rectitude, and official administration flourished, each department attaining good order. Then, in the eighth month of autumn, as the realm was due to recommend scholars through the Provincial Examinations, ahead of the scheduled date the officials of Yingtian Prefecture followed the established system to submit a request. His Majesty commanded your servant Yingqi and your servant Luowen to go and preside over the examination affairs.

Your servant Yingqi humbly reflected upon himself: your servant had twice assisted in the Directorate of Education (Biyong) and unworthily participated in the training of scholars; yet in classical learning, conduct, and ability, I had nothing that could serve as a model, and thus I was constantly filled with trepidation each day. Never did I expect to be unduly favored with a selective appointment and entrusted with the duty of evaluating scholars. Given your servant's scant knowledge and obscurity, without taking my own measure, in the past I unworthily joined the students of the Six Halls…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
考厲志業以不負
聖朝育才至意而逡巡歲月靡效
涓埃私心誠竊愧之矧兹蒐
羅羣材限以三日之試冀所
登進足備
任使豈臣之愚所能稱塞故臣
自受
===
詔
陛辭匝月而始達境藉寐食飲
時時若有神鑒不啻躋岱臨
淵而懼顛隕也既入棘則偕
同事諸臣胥誓胥戒而後即
事乃合提學御史臣謝廷傑
暨諸曹六館所選士四千五
punctuated: 考厲志業，以不負聖朝育才至意，而逡巡歲月，靡效涓埃，私心誠竊愧之。矧兹蒐羅羣材，限以三日之試，冀所登進足備任使，豈臣之愚所能稱塞？故臣自受詔陛辭，匝月而始達境，藉寐食飲，時時若有神鑒，不啻躋岱臨淵而懼顛隕也。既入棘，則偕同事諸臣，胥誓胥戒而後即事。乃合提學御史臣謝廷傑暨諸曹六館所選士四千五
translation_en: …examine and encourage their aspirations and studies, so as not to fail the sacred dynasty's utmost intention of nurturing talent. Yet as the months and years slipped by, I failed to contribute even the slightest bit, and in my private heart I was truly and secretly ashamed of this. How much more so now, when gathering a multitude of talents is restricted to a three-day examination, in the hope that those advanced and selected will suffice to be ready for appointment and service—how could someone as foolish as your servant be equal to fulfilling this responsibility? Therefore, from the time your servant received the imperial decree and took leave of the throne, taking a full month before reaching the jurisdiction, whether sleeping on my mat or eating and drinking, at every moment it was as though spirits were watching over me—no less than climbing Mount Tai or standing at the edge of an abyss in fear of falling and perishing. Once I entered the examination compound, together with all the officials sharing in the task, we mutually swore oaths and admonished one another before taking up our duties. Thereupon, we gathered the four thousand five… [students] selected by the Education-intendant Censor, your servant Xie Tingjie 謝廷傑, as well as the various agencies and the Six Halls of the Directorate of Education…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
百有奇三試之遵
制額舉百三十有五人鐫其名
氏與其所爲文二十篇成録
以
獻〔臣〕始進多士語之曰是舉也
我
皇上紹
===
帝臨君額俊率典之一初也諸所
舉皆產
畿服育成均所謂
豐芑之詒乘時翼
運者也爾諸士亦知所感遇思
奮乎昔我
皇祖定鼎金陵綏猷彰軌
punctuated: 百有奇，三試之。遵制額，舉百三十有五人，鐫其名氏與其所爲文二十篇，成録以獻。〔臣〕始進多士，語之曰：「是舉也，我皇上紹帝臨君，額俊率典之一初也。諸所舉皆產畿服、育成均，所謂豐芑之詒，乘時翼運者也。爾諸士亦知所感遇思奮乎？昔我皇祖定鼎金陵，綏猷彰軌，
translation_en: … hundred and more, and examined them across three sessions. In accordance with the imperially decreed quota, we selected one hundred and thirty-five men as provincial graduates (juren), engraved their names and twenty of the essays written for the occasion, and compiled this record to present to the throne. When Your Servant first brought forward the many scholars, I addressed them, saying: "This examination is the very first occasion on which our August Emperor, having succeeded to the imperial throne to rule as sovereign, selects men of talent according to the established canons. All those who have been selected were born in the Metropolitan domain or nurtured in the National University (Chengjun)—those of whom the Classic of Poetry speaks as the legacy left in Feng where the white millet grew, seizing the moment to assist the dynastic destiny. Do all you scholars also know to feel gratitude for this auspicious encounter and aspire to exert yourselves? In former times, when our August Ancestor established the imperial capital at Jinling [Nanjing], pacifying the realm with his plans and manifesting the proper standards, …

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
南都稱
首善地爾諸士游息長養被化
宜深矧茲躡
昌明之景際
聖作之期不有瑰瑋英特之彥先
四方而充貢籍其自待之謂
何我
===
皇上秉籙御天作新萬國遐方殊
族慕
德嚮
風矧多士發藻
周南首被掄薦即碌碌無可表
見曷以倡郡國士邪臣聞之
堯舜之世臣主俱聖合謀相
punctuated: 南都稱首善地，爾諸士游息長養，被化宜深。矧茲躡昌明之景，際聖作之期，不有瑰瑋英特之彥，先四方而充貢籍，其自待之謂何？我皇上秉籙御天，作新萬國，遐方殊族，慕德嚮風；矧多士發藻周南，首被掄薦，即碌碌無可表見，曷以倡郡國士邪？臣聞之：堯、舜之世，臣主俱聖，合謀相
translation_en: … making the Southern Capital renowned as the place of foremost excellence. Since all of you scholars have studied, rested, and grown to maturity here, you ought to have been deeply imbued with its transforming influence. How much more so now, when you tread upon a scene of flourishing brightness and encounter an era of sagely creation! If there are not extraordinary, heroic, and outstanding talents among you who take the lead before the bốn quarters in filling the rosters of tribute scholars, what would that say of the expectations you hold for yourselves? Our Emperor holds the sacred mandate and rules the realm, renewing the myriad states so that distant regions and foreign peoples admire His virtue and turn toward His transforming wind. How much more so for the many scholars who display their literary brilliance here in Zhounan and are the first to be selected and recommended! If you are merely mediocre and have nothing by which to distinguish yourselves, how could you serve as leaders for the scholars of the commanderies and principalities? Your servant has heard that in the age of Yao and Shun, both ministers and rulers were sages, uniting their counsels to mutually…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
輔乃其時黎獻共臣九德翕
受故能師師敬應後先相承
古今稱綦治者蔑加焉
今天子神智天授豫
欽明濬哲之資
講學
勤政無間寒暑孳孳欲爲
===
堯舜者所謂作民
明辟寔維其始也爾諸士席珍有
年一旦離奥渫而躡風雲之
會鄙異時銜
命服官建夷夔皐禼之業亦必自
今日始方今
廟廊之上濟濟多賢昭
punctuated: 輔，乃其時黎獻共臣，九德翕受，故能師師敬應，後先相承，古今稱綦治者蔑加焉。今天子神智天授，豫欽明濬哲之資，講學勤政，無間寒暑，孳孳欲爲堯、舜者，所謂作民明辟，寔維其始也。爾諸士席珍有年，一旦離奥渫而躡風雲之會，鄙異時銜命服官，建夷、夔、皐、禼之業，亦必自今日始。方今廟廊之上，濟濟多賢，昭
translation_en: …assisted one another. Moreover, at that time the worthy elders among the multitude all served as ministers, and those possessing the nine virtues were harmoniously accepted into office; thus, officials could emulate one another in reverent response, succeeding one another from first to last, so that among all eras past and present praised for supreme governance, none could surpass theirs. Today the Son of Heaven, endowed by Heaven with divine wisdom and possessing beforehand the qualities of reverent clarity and profound perspicacity, engages in scholarly lectures and attends diligently to state affairs without interruption through winter cold or summer heat. Working tirelessly in his desire to become a Yao or a Shun, this is truly the very beginning of what is called acting as an enlightened sovereign for the people. You scholars have cherished your treasured talents upon the mat for many years; now, in a single day, you leave obscurity and humility to tread upon a opportune convergence of wind and clouds. Expecting [?] that in the future, when you hold the imperial mandate and serve in office, you will establish achievements like those of Boyi, Kui, Gaoyao, and Xie—this too must begin from today. At present, above in the imperial court, there is a dignified multitude of worthy men who manifest…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
德弼違非帝道弗舉既足以對揚
新命光輔
鴻圖矣而臣於諸士之始進也顧
騶而期之若是豈不謂
明良啓運千載一時興賢與能宜
先定志士方通籍弗首以帝
臣之道相勸勉致令臣
主異趣而後先不相及是臣之罪
也臣猥以凡流倖際
===
勳華交會之盛深惟謭劣既不能
以心所竊慶者自效諸身獨
幸承之茲役期得眞才以報
明主而凖瘝曠之咎因與諸同事
專精翕慮愼選旁蒐求古所
punctuated: 德弼違，非帝道弗舉，既足以對揚新命、光輔鴻圖矣。而臣於諸士之始進也，顧騶而期之若是，豈不謂明良啓運，千載一時，興賢與能，宜先定志？士方通籍，弗首以帝臣之道相勸勉，致令臣主異趣，而後先不相及，是臣之罪也。臣猥以凡流，倖際勳華交會之盛，深惟謭劣，既不能以心所竊慶者自效諸身，獨幸承之茲役，期得眞才以報明主，而凖瘝曠之咎。因與諸同事專精翕慮，愼選旁蒐，求古所
translation_en: … virtue and rectifying errors, advancing nothing that is not the Way of the Sage-Emperors; they are already sufficient to extol and carry out the New Mandate and gloriously assist the Great Enterprise. Yet as these scholars make their initial entry into advancement, I nonetheless urge [?] and expect this much of them—is it not because when an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers inaugurate a new era, a chance that comes once in a thousand years, in promoting the worthy and empowering the capable one ought first to fix their aspirations? When scholars are just having their names entered on the official register, if I do not first encourage and exhort them with the Way of being ministers to an Emperor, thereby causing ministers and sovereign to pursue different aims and those who come later to fail to match those who went before, that would be my offense. Though an ordinary man, I have had the good fortune to encounter this flourishing convergence of Yao and Shun. Deeply mindful of my own shallow incompetence, since I am unable to personally put into effect what my heart secretly rejoices in, I am uniquely fortunate to have been entrusted with this service, hoping to obtain true talent in order to repay our Enlightened Ruler and offset [?] the blame for neglecting my office. Therefore, together with my colleagues, we have concentrated our spirits and united our thoughts, carefully selecting and searching far and wide to seek those whom the ancients…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
稱俊乂之儔而薦之
上庶不辱
聖明首舉將他日熈載亮工之用
或少裨焉然臣所爲竭力披
校者藝焉已爾爾南金東箭爛
然溢睫其行業固無自見也
諸士行且上南宮奉
===
制對程行計功有日矣
天子垂意至寧思臻古道試令就
列安所自效邪夫竭精發憤
期以致用士之夙心也遇
主遭時俾獲自見士之所大幸也
爾諸士觀光
盛際挾筴
punctuated: 稱俊乂之儔，而薦之上，庶不辱聖明首舉，將他日熈載亮工之用，或少裨焉。然臣所爲竭力披校者，藝焉已爾；爾南金東箭，爛然溢睫，其行業固無自見也。諸士行且上南宮，奉制對，程行計功有日矣。天子垂意至寧，思臻古道，試令就列，安所自效邪？夫竭精發憤，期以致用，士之夙心也；遇主遭時，俾獲自見，士之所大幸也。爾諸士觀光盛際，挾筴
translation_en: … called men of outstanding talent and virtue, and present them to His Majesty. In this way we may perhaps not disgrace the first examination held under His Sacred and Enlightened reign, and may offer some modest help toward the future tasks of brightening imperial undertakings and aiding the ruler's work. Yet that which I have exhausted my strength to sift and evaluate is nothing more than literary skill; although you are like the gold of the south and the bamboo arrows of the east, dazzlingly filling our eyes, your actual conduct and achievements have as yet had no way to manifest themselves. You gentlemen are about to go up to the Southern Palace [the Ministry of Rites for the Metropolitan Examination] and receive the Emperor's decree to reply to; the day when your conduct will be measured and your achievements reckoned is not far off. The Son of Heaven turns His thoughts toward supreme peace and longs to attain the Way of antiquity. Suppose you are placed in the ranks of officials—how will you prove your worth? Now, to exhaust one's spirit and rouse one's ardor in the hope of being put to practical use is the long-held aspiration of a scholar; to encounter a worthy sovereign and meet with the right times, thereby gaining the opportunity to manifest oneself, is a scholar's greatest fortune. You gentlemen, beholding the glory of this flourishing era and clasping your writing tablets in…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
清朝
王德前徽章章較著從違趣舍惟
在一心正如登高順風其呼
易也誠及是時明正始之道
端向往之的砥節礪行秉德
持操而又閑邪于幽獨程行
于前修善有法惡有懲毋忽
===
眞而崇僞毋棄實以鈞名居
則學求爲已出則志存立功
卽見用操茲往焉臣所謂帝
臣者道若是止爾斯何計材
具長短名蹟顯晦所以應
昌期揚
庥命者寔在於茲臣籍是可幸無
punctuated: 清朝，王德前徽，章章較著，從違趣舍，惟在一心，正如登高順風，其呼易也。誠及是時，明正始之道，端向往之的，砥節礪行，秉德持操，而又閑邪于幽獨，程行于前修，善有法，惡有懲，毋忽眞而崇僞，毋棄實以鈞名，居則學求爲已，出則志存立功，卽見用操茲往焉。臣所謂帝臣者，道若是止爾。斯何計材具長短、名蹟顯晦？所以應昌期、揚庥命者，寔在於茲。臣籍是可幸無
translation_en: … pure court. The royal virtues and past models of excellence are brilliantly manifest. Whether to follow or violate them, what to pursue and what to discard, depends solely on one's own heart—just like shouting into the wind from a high vantage point, where one's call carries with ease. Truly, if you seize this moment to clarify the Way of rectifying beginnings, set straight the target of your aspirations, temper your integrity and refine your conduct, hold fast to virtue and maintain your principles, and furthermore guard against depravity in unseen solitude and measure your actions against the worthy predecessors—taking the good as your model and the bad as a warning, neither neglecting the genuine to exalt the false nor abandoning substance to fish for fame, in private life pursuing learning for self-cultivation and in public office setting your ambition on establishing merit—then when you are employed, you will go forth upholding these principles. What I call being a minister fit for an emperor is a Way that goes no further than this. What need is there, then, to calculate the strengths and weaknesses of one's talents or the prominence and obscurity of one's reputation and achievements? That by which you respond to this flourishing era and extol the auspicious mandate truly lies herein. Relying on this, I may count myself fortunate to be free from…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
責脫或不然而徒剽儒以棲
榮執空文以自見即他時躋
列崇要衆見謂踔絕便敏識
者且唾訾之將謂科目不足
以得人藝文奚取于實用都
人士不足爲萬民望也斯不
負
===
聖天子文治維新之一會哉若是
者無論諸士不容于
堯舜之世臣業已舉之安所傳其
罪也爾諸士其勗諸是役也
提調則府尹臣承學府丞臣
標同考則推官臣大倫臣宗
武臣垓知縣臣蘭臣一櫝教
punctuated: 責。脫或不然，而徒剽儒以棲榮，執空文以自見，即他時躋列崇要，衆見謂踔絕便敏，識者且唾訾之，將謂科目不足以得人，藝文奚取于實用，都人士不足爲萬民望也，斯不負聖天子文治維新之一會哉？若是者，無論諸士不容于堯、舜之世，臣業已舉之，安所傳其罪也？爾諸士其勗諸！是役也，提調則府尹臣承學、府丞臣標；同考則推官臣大倫、臣宗武、臣垓，知縣臣蘭、臣一櫝，教
translation_en:
… blame. Should it turn out otherwise—if they merely plagiarize Confucian learning to roost in glory and cling to empty words to show themselves off—then even if in the future they ascend to the ranks of exalted and vital offices, and the crowd regards them as surpassingly brilliant and nimble, men of discernment will spit upon and disparage them. People will say that the examination system is inadequate for obtaining men of talent, ask what practical use can be derived from literary compositions, and declare that the scholars of the capital are unworthy to be looked up to by the myriad people. Would this not betray this unique occasion of the Sacred Son of Heaven's renewal of civil governance? Should it be like this, not only would you scholars not be tolerated in an age of Yao and Shun, but since I, His Majesty's servant, have already recommended them, how could I shift the blame [for their offenses, reading 傳 as 逭]? You scholars, exert yourselves in this!

In this undertaking, the Proctors were Prefect of Yingtian His Majesty's servant Chengxue 承學 and Vice Prefect His Majesty's servant Biao 標; the Associate Examiners were Prefectural Judges His Majesty's servants Dalun 大倫, Zongwu 宗武, and Gai 垓, District Magistrates His Majesty's servants Lan 蘭 and Yidu 一櫝, Prefectural Director of Studies …

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
授〔臣益純臣從教臣志學〕
正〔臣大年〕教諭〔臣希孟臣東〕
昌監試則御史〔臣堂臣守德〕
寔相與祗事而奉例防檢于
外者御史〔臣石檟臣王宣化〕
也於法得並書云
左春坊左中允兼翰林院編
修范應期謹序
punctuated:
授〔臣益純、臣從教、臣志學〕、正〔臣大年〕、教諭〔臣希孟、臣東〕昌，監試則御史〔臣堂、臣守德〕，寔相與祗事；而奉例防檢于外者，御史〔臣石檟、臣王宣化〕也。於法得並書云。
左春坊左中允兼翰林院編修范應期謹序。
translation_en:
…Instructors (jiaoshou) [His Majesty's servants Yichun 益純, Congjiao 從教, and Zhixue 志學], Director of Studies (xuezheng) [?] [His Majesty's servant Danian 大年], and Instructors (jiaoyu) [His Majesty's servants Ximeng 希孟 and Dong]chang 東昌; as for the Monitoring of the Examination (jianshi), Censors (yushi) [His Majesty's servants Tang 堂 and Shoude 守德] truly discharged their duties together with reverence; and those who in accordance with precedent maintained security and inspection on the outside were Censors [His Majesty's servants Shi Jia 石檟 and Wang Xuanhua 王宣化]. By regulation, they may all be recorded together here.

Respectfully prefaced by Fan Yingqi 范應期, Left Companion (zuo zhongyun) of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent (zuo chunfang) concurrently serving as Junior Compiler (bianxiu) in the Hanlin Academy (Hanlin yuan).

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
萬曆元年應天府鄉試
提調官
嘉議大夫應天府府尹陶承學〔子述浙江會稽縣人丁未進士〕

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子張問政子曰居之無倦行之以忠
修身則道立尊賢則不惑
君仁莫不仁君義莫不義君正莫不正一
正君而國定矣
易
直其正也方其義也君子敬以直內義以
方外
===
象曰益損上益下民說无疆自上下下其
道大光利有攸往中正有慶利涉大川
木道乃行益動而巽日進无疆天施地
生其益无方凡益之道與時偕行
乾以易知坤以簡能
齊也者言萬物之潔齊也
書
惟德動天無遠弗屆滿招損謙受益時乃
天道
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
子張問政。子曰：「居之無倦，行之以忠。」
修身則道立，尊賢則不惑。
君仁，莫不仁；君義，莫不義；君正，莫不正。一正君而國定矣。

易
直其正也，方其義也。君子敬以直內，義以方外。
象曰：益，損上益下，民說无疆。自上下下，其道大光。利有攸往，中正有慶。利涉大川，木道乃行。益動而巽，日進无疆。天施地生，其益无方。凡益之道，與時偕行。
乾以易知，坤以簡能。
齊也者，言萬物之潔齊也。

書
惟德動天，無遠弗屆。滿招損，謙受益，時乃天道。
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books (Sishu):
1. Zizhang asked about governance. The Master said, "Hold it in your mind without growing weary; carry it out in action with loyalty." (Analects 12.14)
2. By cultivating one's own person, the Way is established; by honoring the worthy, one does not fall into perplexity. (Doctrine of the Mean 20)
3. When the ruler is benevolent, no one is not benevolent; when the ruler is righteous, no one is not righteous; when the ruler is rectified, no one is not rectified. Once the ruler is rectified, the state will be settled. (Mencius 4A.20)

Classic of Changes (Yi):
1. "Straight" means its rectitude; "square" means its righteousness. The noble man uses reverence to straighten his inner life, and righteousness to square his external conduct. (Hexagram 2, Kun, Wenyan Commentary)
2. The Commentary on the Decision (Tuanzhuan) says: "Increase (Yi): diminishing what is above to increase what is below, the people's joy is boundless. Descending from above to reach what is below, its Way shines brightly. 'It is favorable to have somewhere to go,' because centrality and correctness bring blessing. 'It is favorable to cross the great river,' because the Way of wood is thus put into action. Increase moves and is compliant, advancing daily without bound. Heaven bestows and Earth brings forth; its increase knows no limits. All that pertains to the Way of Increase proceeds in harmony with the time." (Hexagram 42, Yi)
3. Qian knows through the easy; Kun is capable through the simple. (Great Commentary, Xici 1.1)
4. "Ordering" (qi) means that the myriad things are made clean and even. (Discussion of the Trigrams, Shuogua 5)

Classic of Documents (Shu):
1. It is virtue alone that moves Heaven; there is no distance to which it does not reach. Fullness invites loss; humility receives benefit—this is the Way of Heaven. (Counsels of the Great Yu, Da Yu mo)

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
終始愼厥與惟明明后先王惟時懋敬厥
德克配上帝今王嗣有令緒尚監茲哉
若升高必自下若陟遐必自邇無輕民
事惟難無安厥位惟危愼終于始有言
逆于汝心必求諸道有言遜于汝志必
求諸非道嗚呼弗慮胡獲弗爲胡成一
人元良萬邦以貞
小大之臣咸懷忠良其侍御僕從罔匪正
人以旦夕承弼厥辟
昭升于上敷聞在下
===
詩
寬兮綽兮猗重較兮
天保定爾亦孔之固
有馮有翼有孝有德以引以翼豈弟君子
四方爲則顒顒卬卬如圭如璋令聞令
望豈弟君子四方爲綱
春秋
於乎皇考永世克孝念茲皇祖陟降庭止
punctuated:
終始愼厥與，惟明明后。先王惟時懋敬厥德，克配上帝。今王嗣有令緒，尚監茲哉！若升高，必自下；若陟遐，必自邇。無輕民事惟難，無安厥位惟危。愼終于始。有言逆于汝心，必求諸道；有言遜于汝志，必求諸非道。嗚呼！弗慮胡獲？弗爲胡成？一人元良，萬邦以貞。
小大之臣咸懷忠良，其侍御僕從罔匪正人，以旦夕承弼厥辟。
昭升于上，敷聞在下。
詩：
寬兮綽兮，猗重較兮。
天保定爾，亦孔之固。
有馮有翼，有孝有德，以引以翼。豈弟君子，四方爲則。顒顒卬卬，如圭如璋，令聞令望。豈弟君子，四方爲綱。
春秋：
於乎皇考，永世克孝。念茲皇祖，陟降庭止。
translation_en:
Be cautious from beginning to end in whom you associate with—only then will you be a truly enlightened ruler. The former king was ever diligent in revering his virtue, and so was able to match the Lord on High. Now that Your Majesty has succeeded to this fine inheritance, may you take this as your mirror! It is like ascending to a height: one must begin from below; it is like travelling afar: one must begin from near at hand. Do not take lightly the affairs of the people—think only of their difficulty; do not rest at ease in your position—think only of its peril. Be cautious of the end at the very beginning. When words go against your heart, you must seek whether they accord with the Way; when words conform to your will, you must seek whether they depart from the Way. Oh! Without thought, what can be gained? Without action, what can be achieved? When the One Man is supremely good, the myriad states are thereby rectified.

Ministers great and small all cherished loyalty and goodness; his attendants, grooms, and followers were none of them other than upright men, who morning and evening assisted and supported their sovereign.

Brightly it ascends on high, and widely it is heard of below.

Book of Odes (Shi):

How magnanimous, how indulgent! Leaning upon the double crossbar of his chariot!

Heaven protects and establishes you, in utmost security.

You have those to lean upon and those to assist you; you have those who are filial and those who have virtue, to lead you forward and to support you at your side. Easy and self-possessed lord, you are a model to the four quarters. Dignified and majestic, like a jade sceptre and a half-sceptre, of fine reputation and admirable renown—easy and self-possessed lord, you are the guiding cord of the four quarters.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
[Note: The passage below actually belongs to the Book of Odes; in the original woodblock it appears before the heading "Spring and Autumn Annals" or the heading was misplaced in transcription.]
Alas, my august father, through endless generations able to be filial! Thinking upon this august grandfather, ascending and descending in the court.

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
荊人來聘〔莊公二十有三年〕楚人伐鄭〔僖
公元年〕
春王正月城楚丘〔僖公二年〕夏叔詣會晉
趙鞅宋樂大心衛北宮喜鄭游吉曹人
邾人滕人薛人小邾人于黃父〔昭公二
十有五年〕
冬十月甲午叔孫得臣敗狄于鹹〔文公十
有一年〕
楚人及吳戰于長岸〔昭公十有七年〕
===
禮記
君子曰大德不官大道不器大信不約大
時不齊察於此四者可以有志於本矣
三王之祭川也皆先河而後海或源也
或委也此之謂務本
王者功成作樂治定制禮其功大者其樂
備其治辯者其禮具
是故明君在上則諸臣服從
儒有席上之珍以待聘夙夜强學以待問
punctuated:
荊人來聘。〔莊公二十有三年〕楚人伐鄭。〔僖公元年〕
春，王正月，城楚丘。〔僖公二年〕夏，叔詣會晉趙鞅、宋樂大心、衛北宮喜、鄭游吉、曹人、邾人、滕人、薛人、小邾人于黃父。〔昭公二十有五年〕
冬，十月，甲午，叔孫得臣敗狄于鹹。〔文公十有一年〕
楚人及吳戰于長岸。〔昭公十有七年〕

禮記
君子曰：「大德不官，大道不器，大信不約，大時不齊。察於此四者，可以有志於本矣。」三王之祭川也，皆先河而後海；或源也，或委也，此之謂務本。
王者功成作樂，治定制禮。其功大者其樂備，其治辯者其禮具。
是故明君在上，則諸臣服從。
儒有席上之珍以待聘，夙夜强學以待問，
translation_en:
“An envoy from Jing came on a mission of friendly inquiries.” [Twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang] “The people of Chu invaded Zheng.” [First year of Duke Xi]
“In spring, in the King’s first month, they walled Chuqiu.” [Second year of Duke Xi] “In summer, Shu Yi met with Zhao Yang of Jin, Yue Daxin of Song, Beigong Xi of Wei, You Ji of Zheng, and representatives from Cao, Zhu, Teng, Xue, and Little Zhu at Huangfu.” [Twenty-fifth year of Duke Zhao]
“In winter, in the tenth month, on the day jiawu, Shusun Dechen defeated the Di barbarians at Xian.” [Eleventh year of Duke Wen]
“The people of Chu and Wu fought a battle at Chang’an.” [Seventeenth year of Duke Zhao]

Record of Rites (Liji)
“The superior man says: ‘Great virtue is not confined to a single office; the great Way is not limited to a single instrument; great good faith does not require covenants; the great seasons are not uniform. By examining these four things, one may set one’s mind upon what is fundamental.’ When the Three Kings sacrificed to the waters, they all placed the Yellow River first and the sea afterward; the one is the source, the other the outlet—this is called attending to the fundamental.”
“When a true king has achieved his merit, he creates music; when his governance is settled, he institutes rites. The greater his merit, the more complete his music; the more comprehensive his governance, the more fully equipped his rites.”
“Therefore, when an enlightened ruler is above, all his ministers submit and obey.”
“The scholar (ru) possesses treasures upon his mat with which to await an invitation to office; from dawn to night he strives in learning to await questioning; …”

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
懷忠信以待舉力行以待取其自立有
如此者
第貳塲
論
人君先於虛巳
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令禮官勸學詔〔元朔五年〕
擬唐命馬懷素褚無量更日侍讀誥〔開元三年〕
===
擬宋王曾詮錄古先聖賢六十事繪圖以
獻上降詔褒美命禁署月進二十軸仍
鏤版印賜近臣謝表〔天聖元年〕
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
收支留難
禁止迎送
優恤軍屬
盜決河防
punctuated:
懷忠信以待舉，力行以待取，其自立有如此者。

第貳塲

論
人君先於虛巳。

詔、誥、表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令禮官勸學詔〔元朔五年〕
擬唐命馬懷素、褚無量更日侍讀誥〔開元三年〕
擬宋王曾詮錄古先聖賢六十事繪圖以獻，上降詔褒美，命禁署月進二十軸，仍鏤版印賜近臣謝表〔天聖元年〕

判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
收支留難
禁止迎送
優恤軍屬
盜決河防
translation_en:
…cherishes loyalty and trustworthiness while awaiting recommendation, and strives in conduct while awaiting selection; such is the way he establishes himself.

Second Session

Discourse:
"A ruler must first empty himself of self-regard."

Edict, Mandate, and Memorial [Candidates answer one]:
Imitation of a Han-dynasty edict ordering the ritual officials to encourage learning [5th year of the Yuanshuo era (124 BCE)].
Imitation of a Tang-dynasty mandate ordering Ma Huaisu 馬懷素 and Chu Wuliang 褚無量 to serve on alternating days as Expositor-in-waiting [3rd year of the Kaiyuan era (715 CE)].
Imitation of a Song-dynasty memorial of gratitude by Wang Zeng 王曾, after he selected and recorded sixty deeds of ancient sages and worthies and had them illustrated for presentation to the throne, whereupon the Emperor sent down an edict of praise, ordered the palace offices to submit twenty scrolls each month, and further had woodblocks carved to print and bestow copies upon close ministers [1st year of the Tiansheng era (1023 CE)].

Legal Judgments [Five items]:
Issuing service-record certificates for officials and functionaries;
Obstructing receipts and disbursements;
Prohibiting ceremonial welcoming and sending off;
Granting compassionate relief to military dependents;
Illicitly breaching river dikes.

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第叁塲
策五道
問人君之治天下其必由學乎然在昔帝
王或中身受命而後學或弱齡繼統而
始學若幼卽好學非大聖人不能也古
有生而神靈弱而能言者有靜淵疏通
欽明文思者有冲年明于庶物皃時志
如巨人者有身應律度生有聖瑞者謂
之幼能好學可歟後世亦有十歲通春
秋英年向儒術者矣有少卽機穎幼稱
聰睿者矣亦可若是班歟惟我
===
皇上之生
靈明夐異
十齡出閣
英穎妙悟
登極後卽
開講筵
精勤卓邁曠世僅見種種可述中外臣民快
punctuated:
第叁塲

策五道

問：人君之治天下，其必由學乎？然在昔帝王，或中身受命而後學，或弱齡繼統而始學；若幼卽好學，非大聖人不能也。古有生而神靈、弱而能言者，有靜淵疏通、欽明文思者，有冲年明于庶物、皃時志如巨人者，有身應律度、生有聖瑞者，謂之幼能好學可歟？後世亦有十歲通《春秋》、英年向儒術者矣，有少卽機穎、幼稱聰睿者矣，亦可若是班歟？惟我皇上之生，靈明夐異，十齡出閣，英穎妙悟，登極後卽開講筵，精勤卓邁，曠世僅見，種種可述，中外臣民快
translation_en:
Third Session

Five Policy Questions

Question: Does a ruler's governance of all under heaven necessarily derive from learning? Yet among the emperors and kings of old, some received the Mandate in middle age and only then studied, while others succeeded to the throne in youth and only then began to study; as for loving learning from infancy, none but a great sage is capable of it. In antiquity, there was one who was born divinely perceptive and could speak while still frail; there were those who were tranquil, deep, and penetratinglycomprehending, or reverent, intelligent, accomplished, and thoughtful; there were those who in their tender years were clear about the multitude of things, or who in infancy had the aspirations of a great man; and there were those whose person conformed to standard measures, or whose birth was attended by sagely auspices—can these be called capable of loving learning in childhood? In later ages too, there were those who at ten years of age mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) or in their flourishing youth inclined toward Confucian arts, and those who from youth were quick-witted and sharp, or in childhood were praised as clever and perspicacious—can they also be ranked with those? Now our August Emperor was born with spiritual intelligence far out of the ordinary; at ten years of age he came out to the pavilion for princely instruction, brilliantly perceptive and wonderfully discerning; and immediately after ascending the throne he opened the Classics Colloquium, with an unflagging diligence and lofty excellence rarely seen in any age. All these various deeds can be recounted, and officials and commoners within and without the court have delighted in…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
睹傳誦葢亦久矣其視上古數聖人椰
有同歟或謂
王上盛年得此至難然此
天資粹美耳若必
紹千聖之道統
開萬世之太平則
聖學固無涯涯尤有當務者在也其信然歟諸
士績學有日固爲致
君而來也尚明言之用爲啓沃者助
===
問易曰天垂象見吉凶而書曰先王克謹
天戒觀箕範之備庶徵春秋之紀災異
可攷已宋儒有言災者被于物而可知
異者不可知其所以然者也然則災異
固不同歟其說果何本歟漢劉向五行
傳論其言旁引曲證兾寤君心不知當
時能用其言亦可轉災爲祥歟乃宋儒
特爲譏駁抑又何歟後世五行有志天
文有考要皆祖循其說質以時變乃其
punctuated:
睹傳誦，葢亦久矣。其視上古數聖人，椰有同歟？或謂王上盛年得此至難，然此天資粹美耳；若必紹千聖之道統，開萬世之太平，則聖學固無涯涯，尤有當務者在也。其信然歟？諸士績學有日，固爲致君而來也，尚明言之，用爲啓沃者助。
問：《易》曰：「天垂象，見吉凶。」而《書》曰：「先王克謹天戒。」觀箕《範》之備庶徵，《春秋》之紀災異，可攷已。宋儒有言：「災者，被于物而可知；異者，不可知其所以然者也。」然則災異固不同歟？其說果何本歟？漢劉向《五行傳論》，其言旁引曲證，兾寤君心，不知當時能用其言，亦可轉災爲祥歟？乃宋儒特爲譏駁，抑又何歟？後世《五行》有志，《天文》有考，要皆祖循其說，質以時變，乃其
translation_en:
…to behold and pass on in praise, indeed for a long time now. Compared to those several sages of high antiquity, is there a similarity [?]? Some say that for His Majesty [?] to have attained this in his youthful prime is most difficult, yet this is merely the pure beauty of His heavenly endowment; if He is surely to carry on the transmission of the Way of a thousand sages and inaugurate great peace for ten thousand generations, then sage learning is indeed boundless [?], and there are especially pressing priorities that remain. Is this truly so? You gentlemen have accumulated learning for many days and have certainly come in order to serve the sovereign and bring him to perfection; set this forth clearly, so as to serve as an aid to those who enlighten and enrich His mind.

Question: The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "Heaven suspends images, manifesting good fortune and misfortune." And the Book of Documents (Shu) says: "The former kings were able to be謹 cautious toward the warnings of Heaven." Looking at how the Great Plan (Fan) of Viscount Ji sets forth in full the various verifications, and how the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records calamities and anomalies, this can already be examined. A Song-dynasty Confucian scholar said: "Calamities are things that fall upon creatures and can be known; anomalies are things of which one cannot know why they are so." This being so, are calamities and anomalies indeed different? Upon what is this theory actually based? In the Han dynasty, Liu Xiang's Discussions on the Tradition of the Five Phases (Wuxing zhuan lun) cited extensively and adduced intricate proofs in its words, hoping to awaken the sovereign's mind; I do not know whether, had they been able to employ his words at that time, they could also have turned calamities into auspiciousness? Yet Song-dynasty Confucian scholars specially criticized and refuted him—why was that, moreover? In later ages there were treatises on the Five Phases and investigations of Celestial Patterns; in essence they all followed his theories as their model and verified them against the changes of the times, yet among them…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
中有合有不合何歟有謂反常爲妖而
謬以爲祥者有謂其德不稱而反以致
亂者又何指歟我
太祖高皇帝熟知乾象敬忌
天威當其時求言有
詔中書有
勑所以
修德省愆者有可指陳其說歟
世宗肅皇帝
===
聖敬日躋欽崇
天道當其時有星變之
勑
納樂護之言其所以敬
天怒承
天休者何若是之兢兢歟我
皇上嗣服方新
厲精圖治頃因客星示異露禱
宫廷又復
punctuated: 中有合有不合，何歟？有謂反常爲妖而謬以爲祥者，有謂其德不稱而反以致亂者，又何指歟？我太祖高皇帝熟知乾象，敬忌天威，當其時求言有詔，中書有勑，所以修德省愆者，有可指陳其說歟？世宗肅皇帝聖敬日躋，欽崇天道，當其時有星變之勑，納樂護之言，其所以敬天怒、承天休者，何若是之兢兢歟？我皇上嗣服方新，厲精圖治，頃因客星示異，露禱宫廷，又復
translation_en: …among them some correspond to the facts and some do not—why is this? There are those who say that what violates the norm is an ominous prodigy yet mistakenly take it to be an auspicious sign, and those who say that when one's virtue does not match [an auspicious sign], it on the contrary brings about disorder—to what do these refer? Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu), was thoroughly conversant with celestial phenomena and reverently stood in awe of the majesty of Heaven. In his time, there were edicts seeking candid remonstrance and directives to the Secretariat; as for the ways in which he cultivated virtue and examined his faults, can you point out and set forth the accounts thereof? The世宗 (Shizong), Emperor Su, saw his sagely reverence rise daily as he venerated the Way of Heaven. In his time, there was the directive on stellar anomalies and the acceptance of the words of Yue Hu; in the ways he revered the wrath of Heaven and received the blessings of Heaven, why was he so cautiously attentive as this? Our August Emperor has newly succeeded to the throne and is rousing his spirit to strive for good governance. Recently, because a guest star manifested an anomaly, he prayed in the open air in the palace courtyard, and furthermore…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
中飭臣工痛加修省
畏
天一念光于
祖
宗數月之間旋見銷滅矣而雨澤或至愆期災
禝屢形奏牘議者謂臣下不能奉行
德教所致其盡然歟抑或修弭之術當
上下各任其責歟願究言之執事者將轉聞于
上也
===
問天下元元之命係于守令爲其職近民
而恩易及人也三代而下言治民者莫
盛于漢如班固范曄所傳兩漢循吏可
攷已間有一二廉幹之士撥劇整亂奉
公而不顧私斯亦吏治之踔絕者今試
舉其事言之有免京兆而三老訟其功
守東郡而吏民壯其節者有視事馮翊
而贓吏解去奏更二令而兩邑皆治者
有閉閤自責而吏不忍欺有擢用長者
punctuated:
中飭臣工，痛加修省。畏天一念，光于祖宗，數月之間，旋見銷滅矣。而雨澤或至愆期，災禝屢形奏牘，議者謂臣下不能奉行德教所致，其盡然歟？抑或修弭之術，當上下各任其責歟？願究言之，執事者將轉聞于上也。
問：天下元元之命，係于守令，爲其職近民而恩易及人也。三代而下，言治民者莫盛于漢，如班固、范曄所傳兩漢循吏，可攷已。間有一二廉幹之士，撥劇整亂，奉公而不顧私，斯亦吏治之踔絕者。今試舉其事言之：有免京兆而三老訟其功，守東郡而吏民壯其節者；有視事馮翊而贓吏解去，奏更二令而兩邑皆治者；有閉閤自責而吏不忍欺，有擢用長者
translation_en:
… admonished his officials and functionaries [likely 申飭 for 中飭] to painfully cultivate and examine themselves. This single thought of revering Heaven added luster to the Imperial Ancestors, and within a few months, the anomaly soon vanished. Yet timely rains have sometimes failed to arrive on schedule, and portents and calamities [likely 災祲 for 災禝] have repeatedly appeared in memorialized reports. Commentators say this is brought about by ministers and subordinates being unable to carry out his virtuous teachings—is this entirely so? Or is it that in the art of moral cultivation to avert calamities, superior and inferior ought each to bear their own responsibility? I wish you to speak of this exhaustively, as the managers of affairs will transmit your words to the hearing of His Majesty above.

Question: The lives of the common people of the realm depend upon the Grand Administrators (shou) and Magistrates (ling), because their offices are close to the people and their grace easily reaches others. Since the Three Dynasties, when speaking of governing the people, no era was more flourishing than the Han; the upright officials (xunli) of the Two Han dynasties recorded in the biographies by Ban Gu 班固 and Fan Ye 范曄 can readily be examined. Among others, there were also one or two incorrupt and capable gentlemen who cut through complex affairs and brought order to chaos, upholding the public good without regard for private interest—these too were extraordinary examples of administrative governance. Let us now try to cite their deeds and speak of them: there was one who was dismissed as Metropolitan Commandant (Jingzhao) yet had the Thrice Venerable (sanlao) defend his merits, and who served as Grand Administrator of Dong Commandery (Dongjun) while officials and commoners admired his integrity; there was one who took up office in Fengyi 馮翊 whereupon corrupt subalterns resigned and left, and who memorialized to exchange two Magistrates so that both districts became well-governed; there was one who shut himself in his cabinet to blame himself so that his clerks could not bear to deceive him, and one who promoted and employed elders …

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而郡中歡愛有以三異徵奇有以五袴
詠德者迄今道之猶令人擊節豔慕而
不得與循吏竝傳何歟豈二史之所稱
述專於奉法循理而嚴威非所尚歟當
西漢時僞增蒙賞神爵見褒議者謂宣
帝雖稱綜覈而任法太過其上下竝行
僞貌致然歟又謂建武轉易守長吏治
刻深人皆飾詐以干虛譽然歟否歟我
國家軫切民瘼愼重守宰二百年來比多良
===
牧不知有可比迹兩漢者歟方今
廟廊之上作意撫綏議論科條視昔加密乃
吏道靡然具文罔臻實效何歟說者謂
當議久任度曠格明按部嚴刺舉刬煩
苛覈功實重貪殘之禁玆數者時之所
急也誠欲飭吏治而裨化理果以何者
爲要歟願正言之以覯用世之學
問士君子所以垂世不朽者曰理學政事
節義文章四者恒相須也南畿地靈甲
punctuated:
而郡中歡愛，有以三異徵奇，有以五袴詠德者。迄今道之，猶令人擊節豔慕，而不得與循吏竝傳，何歟？豈二史之所稱述，專於奉法循理，而嚴威非所尚歟？當西漢時，僞增蒙賞，神爵見褒，議者謂宣帝雖稱綜覈，而任法太過，其上下竝行僞貌致然歟？又謂建武轉易守長，吏治刻深，人皆飾詐以干虛譽，然歟否歟？我國家軫切民瘼，愼重守宰，二百年來比多良牧，不知有可比迹兩漢者歟？方今廟廊之上，作意撫綏，議論科條視昔加密，乃吏道靡然，具文罔臻實效，何歟？說者謂當議久任，度曠格，明按部，嚴刺舉，刬煩苛，覈功實，重貪殘之禁，玆數者，時之所急也。誠欲飭吏治而裨化理，果以何者爲要歟？願正言之，以覯用世之學。
問：士君子所以垂世不朽者，曰理學、政事、節義、文章，四者恒相須也。南畿地靈甲
translation_en:
…so that all in the commandery rejoiced and loved him; there was one whose three marvels attested to his extraordinary governance, and one whose virtue was sung of in the ballad of the "five pairs of trousers." Even today, speaking of them still makes people strike the table in admiration and envy, yet they were not included alongside the "Upright Officials" (xunli) in the biographies—why is this? Could it be that what the two histories praised was devoted solely to upholding the law and following reason, whereas stern authority was not what they esteemed? During the Western Han, falsified increases in population received rewards and "divine phoenixes" (shenjue) won praise; critics say that although Emperor Xuan was celebrated for his comprehensive verification of nominal and actual performance, he relied excessively on law—was it that superiors and subordinates alike practiced superficial pretense that brought this about? They also say that during the Jianwu era (25–56), Grand Defenders and District Magistrates were frequently transferred and replaced, official governance became harsh and incisive, and everyone adorned themselves with deceit to seek empty reputations—was this so or not? Our Dynasty shows deep solicitude for the sufferings of the people and exercises great caution in appointing local magistrates and prefects. Over the past two hundred years there have consecutively been many good shepherds of the people; I wonder if there are those whose achievements can be compared to those of the Two Han dynasties? At present, those high in the imperial court are intent upon pacifying and comforting the populace, and deliberations and statutory regulations are more detailed and dense than in the past; yet the way of officialdom has grown lax, and mere formalities fail to achieve actual results—why is this? Commentators say we ought to deliberate on long tenure of office, measure exceptions to standard qualifications, clarify the tours of inspection, make impeachment and recommendation strict, pare away vexatiousness and harshness, verify actual achievements, and weight heavily the prohibitions against greed and cruelty—these several matters are what is urgent for the times. If we truly wish to rectify official governance and aid transformative rule, which of these should indeed be taken as the most essential? I wish you to speak forthrightly of this, so that I may observe your learning for practical statecraft.

Question: That by which scholar-gentlemen hand down an imperishable name to posterity is called the Learning of Principle (lixue), statecraft, moral integrity, and literary composition; these four always depend upon one another. The spiritual vitality of the landscape of the Southern Metropolitan Region (Nanji) ranks first in…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
天下人文炳耀自昔趨之當春秋時才
近伯夷者具宏覽博物之稱名列文學
者著武城絃歌之治固彰彰在人睹記
矣自玆以降代不乏人姑舉一二最著
者與諸士評之有學務躬行集諸儒大
成之統有身任師道繼河汾正脉之傳
其於理學著矣較之號雙湖而著易學
啓蒙翼傳謚文通而述四書辨疑者其
有功于後學孰多有教民立學成蜀君
===
鄒魯之風有才負王佐輔奉天艱難之
業其于政事顯矣較之召對天章而條
上十事勸帝親政而手陳八事者其有
裨于時政孰大有正色以叱從亂六館
之士無受汚者有託疾而辭印綬以事
二姓爲耻者視之太學生伏闕上書而
言極憤切左丞相從君海濵而力竭以
殉其節義之優劣何以殊有學擅明經
著新序而人稱其最爲近古有操筆成
punctuated: 天下，人文炳耀，自昔趨之。當春秋時，才近伯夷者，具宏覽博物之稱；名列文學者，著武城絃歌之治，固彰彰在人睹記矣。自玆以降，代不乏人，姑舉一二最著者，與諸士評之：有學務躬行，集諸儒大成之統；有身任師道，繼河汾正脉之傳，其於理學著矣。較之號雙湖而著《易學啓蒙翼傳》、謚文通而述《四書辨疑》者，其有功于後學孰多？有教民立學，成蜀君鄒魯之風；有才負王佐，輔奉天艱難之業，其于政事顯矣。較之召對天章而條上十事、勸帝親政而手陳八事者，其有裨于時政孰大？有正色以叱從亂，六館之士無受汚者；有託疾而辭印綬，以事二姓爲耻者。視之太學生伏闕上書而言極憤切、左丞相從君海濵而力竭以殉，其節義之優劣何以殊？有學擅明經，著《新序》而人稱其最爲近古；有操筆成
translation_en:
… the realm, and its cultural luminescence has been admired since antiquity. In the Spring and Autumn period, one whose talent approached that of Boyi enjoyed a reputation for broad observation and encyclopedic knowledge [Ji Zha 季札]; and one whose name was ranked under the discipline of "literature and learning" became renowned for his governance by stringed instruments and song at Wucheng [Ziyou 子游]—these are indeed vividly preserved in people's sight and memory. From that time onward, no era has lacked worthy figures; let us cite a few of the most prominent to evaluate with you gentlemen.

There was one whose learning was devoted to personal practice and who synthesized the great achievements of the various Confucians [Zhu Xi 朱熹]; and there was one who personally shouldered the Way of the Teacher and carried on the orthodox lineage of Hefen [Hu Yuan 胡瑗]—these men were illustrious in Principle Learning (lixue). Compared with the one styled Shuanghu who authored the Yixue qimeng yizhuan (Supplementary Commentary on the Introduction to the Study of the Classic of Changes) [Hu Yigui 胡一桂], and the one canonized as Wentong who compiled the Sishu bianyi (Critical Inquiries into the Four Books) [Chen Tianxiang 陳天祥 or Wang Lian 王廉?], which of them rendered greater service to later scholars?

There was one who taught the people and established schools, transforming the customs of Shu [printed 蜀君 for 蜀郡, Shu Commandery] into those of Zou and Lu [Wen Weng 文翁]; and there was one who possessed the talent to assist a true king and aided in the arduous enterprise at Fengtian [Lu Zhi 陸贄]—these men were distinguished in governance. Compared with the one who was summoned for an audience at the Tianzhang Pavilion and submitted a ten-point memorial [Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹], and the one who urged the emperor to assume personal rule and presented eight points written in his own hand [Lou Ji 樓機 or Fan Zuyu 范祖禹?], which of them brought greater benefit to the administration of his time?

There was one who with a stern countenance rebuked those who would follow the rebels, so that none of the scholars of the Six Halls were defiled [He蕃 He Fan]; and there was one who pleaded illness to decline the official seal and sash, regarding service to two ruling houses as shameful [龚勝 Gong Sheng or Tao Qian 陶潛]. Compared with the National University Student who prostrated himself at the palace gates to submit a memorial in the most indignant and earnest terms [Chen Dong 陳東], and the Left Grand Councilor who followed his sovereign to the seashore and exhausted his strength to die a martyr [Lu Xiufu 陸秀夫], how is the superiority or inferiority of their moral integrity to be differentiated?

There was one who excelled in the study of the Classics, authored the Xinxu (New Prefaces) [Liu Xiang 劉向], and was praised as coming closest to antiquity; and there was one who took up the brush to compose…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
賦美詞翰而人稱其文深以思者視之
兄弟齊名而文章丞能冠世爲文瓌麗
而典策多出其手其文章之高下何以
辨夫四者稱名雖異而理本合一不知
其在諸賢果能兼乎否耶我
昭代氣隆化洽培養薰蒸之澤涵濡厚矣應
運開
國諸臣姑置無論其間名卿碩儒後先輝映
搢紳長老歷歷道之諸士生于其鄉景
===
慕先哲久矣可槩指其人與所謂理學
政事節義文章具載名臣錄者可稽也
庶幾與前代諸賢有相合歟夫考古以
準今論人以律已兹所願學者何在歟
其究言之以觀尚友之志
問策士起於漢其時用對策顯者更僕未
易數而鼂董公孫爲稱首今綜三子觀
之錯他所論建利害甚悉及對策則謂
五帝神聖其臣莫及又稱文帝大功數
punctuated:
賦、美詞翰，而人稱其「文深以思」者；視之兄弟齊名而文章丞能冠世，爲文瓌麗而典策多出其手，其文章之高下何以辨？夫四者稱名雖異，而理本合一，不知其在諸賢果能兼乎否耶？我昭代氣隆化洽，培養薰蒸之澤，涵濡厚矣。應運開國諸臣姑置無論，其間名卿碩儒，後先輝映，搢紳長老歷歷道之。諸士生于其鄉，景慕先哲久矣，可槩指其人與？所謂理學、政事、節義、文章，具載《名臣錄》者可稽也，庶幾與前代諸賢有相合歟？夫考古以準今，論人以律已，兹所願學者何在歟？其究言之，以觀尚友之志。

問：策士起於漢，其時用對策顯者，更僕未易數，而鼂、董、公孫爲稱首。今綜三子觀之：錯他所論建，利害甚悉，及對策，則謂五帝神聖其臣莫及，又稱文帝大功數
translation_en:
…rhapsodies and excelled in lyric and epistolary composition, so that people praised his writing as "profound and reflective." Compared with those brothers who enjoyed equal fame and whose literary writings both [丞, error for 並?] crowned the age, or the one whose prose was magnificent and from whose hand most court charters and edicts came—how is the relative superiority of their literary achievement to be distinguished? Now, although these four categories—Neo-Confucian learning, statecraft, moral integrity, and literary achievement—differ in name, their underlying principle is fundamentally one. Did those worthies in fact manage to combine them all, or not? In our illustrious dynasty, the vital spirit is flourishing and transformative teaching is pervasive; the grace that nurtures and imbues us has soaked in deeply. Leaving aside without discussion the ministers who responded to Heaven's turn of fortune in founding the dynasty, among the renowned high officials and great Confucian scholars since then, one after another has shone in mutual splendor, and the gentry and elders recount their deeds in vivid detail. Having been born in this region, you gentlemen have long admired the former sages; can you point out in general who those men were? What are called Neo-Confucian learning, statecraft, moral integrity, and literary achievement are all fully recorded in the Records of Eminent Ministers (Mingchen lu), where they can be examined; do they perhaps correspond to those worthies of former dynasties? Now, one investigates antiquity in order to measure the present, and evaluates others in order to discipline oneself: wherein lies that which you now wish to emulate? Discuss this thoroughly, so that we may observe your aspiration to befriend the ancients.

Question: Examining scholars by policy questions originated in the Han dynasty. At that time, those who rose to prominence through their policy responses were too numerous to count even if one changed attendants, yet Chao Cuo 鼂錯, Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒, and Gongsun Hong 公孫弘 are acclaimed as the foremost. Let us now consider the three men together: in his other memorials and proposals, Chao Cuo analyzed advantages and disadvantages in great detail; yet when he answered the palace policy question, he declared that the Five Emperors were so divinely sage that their ministers could not match them, and he further praised Emperor Wen for having several…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
十豈應直言極諫者當爾耶弘策不無
可采至認智爲術以湯旱爲桀餘烈其
旨不有戾耶仲舒三策粹然一出于正
乃武帝猶病其條貫靡竟統紀未終何
也夫三子以彼其才尚猶若是甚矣其
難也我
國家每賓興士終試則策之固漢法已諸士
即有鼂董公孫其人慮不免遺論脫猶
未也賓興之謂何今即不暇與諸士緩
===
頰姑舉二三特事商之教化有國之大
務也乃士風民俗尚多浮僞何以挽之
宗藩本支所宜厚也乃賦稅
邸祿竝苦不給何以足之經費非寡也安所
裕大農之匱書缺有間矣安所充
秘府之藏章程所據者
會典也顧久未刊定罔所折衷豈畫一之法
乎刑獄所準者
大明律也顧意或未晰例日增繁豈慎罰之旨
punctuated: 十，豈應直言極諫者當爾耶？弘策不無可采，至認智爲術，以湯旱爲桀餘烈，其旨不有戾耶？仲舒三策粹然一出于正，乃武帝猶病其條貫靡竟，統紀未終，何也？夫三子以彼其才，尚猶若是，甚矣其難也！我國家每賓興士，終試則策之，固漢法已。諸士即有鼂、董、公孫其人，慮不免遺論；脫猶未也，賓興之謂何？今即不暇與諸士緩頰，姑舉二三特事商之：教化，有國之大務也，乃士風民俗尚多浮僞，何以挽之？宗藩，本支所宜厚也，乃賦稅、邸祿竝苦不給，何以足之？經費非寡也，安所裕大農之匱？書缺有間矣，安所充秘府之藏？章程所據者《會典》也，顧久未刊定，罔所折衷，豈畫一之法乎？刑獄所準者《大明律》也，顧意或未晰，例日增繁，豈慎罰之旨…
translation_en: …ten in number—could one responding to a call for frank speech and utmost remonstrance properly speak thus? In Gongsun Hong's 公孫弘 policy response there is not without merit to be adopted, yet when it comes to mistaking wisdom for statecraft manipulation, and attributing the drought in King Tang's 湯 time to the lingering ferocity of King Jie 桀, does not its purport go awry? Dong Zhongshu's 董仲舒 three policy responses are pure and issue wholly from orthodoxy, yet Emperor Wu 武帝 still faulted them for their threads not being fully carried through and their overarching system not being brought to completion—why was this? Now, with talents such as those three masters possessed, they still fared like this; extreme indeed is the difficulty of the task! Whenever our State ceremoniously elevates scholars for the examinations, in the final session it tests them with policy questions, which is assuredly the Han method. Even if among you scholars there are men the likes of Chao Cuo 鼂錯, Dong Zhongshu, and Gongsun Hong, I fear you would not escape lingering criticism; and if you do not even reach their level, what is the meaning of ceremoniously elevating you? Right now I have no leisure to engage in unhurried discourse with you scholars, so let me provisionally raise two or three specific matters to deliberate upon: Moral transformation through education is the great business of holding a state, yet the ethos of scholars and the customs of the common people still have much superficiality and falseness—how is this to be reversed? The imperial clansmen and princely fiefs are the trunk and branches that ought to be generously treated, yet tax revenues and princely stipends both suffer from insufficiency—how are they to be made adequate? Regular state expenditures are not small; how are we to relieve the depletion of the Grand Minister of Agriculture (i.e., the Ministry of Revenue)? Books have been missing for some time now; how are we to replenish the holdings of the Imperial Library? What administrative regulations rely upon is the Collected Statutes (Huidian 會典), yet for a long time it has not been collated, finalized, and printed, leaving no standard for adjudication—is this a uniform law? What criminal cases and litigation take as their standard is the Great Ming Code (Da Ming lü 大明律), yet its intent is sometimes not clear and supplementary sub-statutes grow daily more numerous and complex—is this the purport of caution in punishment…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
乎自振武悍卒未盡伏辜故脫巾大譟
者往往而起軍政何以肅之今九邊營
田稍閒加墾而內地積壞者比比如故
屯政何以修之史以公萬世之是非而
起居注失其職樂以與一代之制作而
律呂逸其傳方漕河未治海運行之有
效矣玆何以復報罷歟往虜衆跳梁熟
夷恃以黠横矣玆何故猶未戢歟使鼂
董公孫而在計必憂之而具以成畫進
也爾諸士生
明聖之世意所藴結豈遽不若三子其悉吐胸
中之奇著于篇主司將徵其言以需
大對焉
punctuated: 乎？自振武悍卒未盡伏辜，故脫巾大譟者往往而起，軍政何以肅之？今九邊營田稍閒加墾，而內地積壞者比比如故，屯政何以修之？史以公萬世之是非，而起居注失其職；樂以與一代之制作，而律呂逸其傳。方漕河未治，海運行之有效矣，玆何以復報罷歟？往虜衆跳梁，熟夷恃以黠横矣，玆何故猶未戢歟？使鼂、董、公孫而在，計必憂之，而具以成畫進也。爾諸士生明聖之世，意所藴結，豈遽不若三子？其悉吐胸中之奇，著于篇，主司將徵其言以需大對焉。
translation_en: …? Since the unruly soldiers of the Zhenwu Guard did not all suffer punishment for their crimes, those who cast off their headbands and raise a great uproar frequently arise; how can military administration be made strict? Now the military farm-colonies along the Nine Borders have slightly more leisure to expand cultivation, yet those in the interior that have long been ruined remain everywhere just as before; how can the administration of military state farms be restored? History is meant to make impartial the judgments of right and wrong for ten thousand generations, yet the Court Diarists have lost their function; music is meant to participate in the institutional creations of an era, yet the transmission of the pitch-pipes and temperament has been lost. When the Grand Canal was not yet in order, sea transport was practiced with good effect; why has it now again been declared discontinued? In the past, when the northern caitiff hordes were unruly and defiant, the "cooked" (assimilated) barbarians relied on them to be crafty and lawless; for what reason have they now still not been restrained? If Chao Cuo 鼂錯, Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒, and Gongsun Hong 公孫弘 were alive today, we reckon they would certainly be concerned about these matters and present fully formed plans in response. You scholars live in an enlightened and sagely age; in what you have stored up in your thoughts, how could you readily be inferior to those three gentlemen?Pour forth all the extraordinary insights in your breasts and set them down in your essays; the Examiners will test your words in anticipation of your Grand Replies at the Palace Examination.

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子張問政子曰居之無倦行之以忠
方應選
同考試官教授區　批〔作此題者類襲靡語〕
〔是篇刊浮崇雅最得文體之正宜式多士〕
同考試官推官諸　批〔命意渾融措詞精鍊〕
〔純心立政之義發揮殆盡宜錄以式〕
同考試官推官龍　批〔體格正大詞理渾融〕
===
考試官右中允何　批〔平正透徹〕
考試官左中允范　批〔醇正莊雅〕
聖人與賢者論政在存之有常而出之有本也
夫政合始終內外而一之者也存之有常而出
之有本於爲政乎何有且夫久道足以宜民而
誠心斯可出治子張問政蓋志非不銳於初而
意在得行於外者夫子因告之曰政也者心之
著也以心勤民而居之一或有間是倦也倦勤
一起而欲民生之永頼得乎必思斯世斯民無
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「子張問政。子曰：『居之無倦，行之以忠。』」

方應選

同考試官教授區　批〔作此題者，類襲靡語。是篇刊浮崇雅，最得文體之正，宜式多士。〕
同考試官推官諸　批〔命意渾融，措詞精鍊。純心立政之義，發揮殆盡，宜錄以式。〕
同考試官推官龍　批〔體格正大，詞理渾融。〕
考試官右中允何　批〔平正透徹。〕
考試官左中允范　批〔醇正莊雅。〕

聖人與賢者論政，在存之有常而出之有本也。夫政，合始終、內外而一之者也。存之有常而出之有本，於爲政乎何有？且夫久道足以宜民，而誠心斯可出治。子張問政，蓋志非不銳於初，而意在得行於外者。夫子因告之曰：政也者，心之著也。以心勤民而居之，一或有間，是倦也。倦勤一起，而欲民生之永頼，得乎？必思斯世斯民，無
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

"Zizhang asked about governance. The Master said, 'Abide in it without tire; carry it out with loyalty.'" (Analects 12.14)

Fang Yingxuan 方應選

Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoshou) Ou 區, comments: [Those who write on this topic generally repeat florid clichés. This essay pares away superficiality and honors elegance, best attaining correctness of literary form; it ought to serve as a model for the many scholars.]
Associate Examiner, Prefectural Judge (tuiguan) Zhu 諸, comments: [The conception is well-integrated and harmonious, and the phrasing is refined and polished. The meaning of establishing governance with a pure heart is expounded almost to the fullest; it should be recorded as a model.]
Associate Examiner, Prefectural Judge (tuiguan) Long 龍, comments: [Its structure is upright and grand; its diction and reasoning are harmonious and unified.]
Examiner, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent (you zhongyun) He 何, comments: [Balanced, upright, and thoroughly penetrating.]
Examiner, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent (zuo zhongyun) Fan 范, comments: [Pure, orthodox, dignified, and elegant.]

When the Sage discussed governance with a worthy, the point lay in preserving it with constancy and issuing it from a fundamental root. Now governance is that which unites beginning and end, inner and outer, into one. If one preserves it with constancy and issues it from a fundamental root, what difficulty is there in governing? Moreover, an enduring Way suffices to suit the people, and a sincere heart is what allows one to bring forth good order. When Zizhang asked about governance, his ambition was by no means lacking in sharpness at the outset, yet his attention was fixed on achieving results in external action. The Master therefore told him: Governance is the manifestation of the mind. When one abides in it by laboring for the people with one's mind, if there is the slightest interruption, that is weariness. Once weariness in diligence arises, how can one hope that the people's livelihood will have something to rely upon forever? One must reflect that in this world and for these people, there is not…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
一日不待治於我而始之終之無一日不加志
于民凡其悅安之慮强教之懷居之蒞政之初
卽爲久安長治之計而吾之柔肩一心者與至
治相爲無窮斯已焉否則一息少懈卽美意漸
荒此其所關于治體何如者而可或倦耶心也
者政之本也言舉斯心而行之一或未盡非忠
也忠非前定而欲實惠之及民得乎必其章程
所布本吾懇切爲民之實心禁令所須根諸勤
恤民隱之至意雖其惻怛之愛忠利之教行之
===
黎庶之上不無紀綱法度之施而吾之式敷民
德者與吾心相爲流貫斯已焉否則一念弗誠
卽良法徒具此其所係于治功何如者而可弗
忠耶夫恒以居之則終始一而行益純忠以行
之則內外孚而居益永爲政之道曷以尚茲抑
斯道也不越乎誠而已誠則不雜不雜則久而
徵爲博厚高明悠遠之治所謂王道本于誠意
者此也夫子蘊帝王之略而不得試故因子張
之問以發之蓋一言而內聖外王之道備矣豈
punctuated: 一日不待治於我，而始之終之，無一日不加志于民。凡其悅安之慮、强教之懷，居之蒞政之初，卽爲久安長治之計，而吾之柔肩一心者，與至治相爲無窮，斯已焉。否則一息少懈，卽美意漸荒，此其所關于治體何如者，而可或倦耶？心也者，政之本也。言舉斯心而行之，一或未盡，非忠也。忠非前定，而欲實惠之及民，得乎？必其章程所布，本吾懇切爲民之實心；禁令所須，根諸勤恤民隱之至意。雖其惻怛之愛、忠利之教，行之黎庶之上，不無紀綱法度之施，而吾之式敷民德者，與吾心相爲流貫，斯已焉。否則一念弗誠，卽良法徒具，此其所係于治功何如者，而可弗忠耶？夫恒以居之，則終始一而行益純；忠以行之，則內外孚而居益永。爲政之道，曷以尚茲？抑斯道也，不越乎誠而已。誠則不雜，不雜則久，而徵爲博厚、高明、悠遠之治，所謂王道本于誠意者此也。夫子蘊帝王之略而不得試，故因子張之問以發之。蓋一言而內聖外王之道備矣，豈
translation_en: …a single day without depending on me for governance, and from beginning to end, there must not be a single day when I do not set my mind upon the people. In all one's thoughts of bringing them joy and peace, and one's intentions of tirelessly instructing them, when holding them in mind at the very outset of assuming administration, one immediately plans for lasting peace and enduring order; only when my single-minded devotion in bearing this burden [?] continues endlessly alongside supreme governance is it enough. Otherwise, if one relaxes even for a single breath, good intentions will gradually go to waste. How great is the bearing of this upon the substance of governance—and could one ever be weary? The mind is the root of governance. When one speaks of taking up this mind and putting it into practice, if in any single respect it is not fully exhausted, that is not loyalty (zhong). If loyalty is not determined beforehand, and yet one wishes for real benefits to reach the people, how could that be achieved? The regulations promulgated must be rooted in my earnest, sincere mind for the people; the prohibitions required must be grounded in the utmost intention of diligently sympathizing with the people's hidden sufferings. Although when one's commiserating love and one's teachings of loyalty and benefit are practiced over the common multitude, there is inevitably the application of overarching principles and legal measures, only when my spreading of civic virtue flows in mutual continuity with my own mind is it enough. Otherwise, if a single thought is insincere, then good laws exist merely in form. How great is the connection of this to the achievements of governance—and could one fail to be loyal? Now, if one abides in it with constancy, then beginning and end are one, and one's practice becomes ever purer; if one practices it with loyalty, then inner and outer are in accord, and one's abiding in it becomes ever more enduring. In the Way of governing, what could surpass this? Yet this Way goes no further than sincerity (cheng). When there is sincerity, there is no admixture; when there is no admixture, it is long-lasting, and it manifests as governance that is broad and thick, high and bright, and far-reaching and enduring. This is what is meant by the Kingly Way being rooted in making the intentions sincere. The Master harbored the grand strategies of emperors and kings but could not put them to the test; therefore, he took the occasion of Zizhang's question to set them forth. Indeed, in a single statement the Way of inner sageliness and outer kingliness is complete. Could it…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
非爲萬世開太平者哉
修身則道立尊賢則不惑
江文明
同考試官學正黃　批〔發清新於平淡之中藏古雅於追琢之外而道立不惑處宛然在目〕
〔殆非時調所能到者敬服敬服〕
同考試官教授孫　批〔精明古雅中庸義之〕
〔絕佳者錄之以範多士〕
考試官右中允何　批〔有發揮有關係錄之〕
考試官左中允范　批〔明整可錄〕
===
中庸首舉九經之效建皇極而成明后也夫皇
極建而居上明斯可爲政于天下矣然非修身
尊賢曷致是哉夫子以王道望魯君而期之以
此若謂治有常經政有先務顧人君之力行何
如爾彼君身出政之本修之固以道矣而道本
諸身所以立人之極者也身果能修焉則懋德
建中而物軌所彰樹儀刑於下國體元居正而
道揆所著植表正於斯民協和丕式之治定自此
punctuated:
非爲萬世開太平者哉！

修身則道立，尊賢則不惑。
江文明
同考試官學正黃　批：〔發清新於平淡之中，藏古雅於追琢之外，而道立不惑處宛然在目，〕〔殆非時調所能到者。敬服，敬服！〕
同考試官教授孫　批：〔精明古雅，《中庸》義之〕〔絕佳者，錄之以範多士。〕
考試官右中允何　批：〔有發揮，有關係，錄之。〕
考試官左中允范　批：〔明整可錄。〕

《中庸》首舉九經之效，建皇極而成明后也。夫皇極建而居上明，斯可爲政于天下矣；然非修身、尊賢，曷致是哉？夫子以王道望魯君，而期之以此，若謂：治有常經，政有先務，顧人君之力行何如爾。彼君身，出政之本，修之固以道矣；而道本諸身，所以立人之極者也。身果能修焉，則懋德建中，而物軌所彰，樹儀刑於下國；體元居正，而道揆所著，植表正於斯民。協和丕式之治，定自此
translation_en:
… not initiating great peace for ten thousand generations!

"By cultivating one's person, the Way is established; by honoring the worthy, one is free from perplexity."
Jiang Wenming

Associate Examiner Director of Studies Huang comments: [It brings forth freshness and novelty from within plainness, and conceals antique elegance beyond polished carving, while the points on the Way being established and being free from perplexity are vividly before the eyes—] [this is scarcely something that contemporary styles can attain. Truly admirable, truly admirable!]
Associate Examiner Instructor Sun comments: [Clear-sighted and of antique elegance, this is an] [utterly superb exposition on the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong); record it to serve as a model for the many scholars.]
Examiner Right Companion to the Heir Apparent He comments: [It has elaboration and relevance; record it.]
Examiner Left Companion to the Heir Apparent Fan comments: [Clear and well-ordered; worthy of being recorded.]

The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) first cites the efficacy of the Nine Standard Rules in establishing the August Ultimate and bringing to completion an enlightened ruler. Now, when the August Ultimate is established and the one who occupies the supreme position is enlightened, then one can govern the empire; yet without cultivating one's person and honoring the worthy, how could this be achieved? The Master looked to the ruler of Lu with hopes for the Kingly Way, and set this expectation for him, as if to say: Governance has constant standards and administration has primary tasks; all depends on how strenuously the ruler puts them into practice. That person of the ruler is the root from which administration issues, and cultivating it is assuredly done through the Way; and the Way, being rooted in his person, is that whereby the standard for humankind is established. If his person can truly be cultivated, then by exertively cultivating virtue and establishing centrality, where the norms for things are manifested, he sets up a model of conduct for the states below; by embodying the primal good and dwelling in rectitude, where the measure of the Way is displayed, he plants a standard of rectitude for these people. A governance of harmonious concord and grand model will certainly from this…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
豫其基也平章惇睦之化胥此端其準也蓋始
焉以道而自修旣焉以身而範物立于此形于
彼所謂近取諸身其則不遠者是已修身之效
蓋如此賢人爲政之輔尊之固有等矣而后賢
相得所以資君之明者也賢果能尊焉則衆賢
和朝而密勿之論思昭晰乎經綸之藴庶明勵
翼而廟堂之風議闡悉乎道化之微近而齊治
之理相與講明之不蔽也遠而均平之道相與
攷究之不疑也蓋人君好善以忘勢則賢人論
===
道以經邦啓乃心沃乃心所謂聰明睿智足以
有臨者是已尊賢之效蓋如此吁修身要矣尊
賢急焉君子修此二者而推類以盡其餘於爲
政乎何有雖然非有二也修身者修其所以取
人之則而賢人之所與共明者卽此道也緝熙
敬勝其克知灼見之本乎容德義德非丕顯執
兢之助乎此固文武致治之規帝王相傳之要
而夫子蓋以東周望魯矣人君率而行之周道
其有興乎
punctuated: 豫其基也；平章惇睦之化，胥此端其準也。蓋始焉以道而自修，旣焉以身而範物。立于此，形于彼，所謂「近取諸身，其則不遠」者，是已。修身之效，蓋如此。賢人，爲政之輔，尊之固有等矣；而后賢相得，所以資君之明者也。賢果能尊焉，則衆賢和朝，而密勿之論思，昭晰乎經綸之藴；庶明勵翼，而廟堂之風議，闡悉乎道化之微。近而齊治之理，相與講明之，不蔽也；遠而均平之道，相與攷究之，不疑也。蓋人君好善以忘勢，則賢人論道以經邦，啓乃心，沃乃心，所謂「聰明睿智，足以有臨」者，是已。尊賢之效，蓋如此。吁！修身要矣，尊賢急焉，君子修此二者，而推類以盡其餘，於爲政乎何有！雖然，非有二也。修身者，修其所以取人之則；而賢人之所與共明者，卽此道也。緝熙敬勝，其克知灼見之本乎？容德義德，非丕顯執兢之助乎？此固文武致治之規，帝王相傳之要，而夫子蓋以東周望魯矣。人君率而行之，周道其有興乎！
translation_en:
…lays its foundation in advance; and the transformation of harmonizing and fostering amity entirely establishes its standard here. For at first one cultivates oneself through the Way, and afterward one serves as a model for all things through one's own person. Established here, it manifests there; this is indeed what is meant by "taking the model from oneself nearby, the rule is not far off." The efficacy of cultivating the person is such as this.

Worthy men are the assistants in governance, and honoring them certainly has its gradations; yet the mutual accord of the sovereign and the worthy is that whereby the ruler's clarity of vision is aided. If the worthy can truly be honored, then a multitude of worthies will harmonize at court, and their earnest deliberations and reflections will clearly illuminate the depths of statecraft; the many enlightened ones will strive to assist, and the spirited discussions in the ancestral temple and court will fully elucidate the subtleties of moral transformation. Near at hand, the principles of regulating the family and governing the state are expounded and clarified together with them, so that there is no obscuration; far afield, the Way of bringing equilibrium and peace to the world is investigated and examined together with them, so that there is no doubt. For when a ruler loves goodness and forgets his own positional power, worthy men discourse on the Way to order the state, "opening his heart and enriching his heart"; this is indeed what is meant by "being quick in apprehension, clear in discernment, of far-reaching intelligence and all-embracing knowledge, sufficient to exercise rule." The efficacy of honoring the worthy is such as this.

Ah! Cultivating the person is essential, and honoring the worthy is urgent. When the noble man cultivates these two and extends the principle to exhaust all the rest, what difficulty is there in governing? Even so, they are not two separate things. He who cultivates his person cultivates the standard by which he selects men; and that which worthy men join with him in illuminating is none other than this very Way. Are not continuous illumination and reverent self-mastery the root of being able to know and clearly perceive? Are not the virtues of forbearance and righteousness the aid to grandly illustrious and cautious diligence? This is truly the model by which Kings Wen and Wu achieved good order, and the essential principle transmitted from one sovereign to another; and the Master was indeed hoping to make Lu into an Eastern Zhou. If a ruler follows and practices this, will not the Way of Zhou revive?

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
君仁莫不仁君義莫不義君正莫不正一
正君而國定矣
汪䧺立
同考試官教諭丘　批〔命意精深構詞剴切〕
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔場中多駢浮冗獨此〕
〔作詞意詳盡宜錄以式〕
同考試官教授黃　批〔正君定國處發揮明〕
〔切錄之〕
同考試官知縣帥　批〔提掇峻偉氣象莊嚴〕
===
考試官右中允何　批〔明白痛快〕
考試官左中允范　批〔簡當〕
觀大臣格君之極功而臣道無餘藴矣夫君心
萬化之原也大人格之以仁義而一于正焉國
其有不定乎孟子以此立臣極也若曰所謂大
臣者以一身係一國之安危者也人政之失不
足計而格心之功何如哉彼上臣之所以望君
者爲其仁足以容義足以執中正爲觀而以一
人定國焉爾今惟格其不仁之非以歸之仁則
punctuated:
「君仁莫不仁，君義莫不義，君正莫不正。一正君，而國定矣。」

汪䧺立

同考試官教諭丘　批：〔命意精深，構詞剴切。〕
同考試官教諭蔣　批：〔場中多駢浮冗，獨此作詞意詳盡，宜錄以式。〕

觀大臣格君之極功，而臣道無餘藴矣。夫君心，萬化之原也；大人格之以仁義，而一于正焉，國其有不定乎？孟子以此立臣極也。若曰：所謂大臣者，以一身係一國之安危者也。人政之失不足計，而格心之功何如哉？彼上臣之所以望君者，爲其仁足以容，義足以執，中正爲觀，而以一人定國焉爾。今惟格其不仁之非以歸之仁，則
translation_en:
"If the ruler is benevolent, no one will fail to be benevolent; if the ruler is righteous, no one will fail to be righteous; if the ruler is upright, no one will fail to be upright. Once the ruler is rectified, the state will be settled."

Wang Xiongli 汪䧺立

Associate Examiner Instructor Qiu 丘 comments: "Its central conception is profound, and its phrasing is incisive and apt."
Associate Examiner Instructor Jiang 蔣 comments: "In the examination hall there was much flowery, superficial, and verbose writing; this piece alone is thorough in both diction and meaning, and ought to be recorded as a model."
Associate Examiner Professor Huang 黃 comments: "Where it expounds on rectifying the ruler and settling the state, the elaboration is clear and to the point. Record it."
Associate Examiner District Magistrate Shuai 帥 comments: "Its presentation is lofty and magnificent, its bearing solemn and majestic."
Examiner Right Companion of the Heir Apparent He 何 comments: "Clear and forthright."
Examiner Left Companion of the Heir Apparent Fan 范 comments: "Concise and fitting."

When one observes the ultimate achievement of a great minister in rectifying his ruler, the Way of the minister holds no further mystery. Now, the ruler's mind is the source of the ten thousand transformations; when a great man rectifies it with benevolence and righteousness so that it becomes unified in uprightness, how could the state fail to be settled? By this, Mencius established the ultimate standard for ministers. It is as if he said: What is called a great minister is one upon whose single person hangs the safety or peril of an entire state. Faults in personnel and governance are not worth reckoning—what then is the achievement of rectifying the ruler's mind? That which a supreme minister hopes for in his ruler is simply that his benevolence suffices to encompass all, his righteousness suffices to hold fast, his impartial uprightness serves as a model to behold, and through a single man he settles the state. Now, if only one rectifies the wrongs of his lack of benevolence so as to return him to benevolence, then…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
君心一廣居也而非仁無爲矣格其不義之非
以歸之義則君心一大道也而非義弗由矣居
仁由義而弗納于邪則君心一正位也而非正
弗履矣夫非心一格而以莫不正信乎君心所
係之大也故大人者事君無多術而純心其所
急焉一純其心則所用皆正人賢才輔而天下
治所以繫國祚于苞桑者此也而格心之益何
其大哉致主非泛圖而端本其最切焉一端其
本則所行皆善政庶政和而萬國寧所以奠邦
===
家于磐石者此也而正君之功豈其微哉吁此
其所以爲大臣也抑斯道也惟伊周足以當之
蓋其元聖之資明光之德所謂正己物正之大
人也故其師保棐迪不必規規於告語而允德
篤叙君心有默化焉所以定商周不拔之基而
臣主同光於萬世者孰非自精神心術中來耶
後世欲建伊周光輔之烈者當求諸伊周純一
之心
易
punctuated:
君心一廣居也，而非仁無爲矣；格其不義之非以歸之義，則君心一大道也，而非義弗由矣。居仁由義而弗納于邪，則君心一正位也，而非正弗履矣。夫非心一格而以莫不正，信乎君心所係之大也！故大人者，事君無多術，而純心其所急焉。一純其心，則所用皆正人，賢才輔而天下治，所以繫國祚于苞桑者此也，而格心之益何其大哉！致主非泛圖，而端本其最切焉。一端其本，則所行皆善政，庶政和而萬國寧，所以奠邦家于磐石者此也，而正君之功豈其微哉！吁，此其所以爲大臣也！抑斯道也，惟伊、周足以當之。蓋其元聖之資，明光之德，所謂正己物正之大人也。故其師保棐迪，不必規規於告語，而允德篤叙，君心有默化焉。所以定商、周不拔之基，而臣主同光於萬世者，孰非自精神心術中來耶？後世欲建伊、周光輔之烈者，當求諸伊、周純一之心。

易
translation_en:
… the ruler's mind becomes wholly the wide house, and nothing is done that is not benevolent; when he rectifies the wrong of his unrighteousness to return it to righteousness, then the ruler's mind becomes wholly the great path, and nothing is followed that is not righteous. Dwelling in benevolence and following righteousness without leading him into depravity, the ruler's mind becomes wholly the correct position, and nothing is trodden that is not correct. Indeed, once the wrong in his mind is rectified, there is nothing that is not correct—truly great is that which hinges upon the ruler's mind! Therefore, for the great man, serving the ruler does not involve numerous techniques; purifying the mind is his urgent priority. Once he purifies his mind, all whom he employs will be upright men; worthy talents will assist and the world will be well-governed. This is whereby the dynastic fortune is bound to clustered mulberry roots—how great is the benefit of rectifying the mind! Devoting oneself to the ruler is not a matter of vague schemes; rectifying the root is what is most crucial. Once he rectifies the root, all that he carries out will be good governance; the various affairs of state will be harmonious and the myriad states at peace. This is whereby the state and family are established upon a bedrock—how could the achievement of rectifying the ruler be slight! Ah, this is what makes him a great minister! Yet as for this Way, only Yi Yin 伊尹 and the Duke of Zhou 周公 were sufficient to be worthy of it. For with their endowments as paramount sages and their bright, illustrious virtue, they were what are called great men who rectify themselves and thereby rectify others. Therefore, in acting as tutors and protectors to assist and guide, they did not need to busy themselves with petty admonitions, yet through sincere virtue and earnest ordering, the ruler's mind was silently transformed. Whereby they established the unshakable foundations of Shang and Zhou, so that minister and sovereign shared glory for ten thousand generations—how could any of this not have come from their spiritual energy and the art of the mind? Those in later ages who wish to establish the illustrious assisting achievements of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou ought to seek them in the pure and unified minds of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou.

Book of Changes (Yi 易)

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
直其正也方其義也君子敬以直內義以
方外
方應選
同考試官教授區　批〔命詞古雅用意周匝〕
同考試官推官諸　批〔通篇整潔純粹而講〕
敬義之功更是精透足占所養矣
同考試官推官龍　批〔認題精確措詞整齊〕

===
文言釋直方之義而表君子學以成之焉夫直
之爲正方之爲義皆心之德也非君子制心制
事之學何以成之哉坤六二之文言意謂天下
皆有秉彝之德君子能懋成德之功六二之動
直以方矣所謂直方者何蓋直者言乎人心本
體之正也五性未鑿而內邪之不起七情未流
而外邪之不撓無偏陂則無委曲也直非正而
何方者言乎人心裁制之義也百爲異勢而裁
成之有法萬化殊時而宰制之有方有矩度則
punctuated:
「直其正也，方其義也。君子敬以直內，義以方外。」

方應選

文言釋直方之義，而表君子學以成之焉。夫直之爲正，方之爲義，皆心之德也；非君子制心制事之學，何以成之哉？坤六二之《文言》，意謂：天下皆有秉彝之德，君子能懋成德之功。六二之動，直以方矣。所謂直方者何？蓋直者，言乎人心本體之正也。五性未鑿而內邪之不起，七情未流而外邪之不撓；無偏陂則無委曲也，直非正而何？方者，言乎人心裁制之義也。百爲異勢而裁成之有法，萬化殊時而宰制之有方；有矩度則
translation_en:
"Straightness means its correctness; squareness means its righteousness. The superior man uses reverence to straighten the interior, and righteousness to square the exterior."

Fang Yingxuan 方應選

Associate Examiner, Instructor Ou 區, comments: 〔The phrasing is classical and elegant, and the thought is thorough and comprehensive.〕
Associate Examiner, Prefectural Judge Zhu 諸, comments: 〔The entire piece is neat and pure, and in explaining〕 the effort of reverence and righteousness, it is even more incisive and penetrating, which is sufficient to gauge his self-cultivation.
Associate Examiner, Prefectural Judge Long 龍, comments: 〔His grasp of the theme is precise, and his wording is well-ordered.〕
Examiner, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent He 何, comments: 〔Captures the essential meaning.〕
Examiner, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent Fan 范, comments: 〔Balanced and sound.〕

The Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan 文言) explains the meaning of straightness and squareness, and highlights how the superior man brings them to completion through learning. Now, that straightness is correctness and squareness is righteousness—both are virtues of the mind; without the superior man's learning in regulating the mind and regulating affairs, how could they be brought to completion? The Commentary on the Words of the Text for the Second Six line of the Kun 坤 hexagram means to say: All under heaven possess the virtue of an innate moral nature, yet it is the superior man who can exert himself in the work of perfecting virtue. The movement of the Second Six line is straight and thereby square. What is meant by "straight and square"? Straightness refers to the correctness of the original substance of the human mind. When the five natures have not yet been artificially chiseled, internal perversity does not arise; when the seven emotions have not yet flowed into excess, external perversity does not disturb it. Being without partiality or bias, there is no crookedness; if straightness is not correctness, what is it? Squareness refers to the righteousness of the human mind's regulative judgment. When the hundred actions differ in circumstance, there is a method for tailoring and completing them; when the myriad transformations vary in time, there is a principle for governing and regulating them. Having a carpenter's square and measure, there is…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
無圓融也方非義而何此至德也人皆有之人
自失之耳君子則以內之不可不直也是德之
榦也而直之以敬焉儼神明之臨而在室無屋
漏之愧勑時幾之戒而在輿有倚衡之瞻必使
敬常勝怠無回互隱伏之私而歸于正直斯已
也敬以直內而所以利外者不已豫哉又以外
之不可不方也是德之制也而方之以義焉動
與矩合而不縱情于燕僻之私事與道謀而不
溺志於詭常之失必使義常勝欲有均齊方正
===
之美而蹈乎大方斯已也義以方外而所以資
內者不益深哉吁學而至是則直可中繩久之
將不繩而直也方可中矩久之將不矩而方也
不孤之大不從此出乎抑論乾道尚舒兼言仁
禮坤道尚縮獨稱義正蓋君子檢身惟患不嚴
嚴矣猶恐以弛繼之而況敢自爲寬耶故敬義
二言丹書之教誡周公之家範也然二者敬尤
其本孔子告仲弓出門如見大賓使民如承大
祭說者以爲坤道信矣
punctuated: 無圓融也，方非義而何？此至德也，人皆有之，人自失之耳。君子則以內之不可不直也，是德之榦也，而直之以敬焉。儼神明之臨，而在室無屋漏之愧；勑時幾之戒，而在輿有倚衡之瞻。必使敬常勝怠，無回互隱伏之私，而歸于正直斯已也。敬以直內，而所以利外者不已豫哉！又以外之不可不方也，是德之制也，而方之以義焉。動與矩合，而不縱情于燕僻之私；事與道謀，而不溺志於詭常之失。必使義常勝欲，有均齊方正之美，而蹈乎大方斯已也。義以方外，而所以資內者不益深哉！吁！學而至是，則直可中繩，久之將不繩而直也；方可中矩，久之將不矩而方也。不孤之大，不從此出乎？抑論乾道尚舒，兼言仁禮；坤道尚縮，獨稱義正。蓋君子檢身，惟患不嚴；嚴矣，猶恐以弛繼之，而況敢自爲寬耶？故敬、義二言，《丹書》之教誡，周公之家範也。然二者，敬尤其本。孔子告仲弓「出門如見大賓，使民如承大祭」，說者以爲坤道，信矣。
translation_en:
…there is no slick evasiveness. If squareness is not righteousness, then what is it? This is the supreme virtue; all people possess it, yet people lose it of their own accord.

The superior man, however, recognizes that the interior must not fail to be straight—for this is the trunk of virtue—and so he straightens it through reverence. Standing in awe as if spiritual beings were present, when in his chamber he has nothing to be ashamed of even in its darkest corner; maintaining vigilance over every moment and subtle incipient tendency, when in his carriage he sees it resting before him on the crossbar. He insists that reverence always prevail over indolence, leaving no evasive or hidden selfish motives, stopping only when he has returned to uprightness and straightness. Using reverence to straighten the interior, is not that whereby he benefits the exterior already prepared in advance?

He also recognizes that the exterior must not fail to be square—for this is the regulation of virtue—and so he squares it through righteousness. His actions conform to the carpenter's square, without indulging his passions in the selfishness of private ease; his affairs are planned in accordance with the Way, without drowning his will in the error of violating constant norms. He insists that righteousness always prevail over desire, possessing the beauty of evenness, regularity, squareness, and uprightness, stopping only when he treads the path of great squareness. Using righteousness to square the exterior, is not that whereby he nourishes the interior made ever deeper?

Ah! When learning reaches this point, one's straightness can hit the marking-line, and after a long time one will be straight without needing the line; one's squareness can match the carpenter's square, and after a long time one will be square without needing the square. Does not the greatness that is "not solitary" emerge from this?

Yet if we consider further: the Way of Qian (Heaven) values expansion, and so it speaks of benevolence and propriety together; the Way of Kun (Earth) values contraction, and so it singles out righteousness and uprightness. For when the superior man examines himself, his only worry is that he is not strict enough; even when he is strict, he still fears that laxity may follow—how much less would he dare to be indulgent with himself! Therefore, the two words "reverence" and "righteousness" are the instructive admonitions of the Cinnabar Book (Danshu) and the family precepts of the Duke of Zhou. Yet of the two, reverence is especially the root. When Confucius told Zhonggong, "When going abroad, behave as though you were receiving a great guest; when employing the common people, behave as though you were assisting at a great sacrifice," commentators have taken this to represent the Way of Kun—truly so!

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
乾以易知坤以簡能
顧鼎臣〔　〕

大傳論造化之生成一出於無心也蓋天地之
所以大者其機神也知始作成一易簡而已何
===
庸心哉夫子言此欲人法易簡也蓋曰大易之
理備于天地人知天地之化大而亦知其化之
神乎今夫功莫難於創始非若循襲者之易爲
力也乾知大始吾意物之仰於天者衆而天之
生之亦難矣不知乾健而動者也剛決之性當
機則發而觸之者槖籥自開陽生之意遇時則
行而迎之者機緘自動物莫能禦故始萬品之
物易猶一物也時莫能窮故始萬古之物易猶
punctuated:
乾以易知，坤以簡能。
