竊有聖賢之志矢奉賡歌之末非堯舜何
敢敷陳苟惟溫飽之謀撻市朝可勝愧耻
何期齒錄遂見身親茲蓋伏遇
===
○○○○
禹湯勤儉
堯舜寬仁茂稟
英姿備天地中和之極光膺
寶籙纘
祖
宗功德之隆穆穆而宜
君宜
punctuated: 著保衡之訓；周灝絺四墉之狀，爰昭篤棐之猷。蓋書雖盡意，意盡言，故章施是設；而事以不尊不信，則聖哲爲徵。獻忠比于韋弦，懋德資其斧藻，托契攸在，振古如斯。若乃宋弘座障之規，義存好德；班伯畫屏之諫，志在繩愆；璟慕《無逸》于內庭，文績《尚書》于太液，彼雖洵美，終乏兼資。〔臣初〕誦讀之時，竊有聖賢之志，矢奉賡歌之末，非堯、舜何敢敷陳？苟惟溫飽之謀，撻市朝可勝愧耻！何期齒錄，遂見身親。茲蓋伏遇○○○○，禹、湯勤儉，堯、舜寬仁。茂稟英姿，備天地中和之極；光膺寶籙，纘祖宗功德之隆。穆穆而宜君宜…
translation_en: …so as to make manifest the instructions of the Protector and Balancer (Baoheng, i.e., Yi Yin 伊尹); in the Zhou [Hall of] Bright Essence [?; 周灝, for 明堂], they depicted the scenes on the four walls, thereby illustrating the counsels of devoted assistance. For although writing can fully express ideas and ideas can be fully expressed in words, visual displays are nonetheless set up; and since matters that are not revered are not trusted, the sages and worthies are taken as verification. In offering loyalty, these may be compared to the soft leather and taut bowstring [worn for self-correction]; in cultivating virtue, one relies upon their ornamental refinement. Wherein the entrusted bond lies, it has been thus since antiquity. As for Song Hong’s 宋弘 admonition over the seat-screen, its meaning lay in loving virtue; Ban Bo’s 班伯 remonstrance via the painted screen, its intent was to correct faults; [Song] Jing’s 宋璟 emulation of the "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi 無逸) in the inner court, and [Tang] Wen[zong]’s 唐文宗 painting [?; 文績] of the Book of Documents (Shangshu 尚書) at the Taiye Pool—although those were truly admirable, in the end they lacked comprehensive utility. When [I, your servant, first] engaged in recitation and study, I privately cherished the aspirations of the sages and worthies, vowing to serve at the lowest ranks of those who join in the responsive songs of court, and daring not to set forth anything before the throne save the ways of Yao 堯 and Shun 舜. Had I sought only warm clothes and a full belly, how could I bear the shame of feeling as though flogged in the marketplace and court! How could I have expected to be enrolled in the official register and thus witness these things in person? This is because I have humbly encountered [Your Majesty], who possesses the diligence and frugality of Yu 禹 and Tang 湯, and the broad benevolence of Yao and Shun. Richly endowed with heroic bearing, You embody the ultimate harmony and centrality of Heaven and Earth; gloriously receiving the precious mandate, You continue the exalted merit and virtue of the Imperial Ancestors. August and solemn, fitting to be Lord and fitting to be…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
王克邁率由之訓明明而有典有則丕承
貽厥之思屬玆
乾元建始之初已信
令德守文之主然匪進則退者學可無夙夜之
勤矧難得易失者時宜及春秋之富而臣
職叨三事忠罔寸裨涉文字以來之書粗
能成誦憶聖賢未墜之事謂必可師是以
采其較明審厥象肖君如虞夏商周之盛
臣若皐夔伊傅之良周公思而四事兼孔
===
子作而六藝備先聖後聖比肩于毫素之
間大賢次賢接武于蟬緗之上璀璨乎宗
彜藻火粉米黼黻絺繡之文具在依稀乎
几席盤盂觴豆戶牖弓劒之戒如存玉質
金相儼當年之有覿尸居淵默同在目之
無情目擊而不容聲卷開而大有益條爲
六十卷玄黃之體分德罔二三蓋純白之
道備人于今而遊古物有假而助宜纂輯
忻成函封敬
punctuated: 王，克邁率由之訓；明明而有典有則，丕承貽厥之思。屬玆乾元建始之初，已信令德守文之主。然匪進則退者學，可無夙夜之勤；矧難得易失者時，宜及春秋之富。而臣職叨三事，忠罔寸裨。涉文字以來之書，粗能成誦；憶聖賢未墜之事，謂必可師。是以采其較明，審厥象肖。君如虞、夏、商、周之盛，臣若皐、夔、伊、傅之良；周公思而四事兼，孔子作而六藝備。先聖後聖，比肩于毫素之間；大賢次賢，接武于蟬緗之上。璀璨乎，宗彜、藻、火、粉、米、黼、黻、絺繡之文具在；依稀乎，几席、盤盂、觴豆、戶牖、弓劒之戒如存。玉質金相，儼當年之有覿；尸居淵默，同在目之無情。目擊而不容聲，卷開而大有益。條爲六十卷，玄黃之體分；德罔二三，蓋純白之道備。人于今而遊古，物有假而助宜。纂輯忻成，函封敬
translation_en: … king, able to advance the teachings of following established ways; illustriously possessing canons and standards, grandly inheriting the thoughts handed down to posterity. At this very beginning of the inaugural era of the Sovereign Principle, we already trust in you as a ruler of virtuous excellence who upholds the civil order. Yet learning is that which retreats if it does not advance—how could one be without diligence from dawn to night? Moreover, time is that which is hard to gain and easy to lose—one ought to seize it while in the prime of youth. Meanwhile, your servant unworthily holds office among the Three Ducal Ministries, yet my loyalty has yielded not an寸 of benefit. Having perused books since the invention of writing, I can roughly recite them from memory; recalling the deeds of sages and worthies that have not fallen into oblivion, I believe they can surely serve as models. Therefore, I have selected the moreperspicuous among them and examined their depicted likenesses: rulers from the flourishing eras of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou; ministers as virtuous as Gao Yao, Kui, Yi Yin, and Fu Yue; the Duke of Zhou pondering until he encompassed the four matters, and Confucius composing until the Six Arts were complete. Former sages and later sages stand shoulder to shoulder upon brush and silk; great worthies and lesser worthies follow in each other's footsteps across the pale-yellow scrolls. Resplendently, the patterns of ancestral temple vessels, waterweed, flames, white rice, axe-shapes, symbol-pairs, and fine embroidery are all present; faintly, the admonitions inscribed on armrests and mats, basins and bowls, goblets and platters, doors and windows, and bows and swords seem still intact. With jade substance and golden form, it is as dignified as witnessing them in their own day; sitting motionless as a ritual personator in deep silence, they are like unfeeling objects right before the eyes. At a glance, no words are needed; once the scroll is unrolled, there is great benefit. Arranged into sixty chapters (juan), the forms of heaven's dark and earth's yellow are distinguished; virtue knows no duplicity or vacillation, for the way of pure whiteness is complete. Men in the present may thus roam in antiquity, and things borrowed as illustrations help to do what is right. Rejoicing that the compilation is complete, I have sealed it in a case and respectfully …

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
上
絲綸字貴鸞傳華衮之褒組繪心勞頓喜
垂旒之賞
申命清嚴之署月分
進覽之程虞拜陶歌不數從寛問一漢稱賈
語無論使俊陳三尚期流布于薦紳
特詔鍥鐫于文梓錦章緹帙爛披七曜之圖寶
笈牙籤爛發五神之檢
賜出尚方之副榮增近侍之光蓋
===
聖心冥契于百王責臣等交修夫一德
師能自得
善與人同敢不仰體
睠懷俯修舊植學于古乃有獲將助多聞所
求
君而未能敢忘自責必正已而物正斯爲臣兩
盡臣伏願
日月就將念終始典于學
夙宵祗懼於緝熙殫厥心
punctuated: 上。絲綸字貴，鸞傳華衮之褒；組繪心勞，頓喜垂旒之賞。申命清嚴之署，月分進覽之程。虞拜陶歌，不數從寛問一；漢稱賈語，無論使俊陳三。尚期流布于薦紳，特詔鍥鐫于文梓。錦章緹帙，爛披七曜之圖；寶笈牙籤，爛發五神之檢。賜出尚方之副，榮增近侍之光。蓋聖心冥契于百王，責臣等交修夫一德。師能自得，善與人同。敢不仰體睠懷，俯修舊植？學于古乃有獲，將助多聞；所求君而未能，敢忘自責？必正已而物正，斯爲臣兩盡臣。伏願日月就將，念終始典于學；夙宵祗懼，於緝熙殫厥心。
translation_en:
…presented above. Each word of the imperial rescript is precious, as phoenix-like proclamations convey praise assplendid as ceremonial robes; our painstaking efforts in weaving and illustrating are suddenly rewarded with the delight of appreciation from behind the hanging pearls of the imperial crown. You have further commanded the pure and solemn Hanlin offices to divide the schedule for monthly presentation and imperial perusal. With Shun bowing and Gao Yao singing in harmony, one need not even count inquiring of Kuan about a single section; with the Han court praising Jia Yi's discourses, there is no need to mention ordering Jun to expound three chapters. Still hoping that this work might be circulated among the gentry and officials, You issued a special decree to have it carved onto fine catalpa woodblocks. In brocade chapters and red silk covers, the charts of the Seven Luminaries are brilliantly spread open; in treasured book-boxes with ivory tags, the registers of the Five Spirits are resplendently revealed. Bestowing duplicate copies from the Imperial Manufactories has added glory to the luster of Your close attendants.

Indeed, Your Sacred Mind is in silent accord with the hundred kings of antiquity, and You charge Your servants to cultivate together pure and undivided virtue. Finding a teacher in oneself, You share goodness with others. How could we dare not look up to embody Your gracious concern, and bow down to cultivate our established learning? Only by studying antiquity does one attain results, which will aid in broadening Your knowledge; in what we ask of our Ruler yet have not been able to fulfill ourselves, how dare we forget self-reproach? Only when one rectifies oneself are others rectified, and thus in serving as ministers we fulfill both duties [?]. We humbly pray that You will advance daily and monthly, ever mindful from beginning to end of devoting Yourself to learning; and that morning and night You will remain reverently cautious, exhausting Your heart in continuing bright virtue…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
悟彼蒼黃五入而五色之絲隨化
契茲符節千里與千歲之聖非遥
察臣意不在丹青無漸移于山水
覽臣圖異於物色無遽委于塵埃秉茲
蒙養之初益勵
乾行之健士希賢賢希聖聖賢伍而綏猷人
法地地法天天地參而建極臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
===
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策五道
第一問
潘元和
同考試官教諭丘 批〔古帝王靈敏之資勤〕
誠之學敷對詳悉而望我
punctuated:
悟彼蒼黃五入，而五色之絲隨化；契茲符節，千里與千歲之聖非遥。察臣意不在丹青，無漸移于山水；覽臣圖異於物色，無遽委于塵埃。秉茲蒙養之初，益勵乾行之健。士希賢，賢希聖，聖賢伍而綏猷；人法地，地法天，天地參而建極。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁場
策五道

第一問
潘元和
同考試官教諭丘批：〔古帝王靈敏之資、勤〕誠之學，敷對詳悉，而望我
translation_en:
…comprehending how silk dipped five times into dark and yellow dyes transforms into the five colors; matching like two halves of a tally, the sages a thousand miles away and a thousand years removed are not far off. Discern that Your servant's intent does not lie in mere pigments and painting, so do not let Your attention gradually drift toward landscapes; view Your servant's illustrations as distinct from mere outward appearances, and do not hastily cast them away into the dust. Upholding this initial phase of youthful cultivation, all the more strive with the vigor of Heaven's movement. The scholar aspires to be a worthy, and the worthy aspires to be a sage—ranking alongside the sages and worthies, You shall pacify and guide the way; man models himself on Earth, and Earth models itself on Heaven—forming a triad with Heaven and Earth, You shall establish the Supreme Ultimate. Your servant, overcome to the utmost with earnest emotion and trepidation as he gazes up toward Heaven and looks up to Your Sacred Majesty, respectfully presents this memorial of gratitude for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session
Five Policy Essays

First Question
Pan Yuanhe 潘元he
Associate Examiner Instructor Qiu comments: [Regarding the keen innate endowments of the ancient emperors and kings, and their] diligent and sincere learning, the exposition and reply are detailed and thorough, while the hope that our…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖天子法古懋學之意尤爲懇至是有裨於理道者
同考試官教諭蔣　批　我
皇上天縱聰明銳精向道眞邁古帝王者是作揄揚頗悉而於務學
處尤惓惓致意具見忠愛之篤
同考試官教授黃　批　敷敭
聖學具中肯綮且體正而大詞峻而新尤徵素養
同考試官知縣師　批　敷對詳明已徵博洽
而亹亹規言尤悉忠愛之悃
考試官右中允何　批　我
===
皇上天縱神解
英年好學軼蹤近代儷美皇王子能發之而備舉
聖修深寓規勸眞可爲
啓沃助矣
考試官左中允范　批　古帝王冲年御寓致治無
疆雖其明哲天縱而聖學淵源具在訓典子能
撮其綱要盡一以陳而意本忠誠辭復懇惻殆
有志於正
□□國之學者可爲
punctuated:
聖天子法古懋學之意，尤爲懇至，是有裨於理道者。
同考試官教諭蔣批：我皇上天縱聰明，銳精向道，眞邁古帝王者。是作揄揚頗悉，而於務學處尤惓惓致意，具見忠愛之篤。
同考試官教授黃批：敷敭聖學，具中肯綮；且體正而大，詞峻而新，尤徵素養。
同考試官知縣師批：敷對詳明，已徵博洽；而亹亹規言，尤悉忠愛之悃。
考試官右中允何批：我皇上天縱神解，英年好學，軼蹤近代，儷美皇王。子能發之，而備舉聖修，深寓規勸，眞可爲啓沃助矣。
考試官左中允范批：古帝王冲年御寓，致治無疆，雖其明哲天縱，而聖學淵源，具在訓典。子能撮其綱要，盡一以陳，而意本忠誠，辭復懇惻，殆有志於正□□國之學者，可爲
translation_en:
… His Sacred Majesty the Son of Heaven emulate antiquity and exert himself in learning is especially earnest and thorough. This is beneficial to the principles of governance.

Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Jiang comments: Our Emperor is endowed by Heaven with intelligence and sagacity, and focuses his finest energies on pursuing the Way, truly surpassing the emperors and kings of antiquity. This essay sets forth its praise in considerable detail, and on the point of dedicating oneself to learning it is especially earnest and attentive, fully demonstrating the depth of the candidate's loyalty and devotion.

Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoshou) Huang comments: In expounding upon sacred learning, he hits the crucial points throughout; moreover, his style is upright and grand, and his diction is lofty and fresh, which especially attests to his long-cultivated scholarship.

Associate Examiner District Magistrate (zhixian) Shi comments: His exposition and reply are detailed and clear, already attesting to his broad erudition; and his tireless words of admonition especially reveal the sincerity of his loyalty and devotion.

Examiner Right Companion to the Heir Apparent (you zhongyun) He comments: Our Emperor is endowed by Heaven with divine comprehension, and in his youthful years delights in learning, surpassing the traces of recent ages and matching the excellence of the ancient sovereigns and kings. The candidate is able to bring this to light, while comprehensively citing the cultivation of the sages and deeply embedding admonition and encouragement; this can truly serve as an aid to enlightening and enriching the imperial mind.

Examiner Left Companion to the Heir Apparent (zuo zhongyun) Fan comments: When the emperors and kings of antiquity ruled the realm in their tender years and achieved boundless good governance, although their bright wisdom was endowed by Heaven, the origins and foundations of their sacred learning were all contained in the canonical instructions. The candidate is able to grasp their essential outlines and set them forth completely and consistently; his intent is rooted in loyalty and sincerity, and his words are moreover earnest and heartfelt. He is surely one who aspires to the learning that rectifies [the ruler and orders the] state; we may congratulate…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖朝得士慶矣
帝王有所難得者高世之資而尤有所急
務者聖修之學生縱諸天不待年而裕者
高世之資也習成諸人恒與日而新者聖
修之學也茲二者莫尚乎相兼而常患乎
不相發君人者雖任其可恃而力勗其所
可爲故資之局而學充以充猶爲一時之
英辟若天者逈而人益以至非振古之明
后不足與此也執事以帝王生禀學術下
===
詢葢以端本格心之猷啓承學意甚盛也
愚也繪天測海何足以復明問哉雖然敢
略陳之書曰人求多聞時惟建事學於古
訓乃有獲是學之爲王者事其已久矣然
有謂壯而好學如日中之光老而好學如
炳燭之明弗若少而好學如日出之陽夫
王者統三才而育萬有作君師以興治敎
休命雖隆艱大亦集矧震出也獨早豈離
照之遽融且閱理也未深難少成而若性
punctuated:
聖朝得士慶矣。
帝王有所難得者高世之資，而尤有所急務者聖修之學。生縱諸天、不待年而裕者，高世之資也；習成諸人、恒與日而新者，聖修之學也。茲二者莫尚乎相兼，而常患乎不相發。君人者雖任其可恃，而力勗其所可爲。故資之局而學充以充，猶爲一時之英辟；若天者逈而人益以至，非振古之明后不足與此也。執事以帝王生禀學術下詢，葢以端本格心之猷啓承學，意甚盛也。愚也繪天測海，何足以復明問哉？雖然，敢略陳之。《書》曰：「人求多聞，時惟建事，學於古訓，乃有獲。」是學之爲王者事，其已久矣。然有謂：「壯而好學，如日中之光；老而好學，如炳燭之明；弗若少而好學，如日出之陽。」夫王者統三才而育萬有，作君師以興治敎，休命雖隆，艱大亦集。矧震出也獨早，豈離照之遽融？且閱理也未深，難少成而若性。
translation_en:
… rejoice that the Sacred Dynasty has obtained such a scholar!

What is difficult for emperors and kings to obtain is a talent that transcends the age, and what is even more urgent for them is the learning of sage cultivation. That which is endowed by Heaven at birth and is abundant without waiting for age is a talent that transcends the age; that which is formed through human practice and is constantly renewed day by day is the learning of sage cultivation. Nothing is more prized than combining these two, yet the common worry is that they do not mutually reinforce each other. One who rules over men, though he may rely on what is dependable in his nature, must strenuously exert himself in what can be achieved through effort. Therefore, even if one's natural talent is limited, yet through learning one fills it to the utmost, one may still become a heroic ruler of an era; whereas if what comes from Heaven is already towering, and human effort is further brought to perfection, none but an enlightened sovereign of all antiquity would be worthy of this. Your Excellency has condescended to inquire about the innate endowments and scholarly pursuits of emperors and kings; this is surely to inspire us students with plans for rectifying the fundamental and correcting the ruler's heart—a most magnificent intention. Ignorant as I am, trying to paint the heavens and fathom the sea, how could I suffice to answer your enlightened question? Even so, I dare to outline my views briefly. The Book of Documents says: "When a man seeks to hear much, it is to establish affairs; by learning from the ancient lessons, one achieves results." Thus, that learning has been the business of a true king is of long standing indeed. Yet it has been said: "To love learning in one's prime is like the light of the midday sun; to love learning in old age is like the brightness of a lit candle; neither is as good as loving learning in youth, which is like the sun at dawn." Now, a true king unites the Three Powers and nurtures all things, acting as both ruler and teacher to promote governance and instruction; although the Mandate of Heaven is glorious, great difficulties also gather upon him. How much more so when he emerges in the East [as heir and ruler, like the Zhen trigram] uniquely early—how could his radiant illumination [like the Li trigram] suddenly be all-pervading? Moreover, when his experience of principles is not yet deep, it is difficult for what is formed in youth to become like second nature. …

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
昔武丁致中興矣然舊學甘盤則明哲之
作則有基漢宣崇儒術矣然長自民間則
石渠之談經稍暮若是乎功可積而崇顈
不可強而夙也周成襁褓踐阼矣以有周
公等四聖維之故事無過舉漢昭八齡纘
緒矣以得韋賢等諸儒傳之故德用平成
若是乎養可慎而豫道不可徑而悟也粤
稽上古軒轅高辛生而神靈弱而能言而
有大顓栢招之學顓頊帝嚳堯靜淵疏通欽
===
明文思而有綠圖尹壽之學舜在冲年則
明于庶物棄自兒時則志如巨人身應律
度者禹也而其德不違其仁可親其言可
信所謂神而明之者非耶生有聖瑞者文
王也而在毋不憂在傅不勤處師不煩所
謂默而成之者非耶是數聖人者皆卓絕
瓌奇立于才品形器之中通乎耳目心思
之外或先天以開人或垂世而立極猶兩
儀之有日月不得則不奠四序之有寒暑
punctuated: 昔武丁致中興矣，然舊學甘盤，則明哲之作則有基；漢宣崇儒術矣，然長自民間，則石渠之談經稍暮。若是乎，功可積而崇，顈不可強而夙也。周成襁褓踐阼矣，以有周公等四聖維之，故事無過舉；漢昭八齡纘緒矣，以得韋賢等諸儒傳之，故德用平成。若是乎，養可慎而豫，道不可徑而悟也。粤稽上古，軒轅、高辛生而神靈，弱而能言，而有大顓、栢招之學；顓頊、帝嚳、堯靜淵疏通，欽明文思，而有綠圖、尹壽之學；舜在冲年，則明于庶物；棄自兒時，則志如巨人。身應律度者，禹也，而其德不違，其仁可親，其言可信，所謂「神而明之」者非耶？生有聖瑞者，文王也，而在毋不憂，在傅不勤，處師不煩，所謂「默而成之」者非耶？是數聖人者，皆卓絕瓌奇，立于才品形器之中，通乎耳目心思之外，或先天以開人，或垂世而立極。猶兩儀之有日月，不得則不奠；四序之有寒暑，
translation_en:
In antiquity, King Wuding 武丁 of Shang brought about a dynastic restoration, yet because in former days he had studied under Gan Pan 甘盤, his acting as a wise and discerning model had a solid foundation. Emperor Xuan of Han 漢宣帝 revered Confucian learning, yet because he grew up among the common people, his discussions of the classics in the Stone Canal Pavilion (Shiqu ge 石渠閣) came somewhat late in life. Thus it is that merit can be accumulated to reach great heights, whereas acute brilliance cannot be forced to appear prematurely! King Cheng of Zhou 周成王 ascended the throne while still in swaddling clothes, yet because he had the four sages, including the Duke of Zhou 周公, to uphold him, his affairs were free of errant actions. Emperor Zhao of Han 漢昭帝 succeeded to the imperial line at the age of eight, yet because he obtained various Confucian scholars such as Wei Xian 韋賢 to instruct [reading 傅 for 傳] him, his virtue thereby achieved peaceful completion. Thus it is that cultivation can be made careful and prepared in advance, whereas the Way cannot be comprehended by shortcuts!

When we examine high antiquity: Xuanyuan 軒轅 (the Yellow Emperor) and Gaoxin 高辛 (Emperor Ku 帝嚳) were born神靈 (divinely intelligent) and could speak while still infants, yet they had the learning of Dazhuan 大顓 [usually 大填] and Bozhao 栢招; Zhuanxu 顓頊, Emperor Ku, and Yao 堯 were tranquil, deep, and penetrating, reverent, intelligent, accomplished, and thoughtful, yet they had the learning of Lutu 綠圖 and Yin Shou 尹壽. When Shun 舜 was in his youth, he clearly understood the multitude of things; from the time Qi 棄 (Houji 后稷) was a child, his ambitions were like those of an adult. He whose person corresponded to the standard measures and pitch-pipes was Yu 禹—his virtue did not deviate, his benevolence was approachable, and his words were trustworthy; is this not what is meant by "comprehending it through divine insight"? He whose birth was accompanied by sage auspices was King Wen 文王—while with his mother he caused no worry, with his tutor he required no laborious effort, and with his teacher he caused no trouble; is this not what is meant by "completing it in silence"?

These several sages were all unsurpassed and extraordinary; standing amid endowments, capacities, forms, and vessels, they penetrated beyond the reach of ears, eyes, mind, and thought, either preceding Heaven to open the way for humankind, or handing down models to the world to establish the supreme standard. They are like the sun and moon in the Two Modes (heaven and earth), without which they cannot be settled; or cold and heat in the four seasons,…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
不得則不成五氣之有陰陽不得則不運
人物之有造化不得則不蕃知周乎萬類
而不遺道濟乎天下而不過雖無岐于幼
壯無假于修習而幼而好學者必茲其選
矣三代而下卽僅有之亦瞠乎哉漢明帝
十歲通春秋而好學隆師後世鮮儷章帝
英年向儒術而白虎議奏前烈有光少帝
機穎神明爽發讀書七行俱下者宋孝武
也幼稱聰睿屬文立成讀書一覽十行者
===
梁簡文也所謂幼敏而好學四君若亦其
人歟然或治沿雜覇業阻偏安者何也性
天之道未弘則學莫識其大經綸之志有
溺則才弗拓其資可不惜哉天啓休明誕
開太平于億萬世肆我
皇上乃應運而篤生焉
弱齒含元岐嶷神授
十齡出閤溫文日新固已繫天下之望歸四
海之心矣及正位
punctuated: 不得則不成，五氣之有陰陽，不得則不運，人物之有造化，不得則不蕃。知周乎萬類而不遺，道濟乎天下而不過，雖無岐于幼壯，無假于修習，而幼而好學者，必茲其選矣。三代而下，卽僅有之，亦瞠乎哉！漢明帝十歲通《春秋》，而好學隆師，後世鮮儷；章帝英年向儒術，而白虎議奏，前烈有光。少帝機穎，神明爽發，讀書七行俱下者，宋孝武也；幼稱聰睿，屬文立成，讀書一覽十行者，梁簡文也。所謂幼敏而好學，四君若亦其人歟？然或治沿雜覇，業阻偏安者，何也？性天之道未弘，則學莫識其大；經綸之志有溺，則才弗拓其資，可不惜哉！天啓休明，誕開太平于億萬世，肆我皇上乃應運而篤生焉。弱齒含元，岐嶷神授；十齡出閤，溫文日新，固已繫天下之望，歸四海之心矣。及正位
translation_en: … without which they cannot be completed; just as the five atmospheric forces have yin and yang, without which they cannot circulate; and just as humans and creatures have the creative transformations of nature, without which they cannot flourish. Their knowledge encompassed all the myriad things without omission, and their Way brought aid to the entire world without excess. Although there was no divergence between their youth and maturity, and they had no need to rely on cultivation and practice, when it comes to those who loved learning in their youth, they must surely be the foremost examples! From the Three Dynasties onward, even the rare few who existed were left staring helplessly far behind! Emperor Ming of the Han mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) at ten years of age, and in his love of learning and honoring of teachers, later generations rarely had his match; Emperor Zhang in his youthful prime inclined toward Confucian learning, and with the discussions memorialized at the White Tiger Hall (Baihu guan), the achievements of his predecessors shone brightly. He who as a young ruler was quick-witted and sharp, whose spirit and intelligence were bright and vigorous, and who could read seven columns of text at a glance, was Emperor Xiaowu of the Liu Song; he who in childhood was praised for his intelligence and perspicacity, who could compose writings on the spot, and who could take in ten columns of text in a single glance, was Emperor Jianwen of the Liang. As for what is called being clever in youth and fond of learning, might these four rulers also be such men? Yet why is it that some of them followed governance mixed with the Way of the Hegemon, while the enterprises of others were confined to partial rule over a divided realm? Because the Way of their innate heaven-bestowed nature was not broadened, their learning failed to recognize what was great; because their ambition to order the state became bogged down, their talent failed to expand upon its natural endowment—is this not a pity? Heaven has ushered in auspicious brightness, grandly opening up great peace for hundreds of millions of generations, and thus our August Emperor was born in response to this destiny. In his tender years he harbored primal virtue, his precocious distinction bestowed by the divine; at the age of ten he emerged from the eastern palace pavilion to begin his formal education, his gentle and cultured refinement renewing itself daily, so that the hopes of the entire world were already bound to him and the hearts of the Four Seas turned toward him. And when he ascended to the rightful position of…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
宸極
玄德愈光
進道不需于歲時
講學靡間乎寒暑
任輔弼則隆舟楫鹽梅之托
親儒臣則厚晉接蕃庶之恩嘉納
帝鑒圖說而
披覽不倦一金匱丹書之契也
命書四箴六箴而
顧諟常存一盤銘几杖之警也尊養極于
===
兩宮而舜之大孝著
周澤渥于四表而堯之至仁溥
潛心體道而嗜好不萌非清明之在躬乎
虛懷從善而嘉言罔伏非志氣之如神乎易
稱首出庶物萬國咸寧傳表聰明睿智足
以有臨端於
今日見之信乎帝王之禀與衆庶異我
皇上之生尤與近古帝王異謂前有軒轅數聖
punctuated: 宸極，玄德愈光，進道不需于歲時，講學靡間乎寒暑。任輔弼，則隆舟楫鹽梅之托；親儒臣，則厚晉接蕃庶之恩。嘉納《帝鑒圖說》而披覽不倦，一金匱丹書之契也；命書《四箴》、《六箴》而顧諟常存，一盤銘几杖之警也。尊養極于兩宮，而舜之大孝著；周澤渥于四表，而堯之至仁溥。潛心體道而嗜好不萌，非「清明之在躬」乎？虛懷從善而嘉言罔伏，非「志氣之如神」乎？《易》稱「首出庶物，萬國咸寧」，《傳》表「聰明睿智，足以有臨」，端於今日見之。信乎，帝王之禀與衆庶異，我皇上之生尤與近古帝王異。謂「前有軒轅數聖…
translation_en: … the imperial throne, His profound virtue has shone ever more brightly. Advancing in the Way without waiting upon the passage of years and seasons, He pursues His lectures and learning without interruption through winter cold or summer heat. In employing His chief counselors, He elevates the charge of acting as boats and oars, salt and plum; in drawing close to His Confucian ministers, He lavishes the grace of frequent audiences, as in the Jin hexagram. Accepting with approval the Illustrated Mirror for Emperors (Dijian tushuo) and perusing it tirelessly, He matches the accord of the Golden Coffer and the Cinnabar Books; ordering the transcription of the Four Admonitions (Sizhen) and the Six Admonitions (Liuzhen) to keep His gaze ever fixed upon them, He matches the warnings inscribed on washbasins, armrests, and staffs. In reverent care reaching the utmost toward the Two Empresses Dowager, the great filial piety of Shun is made manifest; in all-encompassing beneficence saturating the four quarters of the world, the supreme benevolence of Yao is universally spread. Immersing His mind to embody the Way so that sensual desires do not sprout—is this not "clarity and brightness residing within the person"? Following the good with an open heart so that fine words never lie hidden—is this not "will and vital energy being like a spirit"? What the Book of Changes (Yi) praises as "rising preeminent above the multitude of things, so that all the myriad states enjoy peace," and what the Commentary (Zhuan) highlights as "perspicacity, clarity, wisdom, and intelligence sufficient to exercise rule"—all this is truly witnessed today. Truly indeed do the natural endowments of emperors and kings differ from those of the common multitude, and the birth of Our Sovereign Majesty differs all the more from the emperors and kings of recent antiquity! To say that "in former times there were Xuanyuan and those few…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
人今有
明天子豈爲過哉雖然竊聞古昔聖人所以爲
聖爲神者非徒以其至虛至明無所不知
無所不能也正以其好問好察不敢高天
下以能矜天下以知也是故兢兢業業其
存誠也精一執中其傳心也稽衆舍已詢
岳牧拜昌言其受人也祖識宣序糾虔無
怠朝怠夕其勵精也夫以五帝三王神聖
若彼其好學不厭若此此其故可推矣自
古聖主臨政願治身致太平未有一事不
===
由于學況
御極之始不以講學爲先可乎自古聖主進德
修業終身而行未甞一日敢忘于學況
春秋方盛不以務學爲急可乎且帝王之學
非韋布之所謂學也固將舉而措之以治
天下國家者也若彼日進太平御覽三卷
者末矣作典論三篇者浮矣雅好文辭才
藻甚美者荒矣故曰上學以神中學以心
punctuated: 人，今有明天子，豈爲過哉！雖然，竊聞古昔聖人所以爲聖爲神者，非徒以其至虛至明，無所不知，無所不能也；正以其好問好察，不敢高天下以能，矜天下以知也。是故兢兢業業，其存誠也；精一執中，其傳心也；稽衆舍已，詢岳牧，拜昌言，其受人也；祖識宣序，糾虔無怠朝怠夕，其勵精也。夫以五帝三王神聖若彼，其好學不厭若此，此其故可推矣。自古聖主臨政願治，身致太平，未有一事不由于學，況御極之始，不以講學爲先，可乎？自古聖主進德修業，終身而行，未甞一日敢忘于學，況春秋方盛，不以務學爲急，可乎？且帝王之學，非韋布之所謂學也，固將舉而措之，以治天下國家者也。若彼日進《太平御覽》三卷者，末矣；作《典論》三篇者，浮矣；雅好文辭、才藻甚美者，荒矣。故曰：「上學以神，中學以心，
translation_en: … sages in antiquity, and today we have an enlightened Son of Heaven—how could that be an exaggeration! Even so, I have heard that the reason the sages of antiquity were sage and divine was not merely because they were supremely receptive and supremely clear-sighted, knowing all things and capable of all things; it was precisely because they loved to ask questions and loved to examine things, not daring to set themselves above the world on account of their abilities or boast to the world of their knowledge. Therefore, being cautious and attentive was how they preserved sincerity; being refined and single-minded and holding fast to the Mean was how they transmitted the Way of the Mind; consulting the multitude and setting aside their own views, inquiring of the Four Peaks and the Twelve Pastors, and bowing to splendid words of counsel was how they accepted others; recognizing the old and proclaiming order, and maintaining reverent vigilance without slackening morning or evening, was how they roused their vigor. Now, given that the Five Emperors and Three Kings were as divine and sage as that, yet loved learning without tire like this, the reason for it can be inferred. Since antiquity, among sage rulers who assumed governance wishing for order and personally brought about great peace, there was never a single matter that did not stem from learning; how much more so at the very beginning of ascending the throne—would it do not to put the pursuit of learning first? Since antiquity, sage rulers advanced in virtue and cultivated their enterprise, practicing it throughout their lives and never daring for a single day to forget learning; how much more so when in the very prime of youth—would it do not to make devotion to learning an urgent priority? Moreover, the learning of emperors and kings is not what commoners in leather belts and coarse cloth call learning; rather, it is something to be taken up and put into practice in order to govern the empire and the state. As for one who had three scrolls of the Imperial Readings of the Taiping Era (Taiping yulan) presented to him daily, that was superficial; one who composed the three chapters of the Normative Discourses (Dianlun), that was frivolous; and one who was fond of literary expressions and possessed very fine rhetorical flair, that was indulgent neglect. Therefore it is said: "The highest learning is with the spirit; the middle learning is with the mind; …"

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
下學以耳今
主上信神聖愚以爲高世之資殆可有而不可
恃也聖修之學當以神而弗以耳也是故
其定志貴堅其析理貴精其養德貴純其
體道貴恒何言乎堅也萬化之原起乎君
心心猶水也淸之終日乃見眉睫不過一
撓莫矚方圓故在
明主獨觀而允執之往聖爲的至善爲歸不雜
不移允迪可期易曰正其本萬事理是已
===
何言乎精也今
經筵講讀可謂密矣然非從容降接則無以
盡臣下之情非往復研究則無以見聖人
之奧請於進講之時意有未喻卽詳爲諮
問必至洞徹乃已其諸六曹職掌今時要
務如財用匱乏閭閻疾苦武備積隳士風
日卑一切吏弊國蠹靡不纖析而縷舉之
則訏謨至理日達
睿聰奚必升九天之上而後知日月星辰履八
punctuated: 下學以耳。今主上信神聖，愚以爲高世之資，殆可有而不可恃也；聖修之學，當以神而弗以耳也。是故其定志貴堅，其析理貴精，其養德貴純，其體道貴恒。何言乎堅也？萬化之原，起乎君心。心猶水也，淸之終日，乃見眉睫；不過一撓，莫矚方圓。故在明主獨觀而允執之，往聖爲的，至善爲歸，不雜不移，允迪可期。《易》曰：「正其本，萬事理。」是已。何言乎精也？今經筵講讀可謂密矣，然非從容降接，則無以盡臣下之情；非往復研究，則無以見聖人之奧。請於進講之時，意有未喻，卽詳爲諮問，必至洞徹乃已。其諸六曹職掌、今時要務，如財用匱乏、閭閻疾苦、武備積隳、士風日卑，一切吏弊國蠹，靡不纖析而縷舉之。則訏謨至理，日達睿聰，奚必升九天之上而後知日月星辰，履八
translation_en:
… and the lowest kind of learning is achieved through the ear.” Now His Majesty is truly divine and sagely, yet in my humble opinion, a natural endowment that surpasses the age is perhaps something one may possess, but not something on which one should rely; the learning of sagely self-cultivation ought to be engaged with the spirit and not merely with the ear. Therefore, in fixing one’s resolve, the essential thing is firmness; in analyzing principles, it is precision; in nourishing virtue, it is purity; and in embodying the Way, it is constancy.

What is meant by firmness? The source of the myriad transformations arises from the ruler’s mind. The mind is like water: let it settle and clear all day long, and it will reflect even one’s eyebrows and eyelashes; yet stir it but once, and one can no longer discern square from round. Thus it rests with the enlightened ruler to contemplate in solitude and hold fast to it sincerely, taking the former sages as his target and the highest good as his destination. Unmixed and unwavering, true fulfillment may then be expected. As the Book of Changes (Yi) says: “Rectify the root, and the myriad affairs will be in order.” This is what is meant.

What is meant by precision? At present, the lectures and readings at the Classics Colloquium (jingyan) may indeed be called frequent. Yet without unhurried and gracious reception, there is no way to draw out fully the sentiments of your ministers below; without back-and-forth inquiry and investigation, there is no way to perceive the profound depths of the sages. I beg that during the lectures, whenever the meaning is not yet clear, Your Majesty immediately make detailed inquiries, stopping only when complete comprehension is reached. As for the duties of the Six Ministries (liucao) and the pressing affairs of the present day—such as the exhaustion of fiscal resources, the hardships of the common people in their villages, the long-accumulated decay of military preparedness, the daily decline of scholarly morale, and all manner of bureaucratic abuses and pests of the state—none should fail to be minutely analyzed and enumerated in detail. Then great counsels and supreme principles will daily reach Your Majesty’s sagely hearing. Why must one ascend above the nine heavens before knowing the sun, moon, and stars, or tread to the distant limits of the eight…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
極之遥而後知山川謡俗與鴻濛盤古之
人遊而後識因革治亂哉何言乎純也舜
德罔怠荒是戒
聖齡冲茂輔養宜周必也寡欲以培其真主靜
以立其極戒慎恐懼以謹其獨居
深宮燕閒之中肅乎若
大廷廣衆之地接左右近習之際儼乎若親
近君子之時處聲色貨利之交湛然若夜
氣清明之境或如光武之講論經理夜分
===
乃寐或如成湯之昧爽丕顯懋敬厥德要
使引諭之音不絶于耳開悟之說時溉于
心罔一暴而十寒務月將而日就則純乎
純矣何言乎恒也善始者貴令終進銳者
慮退速故高大成于積小光明生乎緝熙
惟不息體乾之健不已法文之純而後可
也書曰念終始典于學厥德修罔覺其謂
是乎夫順風而呼聲非加疾而聽者自遠
登高而望目非加明而見者自晰今
punctuated: 極之遥而後知山川謡俗，與鴻濛盤古之人遊而後識因革治亂哉？何言乎純也？舜德罔怠，荒是戒。聖齡冲茂，輔養宜周，必也寡欲以培其真，主靜以立其極，戒慎恐懼以謹其獨。居深宮燕閒之中，肅乎若大廷廣衆之地；接左右近習之際，儼乎若親近君子之時；處聲色貨利之交，湛然若夜氣清明之境。或如光武之講論經理，夜分乃寐；或如成湯之昧爽丕顯，懋敬厥德。要使引諭之音不絶于耳，開悟之說時溉于心，罔一暴而十寒，務月將而日就，則純乎純矣。何言乎恒也？善始者貴令終，進銳者慮退速。故高大成于積小，光明生乎緝熙。惟不息體乾之健，不已法文之純，而後可也。《書》曰：「念終始典于學，厥德修罔覺。」其謂是乎！夫順風而呼，聲非加疾而聽者自遠；登高而望，目非加明而見者自晰。今
translation_en:
… the farthest reaches of the eight directions before knowing the mountains, rivers, and folk customs, or roam with the people of primordial chaos and Pangu before understanding institutional continuity and change, order and disorder?

What is meant by "pure"? Even with the virtue of Shun, he was never remiss and guarded against idleness. Since the imperial age is young and flourishing, his guidance and nurture should be comprehensive. Surely he must lessen desires to nourish his true nature, maintain tranquility to establish his ultimate standard, and exercise caution and apprehension to be watchful when alone. When dwelling in the leisure of the deep palace, may he be as reverent as if in the great court before the assembled multitude; when dealing with his attendants and close favorites, may he be as dignified as when drawing near to noble men; when amidst the temptations of music, beauty, goods, and profit, may he be as clear and unclouded as in the pure state of night air. At times, like Emperor Guangwu of Han, he might discuss and expound the principles of the Classics, sleeping only at midnight; or at times, like Tang the Successful, he might rise at dawn to manifest his virtue and earnestly revere it. In short, let the voices of guidance and admonition never cease in his ears, and let words that enlighten and awaken constantly water his mind, without warming it for one day only to freeze it for ten, striving for daily achievement and monthly progress—then his learning will be pure through and through.

What is meant by "constant"? Those who begin well value a good end; those who advance precipitously risk retreating swiftly. Thus, height and greatness are achieved by accumulating the small, and brilliance arises from continuous illumination. Only by ceaselessly embodying the vigor of the Qian hexagram and unremittingly modeling oneself on the purity of King Wen can this be achieved. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Be mindful from beginning to end to devote yourself constantly to learning, and your virtue will be cultivated without your being aware of it." Does it not refer to this!

Now, when one calls out with the wind, the voice is not made any louder, yet those who hear it are naturally far away; when one climbs high to gaze into the distance, the eyes are not made any brighter, yet what is seen is naturally clear. Now …

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
主上當鼎盛之年躬不世出之資蓋謂順呼而
高望之時非歟誠操軒皇以來心印而研
究躬行之是
堯舜之主也推此心以允升大猷是黃虞之世
也士生斯時而獲效用是翼爲明聽之遇
也兆姓得沐浴于德化之成是含哺擊壤
之適也若然則不特赫然爲一代務學之
明君且將卓然爲萬世帝王之標準是在
聖明深加之意而已愚也請拭目以俟
===
第二問
陳榛
同考試官教授區　批〔災異之說自古有之　而其要在於修省此作敷陳往事博洽無遺而〕
望我
皇上及相臣百執事交警感召之道尤惓惓焉眞有憂治危明之忠
著是宜錄
同考試官推官諸　批〔我〕
祖
punctuated:
主上當鼎盛之年，躬不世出之資，蓋謂順呼而高望之時，非歟？誠操軒皇以來心印，而研究躬行之，是堯、舜之主也；推此心以允升大猷，是黃、虞之世也；士生斯時而獲效用，是翼爲明聽之遇也；兆姓得沐浴于德化之成，是含哺擊壤之適也。若然，則不特赫然爲一代務學之明君，且將卓然爲萬世帝王之標準，是在聖明深加之意而已。愚也請拭目以俟。

第二問
陳榛
同考試官教授區　批：〔災異之說，自古有之，而其要在於修省。此作敷陳往事，博洽無遺，而望我皇上及相臣、百執事交警感召之道，尤惓惓焉，眞有憂治危明之忠。著是宜錄。〕
同考試官推官諸　批：〔我祖〕
translation_en:
…His Majesty is in the prime of his years and possesses natural endowments that appear but once in an epoch; is this not what is meant by a time of calling out with the wind and gazing from a height? If he truly grasps the mind-to-mind transmission handed down since the time of the Yellow Emperor, investigating it thoroughly and practicing it in person, he will be a sovereign like Yao and Shun. If he extends this mind to advance grand plans, this will be an age like those of the Yellow Emperor and Yu Shun. That scholars born in this time obtain the opportunity to render service is an encounter matching the assistance, action, clear sight, and keen hearing [spoken of in the Book of Documents]. That the myriad people are able to bathe in the completion of moral transformation is the contentment of eating their fill and drumming on the earth. If this be so, then he will not only shine forth as an enlightened ruler devoted to learning for a single generation, but will also stand preeminently as a standard for emperors and kings for ten thousand generations. This rests solely on His Sacred Brilliance giving deep heed to it. In my ignorance, I beg to wipe my eyes and wait expectantly.

Second Policy Question
Chen Zhen 陳榛
Associate Examiner, Confucian School Instructor Ou 區, comments: [Discussions of natural disasters and anomalies have existed since antiquity, and their essential point lies in self-cultivation and self-examination. This essay sets forth past events with broad learning and without omission, and in hoping that Our Sovereign, the grand secretaries, and all the officiating functionaries will mutually admonish one another in the way of moving Heaven and evoking auspicious responses, it is especially earnest—truly possessing the loyalty that worries in times of order and feels trepidation in times of enlightenment. For displaying this, it ought to be selected for inclusion.]
Associate Examiner, Prefectural Judge Zhu 諸, comments: [Our Ancestors…]

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
宗克蒞天戒恒惓惓於修德省躬我
皇上敬天之實後先相繼子能闡悉而尤切交警是抱忠愛之忱者
同考試官推官龍　批　談古今災異事甚悉
而修彌之論尤中肯綮非徒工於詞藝者
考試官右中允何　批　修德格天君道首務我
皇上敬天實心先于
祖
宗是作獨能發揚而尤以
上下交儆爲望殆貞懷忠以待舉者可錄以
===
獻矣
考試官左中允范　批　我
皇上畏天實意視我
皇祖
世宗後先一揆是作闡揚明悉而歸重于
君臣交儆忠愛之意藹然宜錄以
獻
執事以往者玄象示異致釐
主上之憂圖所以明感召之端而盡修弭之道
punctuated:
宗克蒞天戒，恒惓惓於修德省躬。我皇上敬天之實，後先相繼，子能闡悉，而尤切交警，是抱忠愛之忱者。
同考試官推官龍　批　談古今災異事甚悉，而修彌之論尤中肯綮，非徒工於詞藝者。
考試官右中允何　批　修德格天，君道首務。我皇上敬天實心，先于祖宗。是作獨能發揚，而尤以上下交儆爲望，殆貞懷忠以待舉者，可錄以獻矣。
考試官左中允范　批　我皇上畏天實意，視我皇祖、世宗後先一揆。是作闡揚明悉，而歸重于君臣交儆，忠愛之意藹然，宜錄以獻。
執事以往者玄象示異，致釐主上之憂，圖所以明感召之端，而盡修弭之道，
translation_en:
… [Our Imperial Ancestors] were able to respond to Heaven’s warnings, always earnestly devoting themselves to cultivating virtue and examining their own persons. In the substance of His reverence for Heaven, Our Emperor succeeds what came before; you are able to expound this thoroughly and are especially urgent regarding mutual admonition, showing yourself to be one who cherishes a sincere heart of loyalty and affection.
Associate Examiner Long, Prefectural Judge, comments: It discusses the affairs of calamities and portents past and present very thoroughly, and its argument on cultivation and averting disaster especially hits the crucial point; the author is not someone merely skilled in literary craft.
Examiner He, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent, comments: Cultivating virtue to move Heaven is the foremost duty of the ruler’s way. Our Emperor’s sincere heart in revering Heaven matches that of our Imperial Ancestors [? 先于祖宗: or “takes precedence even as did the Imperial Ancestors / follows the precedent of the Imperial Ancestors”]. This essay alone is able to set this forth clearly, and moreover places its hope especially in mutual admonition between ruler and ministers. Surely this is someone who steadfastly cherishes loyalty while awaiting selection; it may be recorded for presentation to the throne.
Examiner Fan, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent, comments: Our Emperor’s sincere intention in standing in awe of Heaven follows the exact same measure as Our Imperial Ancestor and Emperor Shizong, earlier and later as one. This essay expounds this clearly and thoroughly, while placing its ultimate emphasis on mutual admonition between ruler and ministers. Its spirit of loyalty and affection is abundant; it ought to be recorded for presentation to the throne.

Because in recent times the celestial phenomena have displayed anomalies, causing distress and concern to Our Sovereign, you, Sirs, seek to clarify the beginnings of moral response and resonance and to exhaust the way of cultivating virtue and averting disaster—…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
慮至深也顧愚生何足以知之夫天人相
與之際至難言也何也天道遠人道邇其
幾甚微非意想測度之所能及也和氣致
祥乖氣致戾其理甚著不待聖知而後能
辨也愚嘗博稽載籍諸家之說紛紛矣今
案事考變則有湛溺象數之譏指妄闢妖
則有蒙諱諱諛之失參稽往牒比物連引
則見以為述而無倫規切
主聽慮事廣肆則見以為迂而無當然則欲建
===
必然之畫而紓
當宁之憂必
君臣各任其責儻可少裨萬一乎易曰天垂象
見吉凶而震之象曰君子以恐懼修省夫
洊雷成象而君子慎之以此見君之所畏
者天而畏天即所以事天也書曰先王克
謹天戒而繼之曰臣人克有常憲百官修
輔夫聖王畏天而必資于臣下之輔以此
見君之所助者臣而同寅協恭以交修也
punctuated: 慮至深也。顧愚生何足以知之？夫天人相與之際，至難言也。何也？天道遠，人道邇，其幾甚微，非意想測度之所能及也；和氣致祥，乖氣致戾，其理甚著，不待聖知而後能辨也。愚嘗博稽載籍，諸家之說紛紛矣。今案事考變，則有湛溺象數之譏；指妄闢妖，則有蒙諱諱諛之失；參稽往牒，比物連引，則見以為述而無倫；規切主聽，慮事廣肆，則見以為迂而無當。然則欲建必然之畫，而紓當宁之憂，必君臣各任其責，儻可少裨萬一乎？《易》曰：「天垂象，見吉凶。」而〈震〉之《象》曰：「君子以恐懼修省。」夫洊雷成象而君子慎之，以此見君之所畏者天，而畏天即所以事天也。《書》曰：「先王克謹天戒。」而繼之曰：「臣人克有常憲，百官修輔。」夫聖王畏天，而必資于臣下之輔，以此見君之所助者臣，而同寅協恭以交修也。
translation_en: … [the examiners'] concern is most profound. Yet how is this foolish student sufficient to know of it? Now, the interaction between Heaven and human beings is most difficult to speak of. Why is this? The Way of Heaven is distant, while the Way of human beings is near; its subtle incipient signs are extremely minute, beyond what mere conjecture and calculation can reach. Harmonious qi brings about auspicious signs, while perverse qi brings about calamities; the principle of this is extremely manifest, and does not await sage wisdom before it can be discerned. I have examined the historical records broadly, and the theories of the various schools are manifold and confused. Today, if one examines specific events to investigate anomalies, one incurs the criticism of being mired in images and numerology; if one denounces them as falsehoods and dismisses portents, one commits the error of concealing faults and offering flattery [? 諱諛]; if one cross-references past documents and draws analogies by linking things together, one is regarded as merely recounting the past without coherent order; if one admonishes the Sovereign's hearing earnestly and deliberates on affairs broadly and unreservedly, one is regarded as impractical and wide of the mark. This being so, if we wish to establish a plan of certain efficacy and relieve the anxieties of the Throne, must not ruler and ministers each shoulder their respective responsibilities, so that it might perhaps be of some slight assistance in one part in ten thousand? The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "Heaven suspends images, manifesting good fortune and misfortune." And the Commentary on the Images (Xiang) for the hexagram Zhen ("Thunder") says: "The noble man in fear and trembling cultivates his virtue and examines his faults." Now, repeated thunder forms the image, and the noble man is cautious because of it; by this we see that what the ruler stands in awe of is Heaven, and standing in awe of Heaven is the very means of serving Heaven. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "The former kings were able to heed diligently the warnings of Heaven." And continuing this, it says: "The ministers and officials were able to uphold the constant laws, and the hundred officials cultivated their assistance." Now, the sage kings stood in awe of Heaven, yet necessarily relied upon the assistance of their ministers and subordinates; by this we see that those who aid the ruler are the ministers, and that with shared reverence and united respect they engage in mutual cultivation.

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
箕子陳洪範以五事配五行而推極于庶
徵之感應王與卿士師尹之交省豈不謂
天人一理即呼吸動靜皆有所關而不可
不謹者乎又豈不謂君臣一體即尊卑大
小若有不同而孰非當謹者乎孔子作春
秋書災異而不書事應然其上揆天道下
質人情亦欲使天下後世之爲人君爲人
臣者知天之所以譴告恐懼修省而已矣
若推其應而有合有不合將不視爲漠然
===
而無所用省耶噫夫子之意深矣歐陽修
曰災者被于物而可知水旱螟蝗之類是
已異者不可知其所以然者也日食星孛
之類是已此非修之言也董仲舒曰天心
仁愛人君故出災害以譴告之不知自省
又出恠異以警懼之然則有其異者尤加
謹焉可也漢儒言災異者亡慮十餘家京
房翼奉李尋之徒其言窮極災祥緣傳經
義博而寡要幻而無稽勿論已劉向激目
punctuated: 箕子陳《洪範》，以五事配五行，而推極于庶徵之感應、王與卿士師尹之交省。豈不謂天人一理，即呼吸動靜皆有所關，而不可不謹者乎？又豈不謂君臣一體，即尊卑大小若有不同，而孰非當謹者乎？孔子作《春秋》，書災異而不書事應，然其上揆天道，下質人情，亦欲使天下後世之爲人君、爲人臣者，知天之所以譴告，恐懼修省而已矣。若推其應而有合有不合，將不視爲漠然而無所用省耶？噫！夫子之意深矣。歐陽修曰：「災者，被于物而可知，水旱螟蝗之類是已；異者，不可知其所以然者也，日食星孛之類是已。」此非修之言也。董仲舒曰：「天心仁愛人君，故出災害以譴告之；不知自省，又出恠異以警懼之。」然則有其異者，尤加謹焉可也。漢儒言災異者亡慮十餘家，京房、翼奉、李尋之徒，其言窮極災祥，緣傳經義，博而寡要，幻而無稽，勿論已。劉向激目
translation_en:
When Jizi 箕子 set forth the "Great Plan" (Hongfan 洪範), he matched the five conducts with the Five Phases and carried this principle to its utmost in the sympathetic responses of the various verifications and the mutual self-examination of the king, the Ministers, and the Directors. Does this not mean that Heaven and humanity share a single principle, such that even a breath or a movement is connected to it, and one cannot fail to be cautious? And does it not also mean that ruler and minister form a single body, so that even though there appear to be differences between noble and humble, great and small, who among them ought not to be cautious? When Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋), he recorded calamities and anomalies without recording the specific events to which they responded. Yet in gauging the Way of Heaven above and testing against human sentiments below, he too merely wished to cause those in the world and in later generations who serve as rulers and ministers to understand why Heaven sends its reprimands and warnings, and simply stand in fearful awe to cultivate and examine themselves. If one were to deduce specific responses and find that some match while others do not, would people not come to regard them with indifference and see no need for self-examination? Ah, the Master's intention was profound indeed!

Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修 said: "Calamities are things that affect creatures and can be understood, such as floods, droughts, and plagues of snout-moths and locusts; anomalies are things whose causes cannot be understood, such as solar eclipses and comets." Yet these were not originally Ouyang Xiu's own words. Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 said: "The mind of Heaven benevolently loves the ruler of men, and therefore sends forth calamities and harm to reprimand and warn him; if he does not know to examine himself, it further sends forth strange anomalies to startle and frighten him." This being so, when such anomalies occur, one ought to be all the more cautious. Among the Han-dynasty scholars who discussed calamities and anomalies, there were roughly more than ten schools. Men of the ilk of Jing Fang 京房, Yi Feng 翼奉, and Li Xun 李尋 exhausted the extremes of calamities and auspicious signs in their discourse, grafting them onto commentaries on the meanings of the Classics; their words are broad yet lack essentials, illusory and unfounded, and need not be discussed. Liu Xiang 劉向, stirred by the sight of [?] …

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
時災繫心王室著爲洪範五行傳論奏之
天子雖其推迹行事連傳禍福牽附多端
瑕瑜莫掩然其規切時政感動君心一念
精忠世主見諒使當時能用其言未必不
轉災爲祥也乃蘇洵氏譏其五失鄭夾漈
指爲妖妄不已過乎後之儒者祖循其說
代有論著如所謂五行志天文考者其言
具在乃其占候之端類多舛合有其占者
如元封之星孛于河戍永平之慧出于天
===
船也無其應者如本始之熒惑守房初元
之客星犯斗也若天寶之五星聚箕尾非
所謂其德不稱而反以致亂者乎紹聖之
流星出壁室非所謂反常爲妖而謬以爲
祥者乎大抵導諛者謂天本無心而陳規
者謂天若有意謂天不足畏者王安石之
所以熒惑君心也謂旱爲餘烈者公孫子
之所以曲學阿世也魏相輔政輒白四方
異聞富鄭公雜著洪範春秋災異之故以
punctuated: 時災，繫心王室，著爲《洪範五行傳論》，奏之天子。雖其推迹行事，連傳禍福，牽附多端，瑕瑜莫掩；然其規切時政，感動君心，一念精忠，世主見諒，使當時能用其言，未必不轉災爲祥也。乃蘇洵氏譏其五失，鄭夾漈指爲妖妄，不已過乎？後之儒者，祖循其說，代有論著，如所謂《五行志》、《天文考》者，其言具在。乃其占候之端，類多舛合。有其占者，如元封之星孛于河戍，永平之慧出于天船也；無其應者，如本始之熒惑守房，初元之客星犯斗也。若天寶之五星聚箕、尾，非所謂其德不稱而反以致亂者乎？紹聖之流星出壁、室，非所謂反常爲妖而謬以爲祥者乎？大抵導諛者謂天本無心，而陳規者謂天若有意。謂天不足畏者，王安石之所以熒惑君心也；謂旱爲餘烈者，公孫子之所以曲學阿世也。魏相輔政，輒白四方異聞；富鄭公雜著《洪範》、《春秋》災異之故以
translation_en: … the disasters of the time and keeping his heart bound to the royal house, composed the Discourse on the Commentary on the Five Phases of the Great Plan (Hongfan wuxing zhuan lun) and presented it to the Son of Heaven. Although in tracing past deeds and linking them to good and bad fortune his forced correlations were manifold and their flaws and merits could not conceal one another, yet in earnestly admonishing contemporary governance and moving the ruler's heart, his single-minded pure loyalty was understood by the reigning sovereign; had his words been put to use at the time, disaster might well have been turned into auspiciousness. Yet when Su Xun 蘇洵 ridiculed him for "five failings" and Zheng Qiao 鄭樵 (Zheng Jiazhai 鄭夾漈) denounced his work as portentous delusion, was that not going too far? Later Confucian scholars followed his doctrines as a model, producing treatises in every age—such as the so-called Treatises on the Five Phases (Wuxing zhi) and Investigations of Celestial Patterns (Tianwen kao)—whose words remain intact. Yet the particulars of their prognostications are mostly a mix of misses and hits. Those whose prognostications held true include the comet appearing at the River Guard (Heshu) during the Yuanfeng reign (110–105 BCE), and the broom star [reading 彗 for 慧] emerging at the Celestial Boat (Tianchuan) during the Yongping reign (58–75 CE); those without corresponding fulfillment include Mars (Yinghuo) lingering in the Room (Fang) lodge during the Benshi reign (73–70 BCE), and the guest star trespassing against the Dipper (Dou) during the Chuyuan reign (48–44 BCE). As for the five planets gathering in the Winnowing-Basket (Ji) and Tail (Wei) lodges during the Tianbao reign (742–756), was this not what is called virtue not matching the portent and instead bringing about rebellion? And the meteor emerging from the Wall (Bi) and Encampment (Shi) lodges during the Shaosheng reign (1094–1098), was this not what is called an abnormality that is actually an ominous prodigy being mistakenly taken as an auspicious sign? In general, those who lead their ruler into flattery claim that Heaven originally has no mind, whereas those who present admonitions say that Heaven acts as if with intent. Claiming that "the portents of Heaven are not worth fearing" was how Wang Anshi 王安石 deluded his ruler's mind; claiming that drought was merely the "lingering blaze" [of sage virtue] was how Master Gongsun 公孫子 (Gongsun Hong 公孫弘) twisted his learning to pander to the age. When Wei Xiang 魏相 assisted in governance, he invariably reported strange occurrences from all quarters to the throne; Duke Zheng of Fu (Fu Bi 富弼) compiled the causes of disasters and prodigies from the Great Plan (Hongfan) and the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) in order to…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
爲鑑戒彼二人者皆所謂貞臣碩輔也而
猶若是然則有其變者曷可視爲適然而
漫不加省也哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝久在兵間熟知乾象七政紊常行
則下求言之
詔熒惑犯輿鬼則有中書之
勅觀其所謂殃咎在君惺惺無措省不覺之
過改故爲之愆者何其敬畏之深也
世宗肅皇帝應運
中興敬
===
天法
祖五星聚而
開誠以受樂頀之言妖星見而
虛懷以降星變之
勅觀其指陳禍福嘉納無遺文武臣工訓迪
甚備又何其敬畏之至也我
皇上君臨萬邦
新服厥命嚴恭寅畏克享
punctuated: 爲鑑戒。彼二人者，皆所謂貞臣碩輔也，而猶若是，然則有其變者，曷可視爲適然而漫不加省也哉！洪惟我太祖高皇帝久在兵間，熟知乾象。七政紊常行，則下求言之詔；熒惑犯輿鬼，則有中書之勅。觀其所謂「殃咎在君，惺惺無措，省不覺之過，改故爲之愆」者，何其敬畏之深也！世宗肅皇帝應運中興，敬天法祖。五星聚，而開誠以受樂頀之言；妖星見，而虛懷以降星變之勅。觀其指陳禍福，嘉納無遺，文武臣工，訓迪甚備，又何其敬畏之至也！我皇上君臨萬邦，新服厥命，嚴恭寅畏，克享
translation_en:
…serve as a mirror and a warning. Those two men were both what we call upright ministers and great chief councilors, and yet even they acted thus; when such anomalies occur, how then could one regard them as mere coincidence and carelessly fail to examine oneself!

Reflecting deeply upon our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, r. 1368–1398), he spent long years amidst military campaigns and was intimately familiar with celestial phenomena. When the Seven Regulators [sun, moon, and five planets] fell out of their regular courses, he issued an edict seeking直言 (frank counsel); when Mars (Yinghuo) encroached upon the Ghost (Yugui) constellation, he issued a command to the Secretariat (Zhongshu). When we consider his words—"The calamity and blame lie with the ruler; alert and anxious, I know not what to do, examining faults committed unawares and correcting transgressions done willfully"—how profound was his reverent awe!

The Epochal Exemplar, Emperor Su (Shizong, r. 1521–1567), responded to the turn of destiny by accomplishing a dynastic revival, revering Heaven and modeling himself on the Ancestors. When the five planets gathered in conjunction, he opened his heart in sincerity to accept the words of Yue Hu [樂頀]; when an ominous star appeared, he humbled himself to send down a command concerning the stellar anomaly. When we observe how he pointed out and set forth fortune and misfortune, approvingly accepting advice without omission, and how thoroughly he instructed and guided his civil and military officials, how supreme, too, was his reverent awe!

Our Emperor rules over the myriad states and has newly taken up His mandate; with stern reverence and respectful awe, He is able to satisfy…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
天心頃因客星見于壁宿之次赤光指于東北
之方我
皇上遇災而懼既以露禱于
宮庭親發
德音又
飭交修於臣下
畏天一念質諸
太祖
世宗爲有光矣然猶未能導迎善氣茂著休祥
雨澤或至于愆期災祲屢形于奏牘執事
===
謂
聖德已修而大小臣工未能奉行
德教所致是固然矣然豈可以專責之臣而
已哉明明在下赫赫在上言天人之機一
也惟聖時憲惟臣欽若言君臣之責均也
堯欽曆象而百工釐舜在璣衡而五辰撫
格皇天者在宅俊之登庸祈永命者由上
下之勤恤此位育參贊之能燮理寅亮之
punctuated: 天心。頃因客星見于壁宿之次，赤光指于東北之方，我皇上遇災而懼，既以露禱于宮庭，親發德音，又飭交修於臣下，畏天一念，質諸太祖、世宗，爲有光矣。然猶未能導迎善氣，茂著休祥，雨澤或至于愆期，災祲屢形于奏牘。執事謂聖德已修，而大小臣工未能奉行德教所致，是固然矣；然豈可以專責之臣而已哉？「明明在下，赫赫在上」，言天人之機一也；「惟聖時憲，惟臣欽若」，言君臣之責均也。堯欽曆象而百工釐，舜在璣衡而五辰撫，格皇天者在宅俊之登庸，祈永命者由上下之勤恤，此位育參贊之能、燮理寅亮之
translation_en: … the heart of Heaven. Recently, because a guest star appeared in the lunar mansion Bi, and a red glow pointed toward the northeast, Our August Emperor, encountering disaster, was filled with fear. Having prayed in the open courtyard of the palace, he personally issued a benevolent rescript and further admonished his officials below to engage in mutual self-cultivation. When this single thought of revering Heaven is measured against Grand Progenitor (Taizu) and Epochal Ancestor (Shizong), it adds luster to them. Yet it has still not been possible to usher in auspicious qi and abundantly manifest felicitous omens; timely rains sometimes fail to arrive on schedule, and calamities and ominous portents repeatedly appear in memorialized reports. Your Excellency states that this is because Although Sacred Virtue has already been cultivated, officials great and small have failed to carry out his virtuous teachings. This is certainly so; yet how could the blame be placed solely upon the ministers and leave it at that? "Bright and clear below, awe-inspiring on high"—this means that the subtle mechanism linking Heaven and man is one. "Only the sage takes this as his model; only the ministers reverently accord with him"—this means that the responsibilities of ruler and minister are shared alike. When Yao reverently calculated the calendrical phenomena, the hundred officials were well regulated; when Shun examined the jade-adorned astronomical instruments, the five seasonal divisions were harmoniously ordered. Reaching August Heaven lies in promoting and employing men of outstanding talent in office; praying for an enduring mandate depends upon diligent solicitude from both above and below. This is the capacity to establish order, foster nourishment, and assist in the transforming work of Heaven and Earth, and the [way] of harmonizing, regulating, and reverently illuminating …

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
道也而執事欲詢今日感召之端以為我
皇上格天之助則愚將何辭以對乎竊以為人
君所居者天位所治者天民而臣也者承
君命以代天工佐元后以事上帝者也
天心示警適
聖皇臨御之初而
主德靡寧正臣工兢惕之日是故
君省于上不必下詔罪已如建始停樂減膳如
貞觀避殿露禱如熈寧也思
===
天心之仁愛既形則顧民情之岀險可畏念
皇天之付托甚重則思
元子之責任惟艱
耳目所用必自省曰果能憲天之聰明乎
命令所宣必自省曰果能代天之綸綍乎
乾剛所運必自省曰果能奉天之明畏乎
衷衷所發必自省曰果能勑天之時幾乎天有
敘秩懼吾之惇庸者或有未至也天有命
討懼吾之賞罰者或有未公也輔弼之臣
punctuated: 道也。而執事欲詢今日感召之端，以為我皇上格天之助，則愚將何辭以對乎？竊以為人君所居者天位，所治者天民，而臣也者，承君命以代天工、佐元后以事上帝者也。天心示警，適聖皇臨御之初；而主德靡寧，正臣工兢惕之日。是故君省于上，不必下詔罪已如建始，停樂減膳如貞觀，避殿露禱如熈寧也。思天心之仁愛既形，則顧民情之岀險可畏；念皇天之付托甚重，則思元子之責任惟艱。耳目所用，必自省曰：「果能憲天之聰明乎？」命令所宣，必自省曰：「果能代天之綸綍乎？」乾剛所運，必自省曰：「果能奉天之明畏乎？」衷衷所發，必自省曰：「果能勑天之時幾乎？」天有敘秩，懼吾之惇庸者或有未至也；天有命討，懼吾之賞罰者或有未公也。輔弼之臣，
translation_en:
…way. Now that you, sir, wish to inquire into the causes of the responses and portents of the present day as an aid to our Emperor in moving Heaven, with what words shall I, ignorant as I am, reply?

I venture to hold that the position a ruler occupies is Heaven's position, and the people he governs are Heaven's people; whereas ministers are those who receive the ruler's commands to perform Heaven's work in its stead, and who assist the great sovereign in serving the Lord on High. That the mind of Heaven displays warnings happens right at the beginning of the Sacred Emperor's reign; and when the sovereign's virtue knows no rest, it is precisely the day for ministers and officials to be tremblingly vigilant.

Therefore, when the ruler examines himself above, he need not issue edicts blaming himself as in the Jianshi era (32–29 BCE), suspend music and reduce palace meals as in the Zhenguan era (627–649), or vacate the main hall and pray in the open air as in the Xining era (1068–1077). Reflecting that the benevolent love of Heaven's mind has already manifested itself, he looks upon the perils of the people's condition [?] as something to be feared; mindful that the charge entrusted by August Heaven is exceedingly heavy, he reflects that the responsibility of the First Son of Heaven is truly arduous.

In using his ears and eyes, he must examine himself and say: "Am I truly able to model myself on Heaven's acute hearing and clear sight?" In proclaiming orders and commands, he must examine himself and say: "Am I truly able to speak on behalf of Heaven's silken cords of decree?" In exercising the firm vigor of the sovereign power, he must examine himself and say: "Am I truly able to uphold Heaven's discernment and awe?" In what issues forth from his innermost heart [?], he must examine himself and say: "Am I truly able to attend cautiously to Heaven's timely and subtle springs of action?"

Heaven has its social order and five relations, and he fears lest his own generous observance of them may in some way fall short; Heaven has its mandate for the virtuous and punishment for the guilty, and he fears lest his own rewards and punishments may in some way fail to be impartial. Ministers who assist and counsel…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
稽謀自天者也
召對之典可弗常歟諫諍之臣迪知天威者
也逆耳之言可弗受歟近習之蔽上干天
和者也佞倖之門可弗塞歟而又
端好尚以合天心
防壅蔽以廣天聽
愼威儀以定天則
辯忠邪以昭天監
恤民隱以霈天澤
飭邊圉以固天險至于
深宮獨行之中常若上帝之臨汝服食居處
之際恒如日監之在兹必如是而後
天心降鑒既形之變猶可弭而將來之患可無
君德罔愆
天心降鑒既形之變猶可弭而將來之患可無
===
君德罔愆
萌矣
上之所以自修者豈外是道耶臣竊於下不必
㨗攄規議如京房攻訐王過如谷永連引
禍福如更生也知偶王之在宣而兢兢乎
punctuated: 稽謀自天者也，召對之典可弗常歟？諫諍之臣，迪知天威者也，逆耳之言可弗受歟？近習之蔽，上干天和者也，佞倖之門可弗塞歟？而又端好尚以合天心，防壅蔽以廣天聽，愼威儀以定天則，辯忠邪以昭天監，恤民隱以霈天澤，飭邊圉以固天險。至于深宮獨行之中，常若上帝之臨汝；服食居處之際，恒如日監之在兹。必如是，而後天心降鑒，既形之變猶可弭，而將來之患可無；君德罔愆，天心降鑒，既形之變猶可弭，而將來之患可無，君德罔愆，萌矣。上之所以自修者，豈外是道耶？臣竊於下，不必㨗攄規議如京房，攻訐王過如谷永，連引禍福如更生也。知偶王之在宣，而兢兢乎
translation_en: …are those who examine counsels derived from Heaven; can the practice of summoning them for audiences not be made regular? Remonstrating officials are those who comprehend and know the majesty of Heaven; can words unpleasant to the ear not be accepted? The obfuscations of close attendants offend the harmony of Heaven above; can the gate of flatterers and favorites not be blocked? Furthermore, he should rectify his preferences to accord with the mind of Heaven, guard against obstruction and concealment to broaden the hearing of Heaven, be cautious in his dignified demeanor to establish the norms of Heaven, distinguish loyalty from wickedness to manifest the scrutiny of Heaven, show compassion for the hidden sufferings of the people to shower down the grace of Heaven, and put the frontier defenses in order to secure the natural barriers of Heaven. Even when walking alone in the deep palace, he should always feel as if the Lord on High were looking down upon him; in matters of dress, food, and daily residence, he should constantly act as if Heaven's daily inspection were right here. Only when it is necessarily like this will the sovereign's virtue be without fault and the mind of Heaven look down in scrutiny, so that anomalies already manifested may still be dispelled and future calamities may not sprout [?; transcription repeats "the mind of Heaven looks down in scrutiny, anomalies already manifested may still be dispelled and future calamities may not" and "the sovereign's virtue is without fault"]. How could the way by which the sovereign cultivates himself lie outside of this path? As for those below, I venture to think that they need not hastily pour forth admonitory proposals like Jing Fang 京房, attack and expose the sovereign's faults like Gu Yong 谷永, or string together citations of fortune and misfortune like Liu Gengsheng 劉更生 [Liu Xiang 劉向]. Knowing that serving as companions to the king lies in proclaiming his virtue, they should cautiously…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
分猷念以相從懼天命之難諶而慄慄乎
秉德意以明恤三公以論道爲責則思己
之贊襄
寀勿者何以調燮爕伏乎六卿以若時爲治
則思己之分職率屬者何以撫辰凝績乎
庶官以服采爲職則思己之靖共有位者
何以寅亮天工乎臺諫之臣誠務匡弼所
以格
君亦所以消禝也司牧之臣誠務輯寧所以宣
===
化亦所以導和也封疆之臣誠務安攘所
以建威亦所以銷萌也而又心無隱忠事
不避難身無擇便義無私交不順比滑澤
以阿
王之好也不納權廋惡以蔽
王之聰也不巽蝡觀望以弊
王之行也不衒直沽名以揚
主之過也虛心以待令隨事以納規
上答之不敢以疑
punctuated: 分猷念以相從；懼天命之難諶，而慄慄乎秉德意以明恤。三公以論道爲責，則思己之贊襄寀勿者，何以調燮爕伏乎？六卿以若時爲治，則思己之分職率屬者，何以撫辰凝績乎？庶官以服采爲職，則思己之靖共有位者，何以寅亮天工乎？臺諫之臣誠務匡弼，所以格君，亦所以消禝也；司牧之臣誠務輯寧，所以宣化，亦所以導和也；封疆之臣誠務安攘，所以建威，亦所以銷萌也。而又心無隱忠，事不避難，身無擇便，義無私交；不順比滑澤以阿王之好也，不納權廋惡以蔽王之聰也，不巽蝡觀望以弊王之行也，不衒直沽名以揚主之過也。虛心以待令，隨事以納規；上答之，不敢以疑，
translation_en: …share in His plans and thoughts so as to follow along with Him; and, fearing that the Mandate of Heaven is hard to rely upon, trembles in upholding His virtuous intentions so as to show clear compassion. The Three Dukes take discussing the Way as their responsibility, and thus reflect on how they, who assist in the diligent work of governance, are to harmonize yin and yang and calm hidden anomalies [?]. The Six Ministers take conforming to the seasons as their governance, and thus reflect on how they, who divide duties and lead their subordinates, are to accord with the fivechen seasons and consolidate achievements. The manifold officials take performing their assigned affairs as their duty, and thus reflect on how they, who quietly and reverently hold their posts, are to respectfully assist in Heaven's work. If the Censorial and Remonstrance officials truly devote themselves to rectification and assistance, this is the means to correct the ruler and also the means to dispel ominous vapors; if the territorial administrators truly devote themselves to pacifying and comforting the people, this is the means to propagate moral transformation and also the means to usher in harmony; if the frontier officials truly devote themselves to internal security and repelling external threats, this is the means to establish prestige and also the means to nip incipient troubles in the bud. Furthermore, let their hearts harbor no withheld loyalty, their actions avoid no difficulty, their persons seek no self-serving convenience, and their sense of duty allow no private cliques; let them not be compliant, partisan, and slickly ingratiating in order to pander to the King's preferences; let them not seize power [?] or conceal evils in order to befuddle the King's hearing; let them not be timid, irresolute, and watchful from the sidelines in order to impair the King's actions; let them not flaunt uprightness and fish for fame in order to broadcast the Sovereign's faults. With open minds they await orders, and as matters arise they offer admonition; when the Sovereign responds to them, they dare not be suspicious; …

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
上不答不敢以調翼翼乎勉吾
君以畏天之實政而吾亦事
君如事天焉必如是而後臣
主同德泰道以交人事之旣盡而天意有可回
矣臣之交修于下者豈外是道耶夫
君能自修是格天之本也然必下有謇諤之臣
而後能剔釁孽之萌始臣能交修是格天
之助也然必
上有兢業之君而後能延郄慮之長策故諮兩
鑒夏蓋臣之所以靖獻也旅議庶謗明主
之所以廣達也方今
主聖臣賢厲精化理所以覩事于無見而弭變
于未萌者當必有道矣愚生何足以知之
姑以復執事之問云爾
第三問
王堯封
同考試官學正黃　批〔古今吏治臧否條答〕
甚悉而經畫切當又皆有裨於實用者殆可采
punctuated:
上不答不敢以調。翼翼乎勉吾君以畏天之實政，而吾亦事君如事天焉。必如是而後臣主同德，泰道以交，人事之旣盡，而天意有可回矣。臣之交修于下者，豈外是道耶？夫君能自修，是格天之本也；然必下有謇諤之臣，而後能剔釁孽之萌始。臣能交修，是格天之助也；然必上有兢業之君，而後能延郄慮之長策。故諮兩鑒夏，蓋臣之所以靖獻也；旅議庶謗，明主之所以廣達也。方今主聖臣賢，厲精化理，所以覩事于無見而弭變于未萌者，當必有道矣。愚生何足以知之，姑以復執事之問云爾。

第三問
王堯封
同考試官學正黃　批〔古今吏治臧否條答〕甚悉而經畫切當又皆有裨於實用者殆可采
translation_en:
… and when the Sovereign does not respond, he does not dare to resort to flattery [?]. Reverently and cautiously he urges his ruler to practice actual governance rooted in awe of Heaven, while he himself serves his ruler just as he serves Heaven. Only when it is like this will minister and Sovereign share the same virtue, the Way of Peace (Tai) prevail through mutual communion, human affairs be fully exhausted, and the will of Heaven be turned back. Could the way by which ministers mutually cultivate themselves below lie outside of this? Now, that the ruler is able to cultivate himself is the foundation for moving Heaven; yet there must first be outspoken and honest ministers below before the earliest buds of crises and calamities can be rooted out. That ministers are able to join in mutual cultivation is an aid to moving Heaven; yet there must first be a cautious and diligent ruler above before far-sighted plans of deep concern [?] can be invited. Therefore, consulting the two [dynasties] and taking the Xia as a mirror [?] is how a minister loyally offers his counsel; welcoming the deliberations of the multitude and the criticisms of commoners is how an enlightened ruler broadens his understanding. At present, the Sovereign is sagely and the ministers are worthy, devoting their energies to transformative governance; there must surely be a way by which they perceive affairs before they become visible and quell upheavals before they sprout. How could I, a foolish student, be sufficient to know it? I merely offer this in reply to Your Excellency's question.

Question Three
Wang Yaofeng 
Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Huang comments: [His point-by-point responses on the merits and defects of administrative governance past and present] are extremely thorough, and his proposed measures are pertinent, appropriate, and all beneficial for practical application; they could well be adopted…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而行之矣
同考試官教授孫　批〔陳吏治者若久任等法談之熟矣乃籌度精確超於常談之外而可〕
〔飭官常可裨民瘼者孰與此篇是宜錄〕
考試官右中允何　批〔條答吏治洿隆鑿鑿有據而歸本綜覈明悉確當是識時務者〕
考試官左中允范　批〔談說吏治人人能矣至効實則難焉是策持論甚確而區畫鑿鑿可行殆〕
〔留心民瘼而有槩于中者邪宜錄以備采擇〕
===
善理民者明乎設官之意而後無負乎司
牧之責善審官者取其爲民之實而後可
責乎吏治之成夫設官凡以爲民也人臣
自一命以上孰不有承君治民之責而惟
守令之職最爲親民然於民爲近於君爲
遠也苟任職者徒以其自遠于君也遑遑
焉一心以爲民而又一心以媚上則其澤
必有所壅閼而不流主爵者不思其爲民
以設也屑屑焉拘之以文法而亂之以譽
punctuated:
而行之矣。
同考試官教授孫　批〔陳吏治者，若久任等法，談之熟矣。乃籌度精確，超於常談之外，而可〕〔飭官常、可裨民瘼者，孰與此篇？是宜錄。〕
考試官右中允何　批〔條答吏治洿隆，鑿鑿有據，而歸本綜覈，明悉確當，是識時務者。〕
考試官左中允范　批〔談說吏治，人人能矣，至効實則難焉。是策持論甚確，而區畫鑿鑿可行，殆〕〔留心民瘼，而有槩于中者邪！宜錄以備采擇。〕

善理民者，明乎設官之意，而後無負乎司牧之責；善審官者，取其爲民之實，而後可責乎吏治之成。夫設官凡以爲民也。人臣自一命以上，孰不有承君治民之責？而惟守令之職最爲親民。然於民爲近，於君爲遠也。苟任職者徒以其自遠于君也，遑遑焉一心以爲民，而又一心以媚上，則其澤必有所壅閼而不流；主爵者不思其爲民以設也，屑屑焉拘之以文法，而亂之以譽…
translation_en:
…and put into practice.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Sun comments: "Those who set forth accounts of administrative governance have discussed methods such as extended tenure until they are thoroughly familiar. Yet when it comes to precise and accurate planning that transcends commonplace talk, and that can rectify official standards and remedy the sufferings of the people, what can compare with this essay? It ought to be recorded."
Examiner and Right Companion to the Heir Apparent He comments: "Its point-by-point responses regarding the decline and flourishing of administrative governance are well-founded with solid evidence, and its return to the fundamental issue of comprehensive verification is clear, thorough, and apt. This is someone who understands current affairs."
Examiner and Left Companion to the Heir Apparent Fan comments: "Everyone is capable of talking about administrative governance, but achieving practical results is difficult. This policy essay holds to very sound arguments, and its proposed measures are concrete and practicable. Is this not someone who pays close attention to the sufferings of the people and possesses deep conviction within? It should be recorded and prepared for selection."

Those who are good at governing the people understand the purpose for which offices are established, and only then do they not fail in their responsibility as shepherds of the people; those who are good at evaluating officials look for their actual substance in serving the people, and only then can they demand the perfection of administrative governance. Now, offices are established altogether for the sake of the people. Among subjects who hold even the lowest official rank and above, who does not bear the responsibility of serving the ruler and governing the people? Yet the post of Prefect or Magistrate is the closest of all to the people. However, while they are close to the people, they are far from the ruler. If those who hold such posts, merely because they find themselves far from the ruler, anxiously devote half their mind to serving the people while devoting the other half to flattering their superiors, then the ruler's beneficence will inevitably be obstructed and fail to flow downward. And if those in charge of personnel appointments do not reflect on the fact that offices are established for the sake of the people, and pettily bind officials with legalistic regulations while confusing them with praise and…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
毀則其情必有所隔閡而難盡澤壅則王
德不宣情隔則臣工懈體何惑乎民生日
瘁治效罔聞終無以復隆古之盛哉是故
選用循良推心委任秉實而不秉名者作
新吏治之要術也謹身帥先居以廉平不
嚴而民從化者德讓君子之遺風也明乎
此而郡邑著綏柔之績海㝢有寧謐之休
唐虞三代之治不難致矣何論兩漢哉愚
嘗俯仰今昔見守令之所關重矣自京師
===
達于方外郡有守縣有令凡四方之甲兵
錢穀夷險要害吏弊民隱營建徵發天子
宰相之所度地而居民者守令之所得相
宜而從事者也凡一方之所以興賢褒善
均賦平刑崇祀恤煢宣幽達滯監司制使
之所糾正而參决者守令之所得控制而
罷行者也朝而議政夕下於民矣夕而申
令不俟終朝矣漢宣帝曰使庶民安其田
里而亡嘆息怨恨之心者其惟良二千石
punctuated:
毀，則其情必有所隔閡而難盡。澤壅則王德不宣，情隔則臣工懈體，何惑乎民生日瘁、治效罔聞，終無以復隆古之盛哉？是故選用循良，推心委任，秉實而不秉名者，作新吏治之要術也；謹身帥先，居以廉平，不嚴而民從化者，德讓君子之遺風也。明乎此，而郡邑著綏柔之績，海㝢有寧謐之休，唐虞三代之治不難致矣，何論兩漢哉！
愚嘗俯仰今昔，見守令之所關重矣。自京師達于方外，郡有守，縣有令。凡四方之甲兵、錢穀、夷險、要害、吏弊、民隱、營建、徵發，天子、宰相之所度地而居民者，守令之所得相宜而從事者也；凡一方之所以興賢、褒善、均賦、平刑、崇祀、恤煢、宣幽、達滯，監司、制使之所糾正而參决者，守令之所得控制而罷行者也。朝而議政，夕下於民矣；夕而申令，不俟終朝矣。漢宣帝曰：「使庶民安其田里，而亡嘆息怨恨之心者，其惟良二千石
translation_en:
…and slander, then their true circumstances will inevitably be obstructed by barriers and difficult to express fully. When beneficence is blocked, the Sovereign's virtue is not proclaimed; when true circumstances are cut off, the officials grow lax in their duties. What wonder is it, then, that the people's livelihood grows daily more distressed, that the results of good governance are nowhere heard of, and that in the end there is no way to restore the flourishing of high antiquity? Therefore, selecting and employing upright and capable officials, entrusting them wholeheartedly with responsibilities, and holding to reality rather than mere reputation—this is the essential art of renewing official administration. Conducting oneself with care so as to lead by example, dwelling in integrity and fairness, and bringing the people to follow and be transformed without harshness—this is the bequeathed manner of the noble man of virtue and deference. Once one is clear about this, prefectures and districts will manifest achievements in pacifying and comforting the people, the realm within the seas will enjoy the blessing of peace and tranquility, and the governance of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties will not be difficult to attain—what need is there even to speak of the Two Han dynasties!
I have reflected on the present and the past, and have seen how vital is the role of prefects and magistrates. From the capital out to the distant regions, prefectures have their prefects and districts have their magistrates. In all the four quarters—whether matters of troops and armor, money and grain, level or險 [rugged] terrain and strategic chokepoints, clerical abuses and the hidden sufferings of the people, construction works and requisitions or levies—everything by which the Son of Heaven and the Grand Councilor measure out the land and settle the populace is what prefects and magistrates are able to manage according to local suitability. And within any given region—the means of promoting the worthy and commending the good, equalizing taxes and making punishments fair, honoring the sacrifices and showing compassion to the solitary and helpless, bringing light to the obscure and clearing away what is stagnated—everything that Regional Supervisors and Imperial Commissioners rectify and deliberate upon to decide is what prefects and magistrates are able to regulate, abolish, or put into practice. When a policy is deliberated upon in the morning, by evening it reaches down to the people; when an order is promulgated in the evening, it does not wait until the end of the next morning to take effect. Emperor Xuan of Han said: "To cause the common people to dwell peacefully in their fields and villages, without sighs or resentful hearts—is this not achieved solely by good two-thousand-bushel officials…?"

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
平漢明帝曰郎官出宰百里苟非其人民
受其殃言守令之甚重也後世吏網日密
人情輕外至有羨內徙若登僊視守官如
傳舍者此其故不知守令之重爾三代而
降惟漢世重良吏故其時得人爲多愚嘗
讀班固循吏傳如蜀守文翁而下凡六人
史稱其所居民富所去見思吏治之盛于
西漢者夫固班班可攷也若王尊薛宣皆
所謂身兼數器具謀王斷國之材者也而
===
固獨遺之尊嘗爲京兆矣又嘗守東郡矣
觀其拊循貧弱鉏鋤豪强盡節勞心夙夜
畏職見于公乘興之所訟述者其精敏何
如也河溢金堤老弱奔走身當水衝以安
衆志至爲吏民之所嘉壯者其勇節何如
也宣之守臨淮也教化大行徙陳留也盜
賊禁止矣及其入爲馮翊也高陵令陽湛
櫟陽令謝游故所稱貪滑不遜者也宣始
視事而兩人者輒解印綬以去頻陽令薛
punctuated: 平？漢明帝曰：「郎官出宰百里，苟非其人，民受其殃。」言守令之甚重也。後世吏網日密，人情輕外，至有羨內徙若登僊，視守官如傳舍者，此其故不知守令之重爾。三代而降，惟漢世重良吏，故其時得人爲多。愚嘗讀班固《循吏傳》，如蜀守文翁而下凡六人，史稱其「所居民富，所去見思」，吏治之盛于西漢者，夫固班班可攷也。若王尊、薛宣，皆所謂身兼數器，具謀王斷國之材者也，而固獨遺之。尊嘗爲京兆矣，又嘗守東郡矣。觀其拊循貧弱，鉏鋤豪强，盡節勞心，夙夜畏職，見于公乘興之所訟述者，其精敏何如也！河溢金堤，老弱奔走，身當水衝，以安衆志，至爲吏民之所嘉壯者，其勇節何如也！宣之守臨淮也，教化大行；徙陳留也，盜賊禁止矣。及其入爲馮翊也，高陵令陽湛、櫟陽令謝游，故所稱貪滑不遜者也，宣始視事，而兩人者輒解印綬以去；頻陽令薛
translation_en: … [良二千石乎/平?]!” Emperor Ming of Han said: “Court Gentlemen go out to govern a hundred li; if they are not the right men, the people suffer the calamity of it.” This speaks to the extreme importance of prefects and magistrates. In later ages, the net of bureaucratic regulations grew daily tighter, and human sentiment came to slight provincial posts, to the point where some envied a transfer to the inner court as though ascending to immortality, and regarded holding a provincial office as a mere coaching inn. The reason for this is simply that they did not understand the importance of prefects and magistrates. From the Three Dynasties onward, only the Han era valued good officials, and thus that period succeeded in obtaining the most men of talent. I have read Ban Gu’s “Biographies of Upright Officials” (Xunli zhuan): from Wen Weng, Governor of Shu, on down, there were six men in all. The history praises them by saying, “where they resided, the people grew rich; when they departed, they were fondly remembered.” That the administration of officials flourished in the Western Han can indeed be clearly examined in detail. As for men like Wang Zun and Xue Xuan, both were what was called “combining several capabilities in a single person, possessing the talent to counsel a king and make decisions for the state,” yet Ban Gu alone omitted them. Wang Zun once served as Governor of the Capital (Jingzhao), and also served as Governor of Dong Commandery. Looking at how he comforted the poor and weak, rooted out the powerful and overbearing, exhausted his loyalty and labored his mind, and revered his duties from morning to night, as seen in the defense and account submitted by Gongcheng Xing—how astute and diligent he was! When the Yellow River overflowed the Jindi embankment and the old and weak fled in panic, he personally stood at the brunt of the waters to calm the minds of the multitude, to the point where subofficial functionaries and the common people praised his valor—how brave and principled he was! When Xue Xuan was Governor of Linhuai, moral transformation was greatly carried out; when he was transferred to Chenliu, bandits and thieves were suppressed. And when he entered the capital region to become Governor of Fengyi, the Magistrate of Gaoling, Yang Zhan, and the Magistrate of Yueyang, Xie You, were men previously known as greedy, cunning, and insubordinate; no sooner had Xuan begun attending to business than both men untied their seal-ribbons and departed. The Magistrate of Pinyang, Xue …

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
恭粟邑令尹賞彼二人材指互異也宣一
奏吏不數月而兩邑皆治夫以二子之表
見若此而不得與六人者並傳則是固之
所錄未盡也又嘗讀范曄循吏傳如衛颯
任延而下凡十二人史稱其居官如家視
民如子吏治之盛于東漢者夫亦彷彿西
京也若吳祐延篤魯恭廉范之徒要皆負
器宏遠有牧民御衆之材者也而曄獨遺
之祐之相膠東也政先仁簡篤之尹京兆
===
也政用寬仁一則民有爭隙閉閤訟思一
則擢用長者與參政理卒之怨訟息而三
輔平則二子之居官可紀也宰中牟而表
三異者恭之察舉于肥親也守成都而歌
五絝者民之見懷乎叔度也一則螟不犯
境馴雉應而豎子興仁一則聽民夜作厲
禁削而百姓爲便觀其因俗制宜均足感
人而動物則廉魯之政績何如也夫以數
子之治效若此而不獲與颯延等並稱則
punctuated: 恭、粟邑令尹賞，彼二人材指互異也，宣一奏吏，不數月而兩邑皆治。夫以二子之表見若此，而不得與六人者並傳，則是固之所錄未盡也。又嘗讀范曄《循吏傳》，如衛颯、任延而下凡十二人，史稱其居官如家，視民如子，吏治之盛于東漢者，夫亦彷彿西京也。若吳祐、延篤、魯恭、廉范之徒，要皆負器宏遠，有牧民御衆之材者也，而曄獨遺之。祐之相膠東也，政先仁簡；篤之尹京兆也，政用寬仁。一則民有爭隙，閉閤訟思；一則擢用長者，與參政理。卒之怨訟息而三輔平，則二子之居官可紀也。宰中牟而表三異者，恭之察舉于肥親也；守成都而歌五絝者，民之見懷乎叔度也。一則螟不犯境，馴雉應而豎子興仁；一則聽民夜作，厲禁削而百姓爲便。觀其因俗制宜，均足感人而動物，則廉、魯之政績何如也？夫以數子之治效若此，而不獲與颯、延等並稱，則
translation_en:
… Gong and the Magistrate of Suyi, Yin Shang 尹賞—those two men differed from one another in talent and disposition, yet once Xuan memorialized to have them exchange posts, within a few months both counties were well governed. Now, given that the manifest achievements of these two gentlemen [Wang Zun 王尊 and Xue Xuan 薛宣] were such as this, yet they were not included alongside those six men in the collective biography, what [Ban] Gu 班固 recorded was incomplete.

I have also read Fan Ye's 范曄 "Biographies of Upright Officials" (Xunli zhuan 循吏傳), which includes twelve men in all, from Wei Sa 衛颯 and Ren Yan 任延 onward. The history praises them for treating their offices like their own homes and regarding the common people as their own children; the flourishing of official governance in the Eastern Han thus closely resembled that of the Western Capital [Western Han]. Yet men of the ilk of Wu You 吳祐, Yan Du 延篤, Lu Gong 魯恭, and Lian Fan 廉范 all possessed broad and far-reaching capacities and had the talent to shepherd the people and govern the multitude, and still [Fan] Ye alone left them out. When You served as Chancellor of Jiaodong, his administration put benevolence and simplicity first; when Du served as Governor of Jingzhao, his administration employed leniency and benevolence. In the one case, when the people had disputes and rifts, he would close his chamber doors to reflect on his own faults; in the other, he promoted and employed virtuous elders to participate in the governance. In the end, grievances and lawsuits ceased and the Three Metropolitan Areas (Sanfu 三輔) were pacified—thus the official careers of these two gentlemen are worthy of being recorded. Governing Zhongmou as Magistrate and manifesting the "three marvels" was what led Gong to be observed and recommended by Fei Qin 肥親; serving as Grand Administrator in Chengdu and inspiring the song of the "five pairs of trousers" was how the people cherished Shudu 叔度 [Lian Fan]. In the one case, crop-eating insects did not cross the borders, pheasants grew tame in response, and even a young boy was moved to benevolence; in the other, he permitted the people to work by candlelight at night, abolishing harsh prohibitions to the convenience of the common folk. Observing how they adapted their measures to local customs, both were equally capable of moving people and touching creatures—what, then, can be said of the administrative achievements of Lian and Lu? Now, given that the administrative efficacy of these several gentlemen was such as this, yet they did not get to be praised alongside Sa, Yan, and the others, …

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
是曄之所采未當也蓋古人之所謂循吏
者與俗吏異要皆被服道德明習世務緣
經飾吏體立而致用不偏奉職循理身修
而諸務不亂非徒敢悍精敏表異見奇如
世所稱一切辨給之能可同語也王尊薛
宣皆起佐史躋卿執所在而治爲世吏師
斯足奇者然皆以苛察失名視道德齊禮
之化何相懸也然則固之傳循吏而不及
二子也豈無見耶延吳廉魯皆本世儒富
===
經術殊聞顯迹有可稱談斯足尚者然或
陰蹷趙張故智視鳴琴不下堂之治又何
殊也然則曄之傳循吏而不及四子也豈
無謂耶王成以僞增戶口蒙顯賞無論已
乃若力行教化如黃覇而不免于張敞之
詆譏是使寬和愛利之政不見于天下也
漢宣以操切過制淆名實無論已乃若表
用循良如建武而猶病其吏治之刻深是
使綜覈厲精之治罔顯于後世也通乎此
punctuated: 是曄之所采未當也。蓋古人之所謂循吏者，與俗吏異，要皆被服道德，明習世務，緣經飾吏，體立而致用不偏；奉職循理，身修而諸務不亂。非徒敢悍精敏、表異見奇，如世所稱一切辨給之能，可同語也。王尊、薛宣皆起佐史，躋卿執，所在而治，爲世吏師，斯足奇者；然皆以苛察失名，視道德齊禮之化，何相懸也？然則固之傳循吏而不及二子也，豈無見耶？延、吳、廉、魯皆本世儒，富經術，殊聞顯迹，有可稱談，斯足尚者；然或陰蹷趙、張故智，視鳴琴不下堂之治，又何殊也？然則曄之傳循吏而不及四子也，豈無謂耶？王成以僞增戶口蒙顯賞，無論已；乃若力行教化如黃覇，而不免于張敞之詆譏，是使寬和愛利之政，不見于天下也。漢宣以操切過制淆名實，無論已；乃若表用循良如建武，而猶病其吏治之刻深，是使綜覈厲精之治，罔顯于後世也。通乎此，
translation_en: …this shows that Fan Ye’s 范曄 selection was not wholly fitting. Now, those whom the ancients called upright officials (xunli 循吏) differed from vulgar functionaries. In essence, they all clothed themselves in the Way and its Virtue and were well-versed in the affairs of the world; drawing upon the Classics to adorn their administration, they established the fundamental substance so that its practical application was never one-sided; discharging their duties in accordance with principle, they cultivated their persons so that the myriad affairs never fell into disorder. They cannot be spoken of in the same breath as those who are merely bold, fierce, shrewd, and nimble, displaying novelties and seeking to appear extraordinary—possessing what the world calls a purely expedient talent for brisk competence. Wang Zun 王尊 and Xue Xuan 薛宣 both rose from minor clerical posts to reach the ranks of the Nine Ministers and chief executives; wherever they served, order prevailed, and they became models for the officials of their age. This was certainly remarkable; yet both lost their good reputation through harshness and nitpicking scrutiny. Compared to transformation through leading by virtue and regulating by ritual, how far apart they were! This being so, when Ban Gu 班固 composed his biographies of upright officials and did not include these two men, how could it have been without insight?
