Yan篤 [Yan Du 延篤, or Diwu Lun 第五倫?—here "Yan" 延], Wu祐 [Wu You 吳祐], Lian范 [Lian Fan 廉范], and Lu恭 [Lu Gong 魯恭] were all rooted in hereditary Confucian learning and rich in classical scholarship, with extraordinary reputations and illustrious deeds well worth recounting. This was certainly admirable; yet some among them secretly tripped over the old stratagems of Zhao Guanghan 趙廣漢 and Zhang Chang 張敞. Compared to the governance of strumming the zither without descending from the hall, how different they were! This being so, when Fan Ye composed his biographies of upright officials and did not include these four men, how could it have been without reason? That Wang Cheng 王成 received prominent rewards for falsely inflating household registration figures need not even be discussed; yet if someone who strenuously promoted moral transformation like Huang Ba 黃覇 could still not escape the disparagement and ridicule of Zhang Chang, this would cause gentle, harmonious, benevolent, and beneficial governance to disappear from the empire. That Emperor Xuan of Han 漢宣帝 confused name and reality through overly stringent and coercive measures need not even be discussed; yet if an era that honored and employed upright and good officials like the Jianwu 建武 reign [of Emperor Guangwu 光武帝] is still faulted for the harshness and severity of its bureaucratic administration, this would cause a governance of comprehensive verification and vigorous diligence to remain obscure to later generations. Once one thoroughly understands this,…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而吏道之失得兩漢之所由盛不旣章章
著明也哉我
國家加惠元元愼重守宰其閒名臣碩輔勤
勳旂常固有筮仕郡邑著聲循良者矣擬
諸兩漢奚啻相及已哉今天下吏弊日滋
民生日瘁
當宁之所睠懷鈞衡之所籌畫欲得良牧而拊
循之甚於濟川之望舟楫欲已疾者之急
倉公也乃其閒議論雖多而推行似窒科
===
條雖密而實効罔臻誠有如執事之所慮
者說者歸咎于久任之未行資格之太限
是固一說也不知久任議而積薪之嘆興
曠格度而競進之門啓法固有可言而不
可行者而況守宰非秩滿不遷今時未盡
更也即有超登不離凡品安所示勸耶愚
以今之牧民者未能深惟乎設官之意而
今之課吏者不皆專責其爲民之功是以
名實混淆而治效罔顯有繇然爾茲欲飭
punctuated: 而吏道之失得、兩漢之所由盛，不旣章章著明也哉！我國家加惠元元，愼重守宰，其閒名臣碩輔，勤勳旂常，固有筮仕郡邑、著聲循良者矣，擬諸兩漢，奚啻相及已哉！今天下吏弊日滋，民生日瘁，當宁之所睠懷，鈞衡之所籌畫，欲得良牧而拊循之，甚於濟川之望舟楫、欲已疾者之急倉公也。乃其閒議論雖多而推行似窒，科條雖密而實効罔臻，誠有如執事之所慮者。說者歸咎于久任之未行、資格之太限，是固一說也。不知久任議而積薪之嘆興，曠格度而競進之門啓，法固有可言而不可行者。而況守宰非秩滿不遷，今時未盡更也；即有超登，不離凡品，安所示勸耶？愚以今之牧民者未能深惟乎設官之意，而今之課吏者不皆專責其爲民之功，是以名實混淆而治效罔顯，有繇然爾。茲欲飭
translation_en:
… then are not the successes and failures in the ways of officialdom, and the reasons why the Two Han dynasties flourished, already abundantly clear and manifest?

Our Dynasty bestows favor upon the common people and exercises great care over prefects and magistrates. Among them, renowned ministers and great counselors whose meritorious deeds are inscribed on the royal banners have indeed included those who began their official careers in commanderies and districts and won fame as upright and benevolent officials. Compared to the Two Han dynasties, how could they merely be their equals! Today, administrative abuses across the realm multiply daily, and the people's livelihood grows daily more distressed. What the Sovereign on the throne fondly cares about, and what those who hold the scales of government plan for, is a desire to obtain good shepherds of the people to soothe and comfort them—more urgently than one crossing a river longs for boats and oars, or one wishing to cure an illness anxiously seeks out Canggong [the legendary physician Chunyu Yi]. Yet amid all this, although discussions are numerous, their implementation seems obstructed; although regulations are dense, substantive results are not achieved—truly just as Your Excellency is concerned about.

Commentators lay the blame on the failure to practice long tenures of office and the excessive restriction of seniority qualifications. This is, to be sure, one argument. Yet they do not realize that when long tenure is proposed, the lament of "piling up firewood" [latecomers being promoted over long-serving officials] arises, and when qualification rules are set aside, the door to competitive scrambling for advancement is opened. There are indeed laws that can be spoken of in theory but cannot be put into practice. Moreover, the rule that prefects and magistrates are not transferred before their term of office is completed has not been entirely altered at present; and even if there are extraordinary promotions, if those promoted do not rise above ordinary caliber, how does that serve to encourage anyone? In my humble view, those who shepherd the people today fail to reflect deeply upon the original intent of establishing offices, while those who evaluate officials today do not all hold them strictly accountable for their achievements on behalf of the people. Therefore, reputation and reality are confounded and the effects of good governance fail to become manifest—there is a reason for this. Now, if we wish to rectify…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
文治而佐元元之急其所當議者有五而
久任超格不與焉明按部一也嚴舉刺二
也剗煩苛三也覈功實四也重貪殘之禁
五也夫今之爲民牧者譬則牧牛羊然爲
主人者視其牛羊之蕃茁而已矣不必煩
爲之驅而多爲之監也今以一守令而大
吏十數人制于其上彼督撫巡察之權非
不軒然重也而參以監司臨以制使亦足
廣風厲示激揚矣乃一切持斧之使皆得
===
以計禮數而持短長凡吏之勤苦焦勞日
夜以承伺其上者無餘閒也何暇爲民耶
此按部之所當明者也古者進賢受上賞
誣善有常刑所以防欺蔽專責成也部使
者區別羣吏而論奏之即鈞衡視之以進
退公論因之以重輕者也今或愛憎殊情
臧否任意薦賢以昭德而附下罔上者無
辜擊刺以揚權而深文巧詆者弗論非所
以示大公絶欺詐之路也此舉刺之所當
punctuated: 文治而佐元元之急，其所當議者有五，而久任、超格不與焉：明按部，一也；嚴舉刺，二也；剗煩苛，三也；覈功實，四也；重貪殘之禁，五也。夫今之爲民牧者，譬則牧牛羊然。爲主人者，視其牛羊之蕃茁而已矣，不必煩爲之驅而多爲之監也。今以一守令，而大吏十數人制于其上。彼督撫、巡察之權，非不軒然重也，而參以監司，臨以制使，亦足廣風厲、示激揚矣。乃一切持斧之使，皆得以計禮數而持短長，凡吏之勤苦焦勞，日夜以承伺其上者無餘閒也，何暇爲民耶？此按部之所當明者也。古者進賢受上賞，誣善有常刑，所以防欺蔽、專責成也。部使者區別羣吏而論奏之，即鈞衡視之以進退，公論因之以重輕者也。今或愛憎殊情，臧否任意；薦賢以昭德，而附下罔上者無辜；擊刺以揚權，而深文巧詆者弗論。非所以示大公、絶欺詐之路也。此舉刺之所當
translation_en:
… civil administration and relieve the urgent distress of the common people, there are five matters that ought to be deliberated, and extended tenure and extraordinary promotions are not among them: first, clarifying regional inspection; second, enforcing strictness in recommendations and impeachments; third, eliminating vexatiousness and harshness; fourth, verifying the reality of achievements; and fifth, strengthening the prohibitions against贪婪 (greed) and cruelty.

Now, those who serve as shepherds of the people today may be compared to those who herd cattle and sheep. The master simply looks to see whether his cattle and sheep are flourishing and multiplying; there is no need to trouble oneself with driving them about or setting up numerous overseers for them. Yet today, over a single Prefect or Magistrate, there are a dozen or more high officials exercising control above him. The authority of those Supreme Commanders, Grand Coordinators, and Regional Inspectors is certainly lofty and weighty enough; and when supplemented by Surveillance and Administration Commissioners and overseen by special imperial commissioners, this is already sufficient to broadcast stimulation and encouragement and to display the dismissal of the corrupt and promotion of the worthy. Yet every single envoy bearing the axe of authority is able to nitpick over ceremonial courtesies and hold their faults and merits over them. Thus, in all their diligent toil and anxious labor, local officials have no spare moment day or night from waiting upon and catering to their superiors—what leisure do they have to care for the people? This is why regional inspection ought to be clarified.

In antiquity, those who advanced the worthy received the highest rewards, while those who slandered the good were subject to regular punishments; this was the means to prevent deception and concealment and to focus accountability for results. When regional inspectors distinguish among the various officials and submit memorials evaluating them, the Ministry of Personnel looks to these evaluations to promote or demote, and public opinion relies on them to weigh an official's standing. Today, however, personal likes and dislikes sometimes dictate feelings, and praise or blame is meted out at will. Recommending the worthy is meant to make virtue manifest, yet those who curry favor below and deceive their superiors go unpunished; impeaching the corrupt is meant to assert authority, yet those who manipulate the letter of the law to craftily slander others are not called to account. This is no way to demonstrate great impartiality or to cut off the path of deceit and fraud. This is why recommendations and impeachments ought to be…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
嚴者也夫急轡御者非千里之節也察淵
魚者非含弘之象也故蓋公相齊無擾獄
市汲直守淮陽其治責大指而已此皆淸
淨守法無所變更之明效也今吏道率務
精敏尚操切建白易置日取當世之約束
而紛更之不知政令旁午姦宄滋彰民且
囂然喪其樂生之心而國之元氣亦索矣
此煩苛之所當剗者也夫以名行賞則天
下飾名以求功以文行罰則天下巧文以
===
逃罪弊所繇來非一日矣今薦剡交上于
公車訾毀頻移於月旦籍令僞聲軼而功
罪淆吾恐害不止于民生而且移之國是
也此功實之所當覈者也夫十金之法至
重也殘夫之爲民害至酷烈也汙者視民
如外府而刻者操下若濕薪至于竭膏髓
裂頭腦而不顧則其罪奚止于削籍也今
者一或論罷輒務姑息追呼案驗一切寢
行此浮慕長者之名而不顧凡民之斁者
punctuated: 嚴者也。夫急轡御者，非千里之節也；察淵魚者，非含弘之象也。故蓋公相齊，無擾獄市；汲直守淮陽，其治責大指而已。此皆淸淨守法，無所變更之明效也。今吏道率務精敏，尚操切，建白易置，日取當世之約束而紛更之。不知政令旁午，姦宄滋彰，民且囂然喪其樂生之心，而國之元氣亦索矣。此煩苛之所當剗者也。夫以名行賞，則天下飾名以求功；以文行罰，則天下巧文以逃罪，弊所繇來非一日矣。今薦剡交上于公車，訾毀頻移於月旦。籍令僞聲軼而功罪淆，吾恐害不止于民生，而且移之國是也。此功實之所當覈者也。夫十金之法至重也，殘夫之爲民害至酷烈也。汙者視民如外府，而刻者操下若濕薪，至于竭膏髓、裂頭腦而不顧，則其罪奚止于削籍也？今者一或論罷，輒務姑息，追呼案驗，一切寢行。此浮慕長者之名，而不顧凡民之斁者
translation_en: … must be made strict. Now, driving with tight reins is not the pacing for a thousand-li journey; peering into the depths after fish is not the image of all-embracing magnanimity. Thus, when Master Gai (Gai Gong 蓋公) advised the Chancellor of Qi, he counselled against disturbing the courts and markets; when Ji the Upright (Ji An 汲黯) served as Grand Administrator of Huaiyang, his governance insisted only on the broad essentials. These were all clear effects of remaining tranquil and pure, abiding by the laws, and making no alterations. Today, the way of officials generally strives after keenness and agility and prizes harsh urgency; in making proposals and changing arrangements, they daily take the established regulations of the present age and throw them into confusion by altering them. They do not realize that when administrative orders fly in all directions, villainy and treachery grow ever more manifest; the people, in clamor and distress, lose their joy in living, and the vital energy of the state is likewise exhausted. This is why petty烦-harshness must be pared away. Now, if rewards are dispensed on the basis of reputation, the world will embellish reputations to seek merit; if punishments are carried out on the basis of paper formalities, the world will manipulate the letter of the law to evade guilt—an abuse whose origins do not date from a single day. Today, memorials of recommendation are submitted one after another to the Offices of Public Carriages, while criticisms and slanders shift frequently in the monthly evaluations. Should false reputations surpass reality and merits and offenses become confused, I fear the harm will not stop with the people's livelihood, but will extend even to the fundamental policies of the state. This is why actual achievements must be verified. Now, the law regarding ten-gold bribery is extremely weighty, and the harm done to the people by cruel men is utterly fierce and bitter. Corrupt officials regard the people as their personal outer treasury, while harsh ones bind their subordinates like bundles of wet firewood, going so far as to drain their fat and marrow and split their heads and brains without a backward glance—how could their crime merely end with being struck from the official registers? Yet nowadays, once someone is impeached and dismissed, the authorities immediately practice leniency and indulgence; summonses for recovery and judicial investigations are altogether shelved. This is vainly coveting the reputation of a magnanimous elder while disregarding the ruin of the common people…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
也語曰信于令則令行敢于不善人則善
人安此貪殘之禁之所當重也今誠專督
察之權慎侵官之令臨以撫按矣而臺臣
之各有專勑者勿槩撓焉參之藩臬矣而
諸司之各有分土者勿遥制焉由是而有
所舉也舉必當賢而狥私者有罰有所刺
也刺必當罪而賊善者有刑法守畫一能
者罔以炫其奇治行有稽僞者無所容其
巧用刑次骨者與傷人者同科簠簋不飭
===
者同主盜者抵罪則振刷有條而上之所
爲責成者皆爲民之實意綜理有要而下
之所以展布者皆爲民之實功由是而績
用有叙則任可久如漢之增秩賜金以俟
其成者間一行之而不爲滞也治效異等
則格可超如漢之表爲列卿以示其勸者
間一行之而不爲過也政何以不若古人
治何以不臻實效兩漢之循吏不足多而
况執事之所下詢者直能吏爾何足道哉
punctuated: 也。語曰：「信于令則令行，敢于不善人則善人安。」此貪殘之禁之所當重也。今誠專督察之權，慎侵官之令。臨以撫按矣，而臺臣之各有專勑者勿槩撓焉；參之藩臬矣，而諸司之各有分土者勿遥制焉。由是而有所舉也，舉必當賢，而狥私者有罰；有所刺也，刺必當罪，而賊善者有刑。法守畫一，能者罔以炫其奇；治行有稽，僞者無所容其巧。用刑次骨者，與傷人者同科；簠簋不飭者，同主盜者抵罪。則振刷有條，而上之所爲責成者，皆爲民之實意；綜理有要，而下之所以展布者，皆爲民之實功。由是而績用有叙，則任可久，如漢之增秩賜金以俟其成者，間一行之而不爲滞也；治效異等，則格可超，如漢之表爲列卿以示其勸者，間一行之而不爲過也。政何以不若古人？治何以不臻實效？兩漢之循吏不足多，而况執事之所下詢者直能吏爾，何足道哉！
translation_en: … [those who ignore the ruin of the common people]. As the saying goes: "When there is trustworthiness in commands, commands are carried out; when one is bold against evil men, good men are at peace." This is why the prohibition against greed and cruelty must be given heavy emphasis. Now, if we truly concentrate the authority of supervision and investigation, and exercise caution regarding the rules against encroaching on others' official duties: they are already overseen by the Grand Coordinators and Regional Inspectors, so let other Censorate officials who each hold special imperial commissions not uniformly interfere with them; they are already cross-checked by the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, so let the various offices that each have their own allotted territories not control them from afar. From this, when there are recommendations, the recommendations will surely match the worthy, and those who indulge in private favoritism will be punished; when there are impeachments, the impeachments will surely match the offenses, and those who harm the good will face penalties. When the observance of the law is uniform, the capable will have no way to show off their novelty; when administrative performance is verified, the deceitful will have nowhere to harbor their cleverness. Those who apply punishments that cut to the bone should be sentenced under the same category as those who inflict bodily injury; those whose official conduct is corrupt ("whose sacrificial vessels are not in order") should be punished for their crimes on the same basis as custodians who steal from the treasury. Then reform and renewal will have order, and what superiors demand as results will all be genuine intentions for the good of the people; comprehensive management will have its essentials, and what subordinates put into practice will all be genuine achievements for the good of the people. From this, when achievements and service are properly ranked, tenure in office can be made long—like the Han practice of increasing rank and bestowing gold to await their full accomplishment, which may be carried out from time to time without being considered stagnation. When administrative efficacy is of an exceptional grade, regular qualifications can be bypassed—like the Han practice of elevating officials to the Nine Ministers to demonstrate encouragement, which may be carried out from time to time without being considered excessive. Why then would our governance not equal that of the ancients? Why would our administration not achieve real results? Even the upright officials (xunli) of the Former and Later Han would not be worth making much of—let alone those about whom Your Excellency inquired, who were merely capable officials (nengli) and hardly worth mentioning!

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第四問
同考試官推官劉　批〔理學政事節義文章　錢達道〕
四者貴根極于道此作崇論先哲而以道折衷之不惟品藻之當而且有得于尚友之深者
考試官右中允何　批〔考訂詳核品騭精當而一權衡乎朱子是知所準的者〕
考試官左中允范　批〔考據精詳議論閎博而末復折衷於朱子尤見趨向之正取之〕
===
尚論前修者豈無所準哉亦準乎道而已
夫士生于前垂休光而照後世士生于後
享大名而顯當時其所以負天下之望而
建不朽之業者謂其理學統承乎先聖政
事澤潤乎生民文章闡六藝之菁華節義
扶兩間之正氣而道也者所以爲立德立
功立言之本者也君子而有得于道矣雖
其事功學術迥不相謀植節修辭稱名亦
異要皆充其量之所極以各得其性之所
punctuated:
第四問
同考試官推官劉批〔理學、政事、節義、文章，　錢達道〕：四者貴根極于道。此作崇論先哲，而以道折衷之，不惟品藻之當，而且有得于尚友之深者。
考試官右中允何批〔考訂詳核，品騭精當，而一權衡乎朱子，是知所準的者。〕
考試官左中允范批〔考據精詳，議論閎博，而末復折衷於朱子，尤見趨向之正。取之。〕
尚論前修者，豈無所準哉？亦準乎道而已。夫士生于前，垂休光而照後世；士生于後，享大名而顯當時。其所以負天下之望而建不朽之業者，謂其理學統承乎先聖，政事澤潤乎生民，文章闡六藝之菁華，節義扶兩間之正氣，而道也者，所以爲立德、立功、立言之本者也。君子而有得于道矣，雖其事功、學術迥不相謀，植節、修辭稱名亦異，要皆充其量之所極，以各得其性之所
translation_en:
Fourth Question

Comment by Associate Examiner and Prefectural Judge Liu [Neo-Confucian learning (lixue), statecraft, moral integrity, and literary composition; by Qian Dadao 錢達道]: These four things are valued when they are rooted ultimately in the Way. This essay loftily discusses the former worthies and judges them by the standard of the Way; not only are its evaluations fitting, but it also attains a deep understanding of "making friends with the ancients."

Comment by Examiner and Right Companion to the Heir Apparent He: [Its textual verification is detailed and exact, its evaluations are precise and fitting, and it weighs everything by the standard of Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹)—this shows an understanding of the proper criterion.]

Comment by Examiner and Left Companion to the Heir Apparent Fan: [Its evidential grounding is precise and detailed, its arguments are grand and broad, and at the end it again takes Master Zhu as its final arbiter, which especially reveals the correctness of the author's orientation. Selected.]

Could those who critically discuss the worthies of the past lack a standard? Their standard is simply the Way and nothing else. Scholars born in earlier times hand down asplendid light that illuminates later generations; scholars born in later times enjoy great renown and become illustrious in their own day. The reason they carry the expectations of the world and establish imperishable achievements is that their Neo-Confucian learning continues the transmission of the former sages, their statecraft moistens the living people with blessings, their literary compositions elucidate the finest essence of the Six Arts, and their moral integrity upholds the upright qi between Heaven and Earth—whereas the Way is that which serves as the foundation for establishing virtue, establishing merit, and establishing words. Once a gentleman has attained something of the Way, even if his practical achievements and scholarly learning do not take counsel with one another, and his establishment of integrity and cultivation of rhetoric go by different names, in essence they all fulfill the utmost limits of their capacity so that each attains what his nature…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
近而均可以爲後人法焉不然而徒支離
于訓詁馳騖于功名溺志于浮華甘心于
局曲其去道也遠矣何足爲君子齒哉執
事發策而以鄉之先哲下詢甚盛心也愚
敢無詞以對粤自三代而上風氣醇凝敎
化隆洽士皆沉涵學問漸漬道德蓄殖宏
深而其施爲也必大義理微密而其持守
也必堅識見精明而其論著也必當古之
聖賢固未始局蹐拘方以專攻其所事亦
===
不以偏才薄技特見其所長要之一本于
道而天下之能事畢矣降及叔世風會日
流聖遠言湮莫探道術之蒙晦王綱解紐
寧辭法意之漸荒以至名檢毀裂而軼縱
則廉隅盡忘性術闇洳而卑滐則丹素莫
辨於是後之儒者始有以自得之見求聖
人之心於千載之下而傳經載道以理學
著稱者焉始有以幹濟之材爲國家建必
然之畫而芘民尊主以政事名世者焉有
punctuated: 近，而均可以爲後人法焉。不然而徒支離于訓詁，馳騖于功名，溺志于浮華，甘心于局曲，其去道也遠矣，何足爲君子齒哉？執事發策，而以鄉之先哲下詢，甚盛心也，愚敢無詞以對？粤自三代而上，風氣醇凝，敎化隆洽，士皆沉涵學問，漸漬道德。蓄殖宏深，而其施爲也必大；義理微密，而其持守也必堅；識見精明，而其論著也必當。古之聖賢，固未始局蹐拘方以專攻其所事，亦不以偏才薄技特見其所長；要之一本于道，而天下之能事畢矣。降及叔世，風會日流。聖遠言湮，莫探道術之蒙晦；王綱解紐，寧辭法意之漸荒？以至名檢毀裂而軼縱，則廉隅盡忘；性術闇洳而卑滐，則丹素莫辨。於是後之儒者，始有以自得之見，求聖人之心於千載之下，而傳經載道，以理學著稱者焉；始有以幹濟之材，爲國家建必然之畫，而芘民尊主，以政事名世者焉；有
translation_en:
…what was akin to it, and thus all alike can serve as models for later generations. Otherwise, if one merely fragments oneself in philological exegesis, chases wildly after功名 (merit and fame), drowns one's ambitions in superficial华麗 (showiness), or rests content in narrow pettiness, how far removed that is from the Way! How could such a person be worthy of being mentioned among gentlemen? Your Excellency has issued this policy question to inquire of us concerning the former worthies of our native region. This shows a most magnanimous heart; how dare I, in my ignorance, fail to offer a reply?

Looking back to the Three Dynasties and earlier, customs were pure and solid, and moral transformation was abundant and pervasive. Scholars were all deeply immersed in learning and steeped in morality. Because their accumulation of learning was vast and profound, their practical achievements were necessarily great; because their grasp of moral principles was subtle and precise, their personal integrity was necessarily firm; because their insight was keen and clear, their discourses and writings were necessarily fitting. The sages and worthies of antiquity certainly never confined themselves narrowly to one corner to specialize solely in a single pursuit, nor did they display their strengths merely through one-sided talents or petty skills. In sum, everything was rooted in the Way, and thus all the capabilities required in the world were complete.

Coming down to later, degenerate ages, customs and trends deteriorated day by day. As the sages receded into the distance and their words were lost, no one probed the obscured art of the Way; as the royal cord came untied, how could the spirit of the laws avoid gradually falling into ruin? It reached the point where moral conduct and self-restraint were shattered and cast into unbridled license, so that upright integrity was completely forgotten; inner nature and scholarly arts became dark, sodden, and base [? 卑滐], so that vermilion and white could no longer be distinguished. Thereupon, among later Confucians there first appeared those who, through their own hard-won insights, sought the mind of the sages a thousand years later, transmitting the Classics and conveying the Way, and thus became renowned for the Learning of Principle (lixue); there first appeared those who, with talents for practical administration, established unfailing plans for the state, sheltering the people and honoring the ruler, and thus became famous in their generation for governance; there were…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
獨行高節挺身于威武利祿之衝而以節
義流光于史冊者矣有揚芬振藻驚精于
四科五色之兼而以文章擅美于一時者
矣夫是四者雖各因其所著以得名未必
其皆交修而儷至然立言垂訓者繼絕學
而統聖眞策勳樹庸者經邦家而綏社稷
或以植綱常于媮懦頹決之際或以潤鴻
業于阻深闇汐之中固不必渾融齊一如
古初猶或能振世作人于無已特其於道
===
有聞有未聞故其業之所就因之而人品
高下于其間矣請以是而品隲先正可乎
夫南畿隸江左右晝長江大湖以爲國方
地千餘里林麓川澤之美殆不可計而光
岳冲粹之氣蔚爲人文之盛者固有後先
相繼更僕難數者焉姑即明問所及者言
之公子札宏覽博物輕千乘之國而不居
康節氏謂其才近伯夷所以易諸樊斷髮
之俗者至于今爲烈也言偃身通六藝以
punctuated:
獨行高節，挺身于威武利祿之衝，而以節義流光于史冊者矣；有揚芬振藻，驚精于四科五色之兼，而以文章擅美于一時者矣。夫是四者，雖各因其所著以得名，未必其皆交修而儷至。然立言垂訓者，繼絕學而統聖眞；策勳樹庸者，經邦家而綏社稷；或以植綱常于媮懦頹決之際，或以潤鴻業于阻深闇汐之中。固不必渾融齊一如古初，猶或能振世作人于無已。特其於道有聞有未聞，故其業之所就因之，而人品高下于其間矣。請以是而品隲先正，可乎？
夫南畿隸江左右，晝長江、大湖以爲國，方地千餘里，林麓川澤之美，殆不可計；而光岳冲粹之氣，蔚爲人文之盛者，固有後先相繼、更僕難數者焉。姑即明問所及者言之：公子札宏覽博物，輕千乘之國而不居，康節氏謂其「才近伯夷」，所以易諸樊斷髮之俗者，至于今爲烈也；言偃身通六藝，以
translation_en:
… those of solitary conduct and lofty integrity who stood firm at the crossroads of coercive force and lucrative emolument, and thereby caused their principled righteousness to shine down through the pages of history; and those who spread fragrance and brandished literary elegance, astounding minds by combining the four categories of poetry and the five colors of rhetoric, and thereby commanded sole beauty in literary composition in their own time. Now, although these four types of men each gained renown on account of that in which they excelled, they did not necessarily cultivate all these qualities together or attain them in equal measure. Yet those who established words to hand down instruction continued lost learning and unified the true way of the sages; those who registered merits and erected achievements ordered the state and pacified the altars of soil and grain; some upheld the cardinal human bonds amidst listless cowardice and collapsing norms, while others adorned the great imperial enterprise out of abstruse depths and obscure recesses. Even though they need not have been as seamlessly blended and uniform as the men of high antiquity, they were still able to rouse the world and inspire men endlessly. It is only that some had heard the Way while others had not yet heard it; hence what they accomplished in their undertakings varied accordingly, and the stature of their personal character was ranked higher or lower therein. May I ask permission to use this standard to evaluate the worthies of the past?

Now, the Southern Metropolitan Region (Nanji) governs the territories to the left and right of the Yangtze River, demarcated [晝, read as 畫] by the Yangtze River and the Great Lake (Taihu) to form the realm. Covering an area of more than a thousand li square, the beauties of its wooded foothills, rivers, and marshes are well-nigh incalculable; and those in whom the harmonious and pure vital force of the luminous sacred peaks has flourished into an abundance of cultural and human excellence have indeed succeeded one another from early to late, too numerous to count even if one changed attendants. Let me speak for the moment only of those touched upon in Your enlightened question: Prince Zha (Gongzi Zha, i.e., Jizha of Wu 吳季札) was of broad observation and wide learning, counting a state of a thousand chariots lightly and declining to occupy the throne. Master Kangjie (Shao Yong 邵雍) said that his "talent was close to that of Boyi," and that whereby he transformed the customs of Zhufan's people—who cut their hair short—remains illustrious down to the present day. Yan Yan 言偃 (Ziyou 子游) personally mastered the Six Arts, and with…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
禮樂之教而化民當其時以文學見稱所
謂南方之精華得斯人而爲之盡發者固
其素所蓄積也嗣是厥後代不乏人朱考
亭學務躬行集諸儒大成之統胡安定身
任師道繼河汾正脉之傳固一代理學之
宗盟矣至若號雙湖而著易學啓蒙翼傳
者胡一桂也謚文通而述四書辨疑者胡
炳文也二胡淵源於朱子而各有所發明
不皆有功于後學者乎文翁教民興學變
===
蜀郡僻陋之風敬輿才負王佐輔奉天艱
難之業固漢唐政事之首出矣若希文召
對天章而上十事以釐弊夷簡勸帝親政
而手八事以匡時雖其建置或殊而經濟
則一不皆有裨於時政者乎若其以節義
著聲者漢有龔勝唐有何蕃宋有陳東陸
秀夫也夫勝諫議秀夫宰臣也奸雄竊鼎
則托疾以辭徵聘之臨胡運秉華則蹈海
以全殉君之節若二人者幾于守死善道
punctuated: 禮樂之教而化民，當其時以文學見稱，所謂「南方之精華，得斯人而爲之盡發」者，固其素所蓄積也。嗣是厥後，代不乏人。朱考亭學務躬行，集諸儒大成之統；胡安定身任師道，繼河汾正脉之傳，固一代理學之宗盟矣。至若號雙湖而著《易學啓蒙翼傳》者，胡一桂也；謚文通而述《四書辨疑》者，胡炳文也。二胡淵源於朱子而各有所發明，不皆有功于後學者乎？文翁教民興學，變蜀郡僻陋之風；敬輿才負王佐，輔奉天艱難之業，固漢、唐政事之首出矣。若希文召對天章而上十事以釐弊，夷簡勸帝親政而手八事以匡時，雖其建置或殊而經濟則一，不皆有裨於時政者乎？若其以節義著聲者：漢有龔勝，唐有何蕃，宋有陳東、陸秀夫也。夫勝，諫議；秀夫，宰臣也。奸雄竊鼎，則托疾以辭徵聘之臨；胡運秉華，則蹈海以全殉君之節。若二人者，幾于守死善道…
translation_en: …the teaching of rites and music to transform the common people, and in his own time he was renowned for culture and learning. The saying that "the finest essence of the South found in this man its complete expression" truly reflects what had long been accumulated there. From that time onward, no era has lacked worthy men. Zhu Kaoting (Zhu Xi 朱熹) devoted his learning to personal practice and brought together the great synthesis of the various Confucian scholars' traditions; Hu Anding (Hu Yuan 胡瑗) took upon himself the Way of the teacher and carried on the orthodox lineage of Hefen (Wang Tong 王通). Truly they were the leading masters of Neo-Confucianism (lixue) for their ages. As for the one styled Shuanghu who wrote the Supplementary Commentary on the Introduction to the Study of the Changes (Yixue qimeng yizhuan), that was Hu Yigui 胡一桂; and the one posthumously titled Wentong who compiled the Resolving Doubts on the Four Books (Sishu bianyi), that was Hu Bingwen 胡炳文. Both Hus traced their scholarly origins to Master Zhu and each made his own elucidations—did they not both render meritorious service to later scholars? Wen Weng 文翁 instructed the people and promoted schools, transforming the rustic and narrow customs of Shu Commandery; Jingyu (Lu Zhi 陸贄) possessed the talent of a kingly counselor and assisted in the arduous enterprise at Fengtian. Truly they stood foremost in statesmanship during the Han and Tang dynasties. As for Xiwen (Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹), who was summoned to an audience at the Tianzhang Pavilion and submitted ten proposals to reform abuses, and Yijian (Lü Yijian 呂夷簡), who urged the emperor to assume personal rule and presented in his own hand eight measures to rectify the times—although the policies they established differed in some respects, their statecraft was one and the same. Were they not both of benefit to the governance of their times? As for those who gained renown through moral integrity and righteousness: in the Han there was Gong Sheng 龔勝, in the Tang there was He Fan 何蕃, and in the Song there were Chen Dong 陳東 and Lu Xiufu 陸秀夫. Now Gong Sheng was a Remonstrant (jianyi) and Lu Xiufu was a chief minister. When a treacherous usurper stole the imperial tripods, the former pleaded illness to decline the arrival of a summons to office; when the fortune of the northern barbarians took hold of China, the latter cast himself into the sea to fulfill his integrity in dying for his sovereign. Men like these two came close to "holding fast to the good Way unto death"…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
矣蕃東太學生爾蕃以書生而正色以遏
六舘之邪謀東以布衣而昌言以排六賊
之奸諛英風義烈不可與日月爭光乎以
文章鳴盛者若漢之劉向魏之曹植晉之
機雲宋之王珪皆是也夫向本名儒植負
異質一則明經有行著新序而曾鞏氏稱
其最爲近古一則登臺作賦美詞翰而王
通氏稱其文深以思若二人者可謂藝苑
之英矣機雲兄弟齊名稱爲雲間二陸而
===
文章豈能冠世王珪閎侈瓌麗爲文自成
一家而典策多出其手鴻裁黼製不可以
伯仲曹劉乎夫是四者析之而各一其稱
合之而同歸於道得則體用相須而靡施
之弗當失則氣質任事而致用之或偏士
君子所以垂世不朽者恃有此道而已矣
自今言之厲志聖賢者篤愛君憂國之誠
教授蘇湖者有稽古愛民之實文正志在
匡時而况通六經學者多從質問宣公才
punctuated: 矣。蕃、東，太學生爾。蕃以書生而正色以遏六舘之邪謀，東以布衣而昌言以排六賊之奸諛，英風義烈，不可與日月爭光乎？以文章鳴盛者，若漢之劉向、魏之曹植、晉之機雲、宋之王珪，皆是也。夫向本名儒，植負異質；一則明經有行，著《新序》而曾鞏氏稱其最爲近古；一則登臺作賦，美詞翰而王通氏稱其文深以思。若二人者，可謂藝苑之英矣。機、雲兄弟齊名，稱爲「雲間二陸」，而文章豈能冠世？王珪閎侈瓌麗，爲文自成一家，而典策多出其手，鴻裁黼製，不可以伯仲曹、劉乎？夫是四者，析之而各一其稱，合之而同歸於道。得則體用相須，而靡施之弗當；失則氣質任事，而致用之或偏。士君子所以垂世不朽者，恃有此道而已矣。自今言之，厲志聖賢者，篤愛君憂國之誠；教授蘇、湖者，有稽古愛民之實。文正志在匡時，而况通《六經》，學者多從質問；宣公才
translation_en:
… Indeed, He Fan and Chen Dong were merely students of the National University! Yet He Fan, as a simple scholar, assumed a stern countenance to thwart the treacherous plots of the Six Halls; and Chen Dong, as a commoner, spoke out boldly to denounce the wicked flattery of the Six Traitors. May not their heroic spirit and righteous ardor vie in brilliance with the sun and moon? As for those who gained renown for their literary compositions, such were Liu Xiang 劉向 of the Han, Cao Zhi 曹植 of the Wei, Lu Ji 陸機 and Lu Yun 陸雲 of the Jin, and Wang Gui 王珪 of the Song. Now, Liu Xiang was originally a celebrated Confucian scholar, while Cao Zhi was endowed with extraordinary talent. The former mastered the classics, maintained virtuous conduct, and authored the New Prefaces (Xinxu), which Zeng Gong 曾鞏 praised as being closest to antiquity; the latter ascended the terrace to compose rhapsodies, excelling in literary brush, so that Wang Tong 王通 praised his writing as profound and thoughtful. Men like these two may truly be called the flower of the literary garden! The brothers Lu Ji and Lu Yun shared equal fame and were known as the "Two Lus of Yunjian," yet how could their writings crown the age [or: and their writings were said to crown the age(?)]? Wang Gui was grand, lavish, and magnificent; in writing he formed a school of his own, and imperial edicts and state documents mostly came from his hand. In grand design and embroidered execution, could he not stand shoulder to shoulder with Cao Zhi and Liu Xiang?

Now, when these four categories are analyzed separately, each has its own distinct designation; when combined, they all converge in the Way. When the Way is attained, substance and function support one another, and nothing applied fails to be appropriate; when it is missed, one acts merely upon innate temperament, and practical application may become one-sided. That by which a scholar-gentleman hands down an imperishable name to posterity relies solely upon the possession of this Way! Speaking of it from the present perspective: those who set their minds on the sages and worthies were earnest in their loyalty to the ruler and concern for the state; he who taught in Suzhou and Huzhou [Hu Yuan 胡瑗] possessed the reality of investigating antiquity and loving the people. Fan Wenzheng [Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹] set his ambition on rectifying the times, and moreover mastered the Six Classics, so that scholars frequently came to him to ask questions; Duke Xuan [Lu Zhi 陸贄] had talent …

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
本王佐而力辭萬鎰之者顧附志年何蕃
有學成行尊之譽龔勝兼明經孝廉之科
更生以忠直見褒寧論著述子建以天下
爲讓詎止文詞然則諸賢之得名各自其
著者言之而非謂其不能相兼也若文靖
之剛愎妨賢少陽之危言召禍忠節之不
能存宋機雲之駢首就戮夫亦其賦質之
偏遭時之厄固有不容例論者律之以道
而才品之優劣不既章章較著也哉我
===
國家道化隆茂超軼千古無論
開國翼運忠賢叅合即其間哲士貞臣詞人
碩輔固有炳炳烺烺所在挺生者矣矧南
畿地靈人傑甲于寰寓愚生生齒其鄉景
行前哲豈無可以復執事之問者乎試言
其著則吳文恪之古道古心王文恪之明
理克己邵文莊之定性書說夏正夫之三
惜名言張莊簡之力學篤行莊定山之持
身有法皆無媿于明理反躬之實學矣而
punctuated: 本王佐，而力辭萬鎰之者，顧附志年。何蕃有學成行尊之譽，龔勝兼明經、孝廉之科；更生以忠直見褒，寧論著述？子建以天下爲讓，詎止文詞？然則諸賢之得名，各自其著者言之，而非謂其不能相兼也。若文靖之剛愎妨賢，少陽之危言召禍，忠節之不能存宋，機、雲之駢首就戮，夫亦其賦質之偏、遭時之厄，固有不容例論者。律之以道，而才品之優劣不既章章較著也哉？我國家道化隆茂，超軼千古，無論開國翼運，忠賢叅合；即其間哲士貞臣、詞人碩輔，固有炳炳烺烺，所在挺生者矣。矧南畿地靈人傑，甲于寰寓，愚生生齒其鄉，景行前哲，豈無可以復執事之問者乎？試言其著：則吳文恪之古道古心，王文恪之明理克己，邵文莊之《定性書說》，夏正夫之「三惜」名言，張莊簡之力學篤行，莊定山之持身有法，皆無媿于明理反躬之實學矣。而
translation_en:
… was fundamentally that of a kingly assistant, yet he forcefully declined gifts of ten thousand yi of gold and attached himself [to the younger generation in his later years? 顧附志年—likely a garbled printing of 顧附忘年, "yet formed friendships that forgot differences in age"]. He Fan 何蕃 enjoyed the reputation of accomplished learning and venerable conduct, while Gong Sheng 龔勝 combined the qualifications of Illuminated the Classics (mingjing) and Filial and Incorrupt (xiaolian). Gengsheng 更生 (Liu Xiang 劉向) was praised for his loyalty and uprightness—why speak only of his writings? Zijian 子建 (Cao Zhi 曹植) yielded the realm—how could he be known merely for his literary compositions? Thus, when these worthies acquired their reputations, each was spoken of in terms of what was most prominent in him, not because he was incapable of combining the other virtues. As for Duke Wenjing's 文靖 (Lü Yihao 呂頤浩) stubborn perversity and obstruction of the worthy, Shaoyang's 少陽 (Chen Dong 陳東) perilous words that invited disaster, Duke Zhongjie's 忠節 [or loyal integrity's] inability to preserve the Song, and Ji 機 (Lu Ji 陸機) and Yun's 雲 (Lu Yun 陸雲) being executed side by side—these too resulted from the biases of their endowed natures or the misfortunes of the times they encountered, which certainly cannot be judged by a single uniform standard. Yet if we measure them by the Way, are not the superiority and inferiority of their talents and character already abundantly clear and manifest?

Our Dynasty's moral transformation is grand and flourishing, surpassing all antiquity. Not to mention the founding of the state and the assisting of its destiny, when loyal and worthy men joined together in harmony; even in the period since, wise scholars, steadfast ministers, literary men, and great辅弼 (counsellors) have truly shone with brilliant luster, springing forth everywhere. How much more so in the Southern Metropolitan Region (Nanji 南畿), where the numinous land and outstanding people rank first in the world! Born and raised in this region, I, a foolish student, look up to the former wise men with admiration—how could I lack examples with which to reply to Your Excellency's question? Let me try to speak of the most prominent among them: Wu Wenke's 吳文恪 (Wu Na 吳訥) ancient Way and ancient heart; Wang Wenke's 王文恪 (Wang Ao 王鏊) illumination of principle and self-mastery; Shao Wenzhuang's 邵文莊 (Shao Bao 邵寶) Explanation of the Letter on Calming the Nature (Dingxing shu shuo 定性書說); Xia Zhengfu's 夏正夫 (Xia寅 Xia Yin) famous words on the "Three Regrets" (san xi 三惜); Zhang Zhuangjian's 張莊簡 (Zhang Yue 張悅) strenuous study and earnest practice; and Zhuang Dingshan's 莊定山 (Zhuang Chang 莊昶) regulated personal conduct—all of these are worthy, without shame, of the substantive learning that illuminates principle and reflects upon oneself. And…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
夷考其華國之文經時之政立朝之節則
數君子之成名自博也而端靖淵穆如文
定清和恭靖如忠安瀟灑絕俗如虞謙潜
心性命如薛蕙非吏生敬輿之流亞乎倪
文毅之留心世務葉文莊之忠言遠識年
恭定之廉靖朴忠徐武功之訏謨贊畫韓
襄毅之決策應機陳僖敏之寬平簡易皆
庶幾乎先憂後樂之襟期矣而締觀其材
猷之顯風節之高著述之富則數君子之
===
取數自多也而開薦不怡如文恭臨敵無
怖如節愍執法抗論如陳祚慷慨論事如
練綱非君賓少陽之等埒乎夫吳自季札
迄于今上下數千百年而聞其風者猶使
人竦意振奮意者諸賢之在當時其興感
未必無自也矧
皇明獻實獨盛于吳楚之郊若與其氣運山川
交流互發以垂懿範于來艾愚生讀國寶
之緗閱琬琰之集甞躍然而興則傚之思
punctuated: 夷考其華國之文、經時之政、立朝之節，則數君子之成名自博也。而端靖淵穆如文定，清和恭靖如忠安，瀟灑絕俗如虞謙，潜心性命如薛蕙，非吏生、敬輿之流亞乎？倪文毅之留心世務，葉文莊之忠言遠識，年恭定之廉靖朴忠，徐武功之訏謨贊畫，韓襄毅之決策應機，陳僖敏之寬平簡易，皆庶幾乎先憂後樂之襟期矣。而締觀其材猷之顯、風節之高、著述之富，則數君子之取數自多也。而開薦不怡如文恭，臨敵無怖如節愍，執法抗論如陳祚，慷慨論事如練綱，非君賓、少陽之等埒乎？夫吳自季札迄于今，上下數千百年，而聞其風者猶使人竦意振奮；意者諸賢之在當時，其興感未必無自也。矧皇明獻實獨盛于吳楚之郊，若與其氣運山川交流互發，以垂懿範于來艾。愚生讀國寶之緗，閱琬琰之集，甞躍然而興則傚之思…
translation_en:
…when one calmly examines their writings that adorned the state, their governance that ordered the age, and their integrity in standing at court, the renown achieved by these several gentlemen was naturally broad. Moreover, those who were upright, tranquil, deep, and solemn like Wending (Wu Kuan 吳寬); pure, harmonious, reverent, and tranquil like Zhong'an (Hu Ying 胡濙); uninhibited and transcending the vulgar world like Yu Qian 虞謙; or immersed in the study of human nature and destiny like Xue Hui 薛蕙—were they not the peers of Lisheng [?] and Jingyu (Lu Zhi 陸贄)?

Ni Wenyi's (Ni Yue 倪岳) close attention to worldly affairs, Ye Wenzhuang's (Ye Sheng 葉盛) loyal words and far-reaching vision, Nian Gongding's (Nian Fu 年富) incorruptibility, quietude, and unadorned loyalty, Xu Wugong's (Xu Youzhen 徐有貞) grand counsels and assisting plans, Han Xiangyi's (Han Yong 韓雍) decisive strategies in responding to crises, and Chen Ximin's (Chen Xuan 陳鎰/陳選) broad-minded fairness and unpretentious simplicity—all came close to the aspiration of "worrying before the world worries and rejoicing after the world rejoices." And when one closely observes the prominence of their talents and plans, the loftiness of their moral character, and the richness of their writings, what these several gentlemen drew upon was naturally abundant. Furthermore, those who showed no pleasure upon being recommended for office [?] like Wengong (Liu Xuan 劉鉉), who faced the enemy without fear like Jiemin (Chen Qia 陳洽), who upheld the law and argued forthrightly like Chen Zuo 陳祚, or who spoke on affairs with impassioned vigor like Lian Gang 練綱—were they not the equals of Junbin (Mei Fu 梅福) and Shaoyang (Chen Dong 陳東)?

Now, in the region of Wu, from the time of Jizha 季札 down to the present—spanning several thousand or hundred years—hearing of his moral风範 still causes people to stand in awe and be roused to action; one may suppose that when those worthies lived in their own times, their inspiration was not without a source. How much more so when the worthy men and substantive achievements of our August Ming have flourished uniquely in the regions of Wu and Chu, as if flowing together and mutually inspiring the vital fortune of the age and its mountains and rivers, so as to hand down an admirable model to future generations! When I, your humble student, read the light-yellow scrolls of the state's treasures and peruse the collections carved on fine jade (such as the Mingchen wanyan lu 名臣琬琰錄), I have often leaped up in excitement and conceived the thought of emulating them…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
矣而執事猶欲審所願學以對愚以爲挾
冊而談往哲者其持論貴公程行而稽衆
美者其擇術貴審論焉而不準諸道譬諸
鍾石雜陳而宫商莫辨也學焉而不定其
趨譬諸滄流渺泛而津涯莫從也
國朝諸君子弗論已朱子之學兼總乎周程
張氏之說而獨接乎千載不傳之統觀其
平生所得數對必盡蒞職勤敏纖悉必親
致君澤民之猷雖不能盡行其志而亦可
===
以無媿于心難進易退之節雖未嘗矯以
爲名而實未嘗貶以求售語其博即天文
地志律曆兵機亦皆洞究其精微論其文
即騷人才士疲精竭神而常病其難至蓋
學已會其大原而道則無所不貫眞可謂
百世之師矣今天下兼材奇節誠不乏人
所慮者學術不明爾是故自漢以下之諸
賢雖皆以卓絶之標流光奕世而宋之仲
淹尤爲人物第一吾非不愛之慕之欲起
punctuated: 矣。而執事猶欲審所願學以對，愚以爲挾冊而談往哲者，其持論貴公；程行而稽衆美者，其擇術貴審。論焉而不準諸道，譬諸鍾石雜陳而宫商莫辨也；學焉而不定其趨，譬諸滄流渺泛而津涯莫從也。國朝諸君子弗論已。朱子之學，兼總乎周、程、張氏之說，而獨接乎千載不傳之統。觀其平生所得，數對必盡，蒞職勤敏，纖悉必親。致君澤民之猷，雖不能盡行其志，而亦可以無媿于心；難進易退之節，雖未嘗矯以爲名，而實未嘗貶以求售。語其博，即天文、地志、律曆、兵機，亦皆洞究其精微；論其文，即騷人才士疲精竭神，而常病其難至。蓋學已會其大原，而道則無所不貫，眞可謂百世之師矣。今天下兼材奇節誠不乏人，所慮者學術不明爾。是故自漢以下之諸賢，雖皆以卓絶之標流光奕世，而宋之仲淹尤爲人物第一，吾非不愛之慕之，欲起…
translation_en: … And yet Your Excellency still wishes to examine carefully whom I aspire to emulate in my reply. In my humble opinion, for those who hold books and discuss the worthies of the past, their arguments must value impartiality; for those who measure conduct and investigate the various virtues, their choice of path must value careful discernment. To discuss them without taking the Way as the standard is like setting out bells and chimes in a jumble where the musical notes gong and shang cannot be distinguished; to study them without fixing one's direction is like drifting across a vast, boundless current where no ford or shore can be followed. Let us leave aside for now the worthy gentlemen of our Reigning Dynasty. The learning of Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] comprehensively synthesizes the doctrines of Zhou [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤], the Chengs [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤], and Zhang [Zhang Zai 張載], and uniquely continues the transmission of the Way that had gone unpassed for a thousand years. Looking at what he attained throughout his life, in his repeated audiences with the throne he always spoke exhaustively, and in assuming office he was diligent and earnest, personally attending to the smallest details. As for his plans to serve the ruler and benefit the people, although he could not fully carry out his ambitions, he could still have no shame in his heart; as for his integrity in being reluctant to advance and quick to retire, although he never feigned it to win a reputation, in truth he never compromised himself to seek advancement. Speaking of his breadth of knowledge, even in astronomy, geography, pitch-pipes and calendrical science, and military strategy, he thoroughly investigated their subtlest essentials; discussing his literary writings, even poets and men of talent who exhaust their spirits and energies constantly lament how hard it is to reach his level. For his learning had already grasped the great source, and the Way penetrated everything without exception; truly he may be called a teacher for a hundred generations. In the world today, there is indeed no lack of men with combined talents and extraordinary integrity; what is cause for concern is only that scholarly learning is not clear. Therefore, although the various worthies from the Han dynasty onward have all cast their brilliance across successive generations through their outstanding exemplars, and Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹 of the Song stands out as the foremost figure among them—it is not that I do not love and admire them, wishing to raise…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
斯人而親炙之乃所願則學朱子而已矣
非謂政事文章節義之不必兼也理學既
明而餘者可推也非謂諸賢之不足學也
學貴專一而志有所在也由朱子之訓以
力探乎六經語孟之旨充性命之學以竊
附乎聖賢道統之傳出則行道濟時而功
加上下居則明道淑人而身係綱常愚之
志如斯而已夫山川阻深聲教隔閡特起
而自躍于光明者哲人之逸軌也炳靈發
===
祥前徽在望有所緣而興起者孟軻氏之
所謂凡民也愚也生長于斯日聞休懿卽
志獲竟成猶然非傑矧甘于自棄卽凡民
弗若哉惟執事進而教之幸甚
第五問
袁應陽
同考試官知縣徐　批〔古今稱策士類各攄所見陳時談事不一而足而其眞有裨於理道〕
之猷者亦屈指可數焉是作條陳時務鑿鑿可
punctuated:
斯人而親炙之，乃所願則學朱子而已矣。非謂政事、文章、節義之不必兼也，理學既明而餘者可推也；非謂諸賢之不足學也，學貴專一而志有所在也。由朱子之訓以力探乎《六經》、《語》、《孟》之旨，充性命之學以竊附乎聖賢道統之傳，出則行道濟時而功加上下，居則明道淑人而身係綱常，愚之志如斯而已。夫山川阻深，聲教隔閡，特起而自躍于光明者，哲人之逸軌也；炳靈發祥，前徽在望，有所緣而興起者，孟軻氏之所謂凡民也。愚也生長于斯，日聞休懿，卽志獲竟成，猶然非傑；矧甘于自棄，卽凡民弗若哉！惟執事進而教之，幸甚。

第五問
袁應陽
同考試官知縣徐　批〔古今稱策士，類各攄所見，陳時談事，不一而足；而其眞有裨於理道〕之猷者，亦屈指可數焉。是作條陳時務，鑿鑿可
translation_en:
… these men from the dead and personally receive their instruction, yet what I truly wish is simply to learn from Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹]. This is not to say that statecraft, literary composition, and moral integrity need not be combined; rather, once the Learning of Principle (lixue) is illuminated, the rest can be extended from it. Nor is it to say that the various worthies are not worth emulating; rather, learning prizes single-minded concentration, and one's aspiration must have a definite focus. By following the teachings of Master Zhu to vigorously explore the purport of the Six Classics, the Analects (Lunyu), and the Mencius (Mengzi), and by fulfilling the learning of human nature and destiny so as to humbly attach myself to the transmission of the Succession of the Way (daotong) of the sages and worthies—when going forth into office, to practice the Way and aid the times so that merit reaches both above and below; when dwelling in retirement, to clarify the Way and improve others so that one's person upholds the cardinal guides and constant virtues—my humble aspiration is nothing more than this. Now, where mountains and rivers are deep and obstructing, and where the transforming influence of civilization is cut off, to rise up independently and leap of oneself into the light is the transcendent path of wise men; where numinous brilliance brings forth auspiciousness and the fine models of predecessors are in plain sight, to be roused to action because of such inspiring conditions is what Meng Ke [Mencius] called the "ordinary folk." Born and raised in this region, I daily hear of its splendid and admirable traditions. Even if my aspiration is ultimately fulfilled, I would still not be a hero; how much worse if I willingly abandon myself, becoming not even the equal of ordinary folk! May Your Excellency bring me forward and instruct me; I would be most fortunate.

Question Five
Yuan Yingyang 袁應陽
Comment by Associate Examiner and District Magistrate Xu: 〔Those known across antiquity and the present as policy strategists generally each set forth their own views, presenting current issues and discussing affairs in countless ways; yet those whose counsels truly benefit the principles of governance〕 can be counted on one's fingers. This essay sets forth current affairs point by point, and with concrete certainty can…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
見之行至其所自折衷又不欲以公孫諸流自
安尤徵趨向之正
考試官右中允何　批〔經生抵掌而談當世求不詭于道術時變者絕少子能纚纚剖析咸中肯〕
綮是皆究心經濟者
考試官左中允范　批〔策士之制經濟是論非欲其鉤隱扶微炫才騁博已也是作條對精詳爲〕
國家畫便事如指掌非其抱負恢奇明習世務者曷以有此第令
晁董公孫復生今日必且當予之言矣允宜首
錄以式多士
===
執事發策經篇誘進諸生以鼂董公孫之
故使畢其愚厚矣其望之也夫三子居策
士之林猶鷙鳥之有鶚騏羣之有騄耳喬
林之有豫章由漢以來人代亡慮十數無
不有以自下者愚生安所挾持而希蹤若
是雖然泯泯沁沁居無一物亦士所深耻
也矧方胠篋以來敢誰讓乎且策士何昉
哉其法始于漢文則鼂錯爲之冠其事盛
punctuated:
見之行，至其所自折衷，又不欲以公孫諸流自安，尤徵趨向之正。
考試官右中允何　批〔經生抵掌而談當世，求不詭于道術時變者絕少。子能纚纚剖析，咸中肯〕綮，是皆究心經濟者。
考試官左中允范　批〔策士之制，經濟是論，非欲其鉤隱扶微、炫才騁博已也。是作條對精詳，爲〕國家畫便事如指掌，非其抱負恢奇、明習世務者，曷以有此？第令晁、董、公孫復生今日，必且當予之言矣。允宜首錄，以式多士。
執事發策經篇，誘進諸生以鼂、董、公孫之故，使畢其愚，厚矣其望之也！夫三子居策士之林，猶鷙鳥之有鶚、騏羣之有騄耳、喬林之有豫章。由漢以來，人代亡慮十數，無不有以自下者，愚生安所挾持，而希蹤若是？雖然，泯泯沁沁，居無一物，亦士所深耻也。矧方胠篋以來，敢誰讓乎？且策士何昉哉？其法始于漢文，則鼂錯爲之冠；其事盛
translation_en:
…be put into practice. As for the balanced judgments he arrives at on his own, he refuses to rest content with the likes of Gongsun Hong and his sort, which all the more demonstrates the rectitude of his orientation.

Examiner He, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent, comments: 〔When classical scholars clap their hands and discourse upon contemporary affairs, those who manage not to violate the principles of the Way or the exigencies of the times are exceedingly rare. You are able to analyze matters at length and in orderly fashion, hitting the crucial points in every case;〕 all of this shows one who has devoted his mind to statecraft.

Examiner Fan, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent, comments: 〔The institution of testing scholars by policy questions is meant to discuss statecraft, not merely to have them pry into obscurities and draw out subtleties, showing off their talent and parading their erudition. This essay answers item by item with precision and thoroughness,〕 planning advantageous measures for the state as clearly as pointing to the palm of one's hand. Were he not someone of grand and extraordinary aspirations who clearly understands worldly affairs, how could he achieve this? Even if Chao Cuo, Dong Zhongshu, and Gongsun Hong were born again today, they would surely agree with my words. It is truly fitting to place this first on the roster as a model for the multitude of scholars.

Your Excellency has issued this final policy question, encouraging and guiding us students with the precedents of Chao Cuo, Dong Zhongshu, and Gongsun Hong so that we may fully express our humble thoughts—generous indeed is your expectation of us! Now, those three gentlemen stand among the forest of policy-essayists like the osprey among birds of prey, the thoroughbred Lu'er among herds of fine steeds, or the camphor tree in a lofty forest. Since the Han dynasty, through roughly a dozen dynasties and generations, there has been no one who did not consider himself inferior to them. What do I, a foolish student, possess that I should hope to follow in such footsteps? Even so, to muddle along in obscurity without a single thing to offer is also what a scholar deeply despises. How much more so when, ever since opening my book-boxes to study, to whom would I dare yield? Moreover, when did the testing of scholars by policy questions begin? Its method started under Emperor Wen of the Han, and Chao Cuo stood at the head; the practice flourished…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
于武帝則董仲舒公孫弘擅其雄故文中
子曰洋洋乎鼂董公孫之對蓋取之矣就
而論之錯之得者在貫粟諸篇失者在賢
良一對何也三王討安天下本乎人情是
矣然帝所優為也其曰王帝神聖其臣莫
及非邪說乎曰文帝大功數十非諛詞乎
帝以直言極諫求錯以邪說諛詞應可罪
哉弘之醇者弗足以致主駁者適足以借
資何也禮義刑罰之端道在素行是矣然
===
非其主論也其曰智者術之原果常理乎
曰湯旱桀之餘烈果天戒乎帝詢以道術
治體弘導以悖理忽天曲學哉大惟仲舒
三策吾取焉所明者微言所陳者王道而
帝也侈心方萌見以為迂即嘗因之興太
學表六經黜百家舉孝廉豈為盡其用哉
雖然道有淺深學有陂正吾不能為三子
諱乃其言即可行學即可用鑿鑿非後世
比也今諸生者所謂明枯竹守空言耳摭
punctuated: 于武帝，則董仲舒、公孫弘擅其雄。故文中子曰：「洋洋乎，鼂、董、公孫之對！」蓋取之矣。就而論之，錯之得者，在貴粟諸篇；失者，在賢良一對。何也？三王計安天下本乎人情，是矣，然帝所優為也；其曰五帝神聖其臣莫及，非邪說乎？曰文帝大功數十，非諛詞乎？帝以直言極諫求，錯以邪說諛詞應，可罪哉！弘之醇者弗足以致主，駁者適足以借資。何也？禮義刑罰之端，道在素行，是矣，然非其主論也；其曰智者術之原，果常理乎？曰湯旱桀之餘烈，果天戒乎？帝詢以道術治體，弘導以悖理忽天，曲學哉！大惟仲舒三策吾取焉：所明者微言，所陳者王道，而帝也侈心方萌，見以為迂；即嘗因之興太學、表六經、黜百家、舉孝廉，豈為盡其用哉！雖然，道有淺深，學有陂正，吾不能為三子諱；乃其言即可行，學即可用，鑿鑿非後世比也。今諸生者，所謂明枯竹、守空言耳，摭
translation_en:
… under Emperor Wu, when Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 and Gongsun Hong 公孫弘 claimed preeminence. Thus Master Wenzhong (Wang Tong 王通) said: "How vast and magnificent are the responses of Chao, Dong, and Gongsun!" Clearly, he approved of them.

To examine them in detail: Where Chao Cuo 鼂錯 succeeded was in his essays on valuing grain [here misprinted as 貫粟 for 貴粟] and related pieces; where he failed was in his single response to the decree seeking the "worthy and good" (xianliang). Why is this? That the Three Kings planned for the security of the realm on the basis of human feelings is true enough, yet that was something the Emperor was already more than capable of doing. When he said that the Five Emperors [printed 王帝 for 五帝] were so divinely sage that their ministers could not match them—was that not a perverse doctrine? When he said that Emperor Wen had dozens of great achievements—was that not flattering speech? The Emperor sought forthright words and unsparing remonstrance, yet Cuo responded with perverse doctrines and flattering words—how culpable indeed!

As for Gongsun Hong, what was pure in his thought was insufficient to bring his ruler to perfection, while what was impure served only to lend pretexts to his ruler's inclinations. Why is this? That in the beginnings of ritual, righteousness, and penal law, the Way lies in practicing them first in one's own conduct—this is true enough, yet it was not his main argument. When he said that cleverness is the source of statecraft (shu)—is that truly a constant principle? When he said that the drought under Tang was the lingering ferocity of Jie—is that truly a reverence for Heaven's warnings? The Emperor inquired about the Way, statecraft, and the substance of governance, yet Hong guided him toward defying principle and slighting Heaven—what crooked learning indeed!

On the whole, it is only Dong Zhongshu's three policy essays that I approve of: what he elucidated were subtle words of the sages, and what he set forth was the Kingly Way. Yet extravagant ambitions were just then sprouting in the Emperor's heart, and he regarded Dong's views as impractical. Even though the Emperor did on account of his words establish the Imperial University (Taixue), exalt the Six Classics, dismiss the Hundred Schools, and recommend the "filial and incorrupt" (xiaolian), how could that be considered exhausting his usefulness?

Nevertheless, although the Way has its shallow and deep aspects and learning has its biased and upright forms—shortcomings I cannot conceal on behalf of the three masters—still, their words could be put immediately into practice, and their learning could be put immediately to use, with a concrete certainty unmatched by later generations. The examination candidates of today, however, are what one calls those who merely elucidate dried bamboo slips and cling to empty words. If one gathers…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之握筭未知縱橫試之當塗或昧軌轍何
以究切當世之務歷歷不詭于事情耶蓋
聞之明王不借才于異代天下事豈異人
任乎語曰吹竽滿庭孰辨其美一一聽之
乃識其音愚生請嘗試言之執事請嘗試
聽之教化行然後風俗美今士風尚瀉民
俗尚婾猶謂有敎化乎是故勵躬行則表
率端崇廉讓則勸沮明興禮俗則邪淫去
皆不可緩也厚祿位所以勸親親今
宗患祿窘民困財殫長此欲安極乎是故限
封爵以正倫分弛禁例以廣
===
德厚裁
恩數以節浮冗咸所當議也歛財無餘術宜
制用有奇羨矣乃計往歲出浮于入且百
五十萬今內之度支外之供億雖漸以裁
度可紓目前耳所謂國有九年之蓄積于
不涸之倉者猶未也是在
天子躬行節儉罷宣索愼賫予止興作精搜覈
punctuated: 之握筭，未知縱橫；試之當塗，或昧軌轍。何以究切當世之務，歷歷不詭于事情耶？蓋聞之：「明王不借才于異代。」天下事豈異人任乎？語曰：「吹竽滿庭，孰辨其美？一一聽之，乃識其音。」愚生請嘗試言之，執事請嘗試聽之。教化行然後風俗美，今士風尚瀉，民俗尚婾，猶謂有敎化乎？是故勵躬行則表率端，崇廉讓則勸沮明，興禮俗則邪淫去，皆不可緩也。厚祿位所以勸親親，今宗患祿窘，民困財殫，長此欲安極乎？是故限封爵以正倫分，弛禁例以廣德厚，裁恩數以節浮冗，咸所當議也。歛財無餘術，宜制用有奇羨矣。乃計往歲，出浮于入且百五十萬。今內之度支、外之供億，雖漸以裁度，可紓目前耳；所謂「國有九年之蓄，積于不涸之倉」者，猶未也。是在天子躬行節儉，罷宣索，愼賫予，止興作，精搜覈，
translation_en:
… them to hold the counting rods, they do not know whether to place them vertically or horizontally; test them in positions of authority, and they may be blind to the proper tracks. How then can they thoroughly address the pressing affairs of the present age, item by item without contradicting the actual reality of things? Indeed, I have heard it said: "An enlightened ruler does not borrow talent from another era." Are the affairs of the empire to be left to others to shoulder? The proverb says: "When mouth-organs are played filling the courtyard, who can distinguish which is fine? Only by listening to them one by one can one recognize their true sound." May this foolish student venture to speak of these matters, and may Your Excellency venture to listen.

Only when moral transformation is carried out do customs become beautiful. Today, the ethos of the literati remains shallow [? 瀉, likely for 澆], and the customs of the common people remain frivolous; can it still be said that there is moral transformation? Therefore, encouraging personal conduct so that leadership by example becomes upright, esteeming integrity and deference so that rewards and deterrents become clear, and promoting ritual customs so that perverse and licentious practices are eliminated—none of these can be delayed.

Generous stipends and ranks are the means to encourage affection for Imperial kin. Today, the Imperial clansmen suffer from the inadequacy of their stipends, while the common people are distressed by the exhaustion of their wealth; if this continues, where will it end? Therefore, limiting the enfeoffment of noble titles to rectify hierarchical distinctions, relaxing prohibitive regulations to broaden generous benevolence, and curtailing expressions of Imperial grace to trim superfluous expenditures—all of these ought to be deliberated upon.

Since there are no further methods for extracting revenue, regulating expenditures ought to yield a surplus. Yet if we reckon the past years, expenditures have exceeded revenues by nearly one million five hundred thousand. Today, although the regular disbursements of the court within and the provisioning of supplies without are gradually being curtailed and regulated, this can only relieve the immediate present; as for what is called "a state having nine years of reserves, stored in an inexhaustible granary," that has not yet been achieved. This rests upon the Son of Heaven personally practicing frugality, halting palace requisitions, exercising prudence in bestowing gifts, ceasing construction projects, and conducting thorough audits and verifications—…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
則淳費冗食庶其大省乎承平利右文宜
經籍盈冊府矣乃考
先朝東壁之藏散逸略盡今
文昭所貯
內閣所儲蓋僅可數十才存二三耳視諸天
祿石渠之富三館四庫之多者無幾也是
在
當宁垂情圖史或
遺購或
===
詔求俾各以遺書來上而錄其副則奇文奥
帙庶其間出乎考制度審憲章一稽諸
會典然因革漸歧增損互異所當刊定者多
矣而未有成書今何所守後何所鑒哉謂
宜參訂而葺布之使
典則昭垂較若日月顧不韙歟明刑辟服情
罪一麗諸律然疑文隱義比部廷尉爭若
聚訟者有矣而例益加多傳予曷依趨避
曷措哉謂宜講明而齊一之使科條纖悉
punctuated: 則淳費冗食庶其大省乎！承平利右文，宜經籍盈冊府矣。乃考先朝東壁之藏，散逸略盡；今文昭所貯、內閣所儲，蓋僅可數十，才存二三耳。視諸天祿、石渠之富，三館、四庫之多者，無幾也。是在當宁垂情圖史，或遺購，或詔求，俾各以遺書來上，而錄其副，則奇文奥帙庶其間出乎！考制度，審憲章，一稽諸《會典》。然因革漸歧，增損互異，所當刊定者多矣，而未有成書，今何所守，後何所鑒哉？謂宜參訂而葺布之，使典則昭垂，較若日月，顧不韙歟！明刑辟，服情罪，一麗諸律。然疑文隱義，比部、廷尉爭若聚訟者有矣，而例益加多，傳予曷依，趨避曷措哉？謂宜講明而齊一之，使科條纖悉，
translation_en: …then extravagant expenditures and superfluous stipends will perhaps be greatly reduced! In an era of lasting peace, it is advantageous to esteem civil culture, and the classics and books ought to fill the imperial archives. Yet when we examine the collections of the Eastern Wall [the imperial library] from earlier reigns, they have been almost entirely scattered and lost; today, what is stored in the Wenzhao Pavilion and kept in the Grand Secretariat amounts to scarcely a few dozen [categories?], with only two or three tenths surviving. Compared to the richness of the Tianlu and Shiqu Pavilions [of the Han] or the abundance of the Three Institutes and Four Treasuries [of the Tang and Song], there is very little left. This depends on the reigning sovereign bestowing attention upon maps and histories, either dispatching envoys to purchase them [?] or issuing edicts to seek them out, so that people each submit surviving books to the throne and duplicate copies are transcribed; then rare writings and profound volumes will perhaps occasionally emerge! To examine institutions and scrutinize fundamental statutes, one consults the Collected Statutes (Huidian) in all matters. Yet as continuities and changes have gradually diverged, and additions and deletions have differed from one another, there is much that ought to be edited and fixed; still, there is no completed work. What is the present to abide by, and what is posterity to take as a mirror? I would say they ought to be collated, revised, compiled, and promulgated, so that the institutional canons shine forth and are handed down as clearly as the sun and moon—would this not be right? To clarify punishments and penalties and make the punishment fit the crime and circumstances, one attaches everything to the Code (Lü). Yet over doubtful wording and obscure meanings, there are cases where the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review argue like a clamorous assembly of litigants; meanwhile, sub-statutes (li) have grown ever more numerous. Upon what are those who apply the law [?] to rely, and how are people to know what to pursue or avoid? I would say they ought to be elucidated and made uniform, so that the articles and clauses in all their fine details…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
判若白黑顧不懿歟天下之漸最不可長
者在兵不畏法而易動自振武稱變渠魁
未盡殄戮故時復驕蹇而四方效尤日者
衛兵訌安慶運卒戕侍臣若是屢見告矣
平居如奉驕子緩急責以用命其將能乎
計莫若明約束以絕鼓扇正統馭以起凌
替嚴紀律以警姑息審調補以携黨與恩
威允濟而法令必行如是而軍政不肅未
之有矣積𡚁之弊亟當振舉者在營田久
===
弛而弗理往虜勢猖獗士難解甲就耕卽
乗閒而耕亦秪秣虜馬迺者虜衆旣悔旣
戰士方息肩邊屯稍加墾矣絕徼尚可闢
治內地乃務因循不大舛乎計莫若嚴兼
幷之法正侵隱之罪辨肥瘠之等催逋負
之科任得其人而責成不變如是而屯政
不修未之有矣得失一朝榮辱千載孰重
于史乎然古之史也掌載有專官言動有
記注故核實而傳信今之史也於一世之
punctuated:
判若白黑，顧不懿歟？

天下之漸最不可長者，在兵不畏法而易動。自振武稱變，渠魁未盡殄戮，故時復驕蹇，而四方效尤。日者，衛兵訌安慶，運卒戕侍臣，若是屢見告矣。平居如奉驕子，緩急責以用命，其將能乎？計莫若明約束以絕鼓扇，正統馭以起凌替，嚴紀律以警姑息，審調補以携黨與，恩威允濟而法令必行，如是而軍政不肅，未之有矣。

積𡚁之弊亟當振舉者，在營田久弛而弗理。往虜勢猖獗，士難解甲就耕；卽乗閒而耕，亦秪秣虜馬。迺者，虜衆旣悔旣戰，士方息肩，邊屯稍加墾矣。絕徼尚可闢治，內地乃務因循，不大舛乎？計莫若嚴兼幷之法，正侵隱之罪，辨肥瘠之等，催逋負之科，任得其人而責成不變，如是而屯政不修，未之有矣。

得失一朝，榮辱千載，孰重于史乎？然古之史也，掌載有專官，言動有記注，故核實而傳信。今之史也，於一世之
translation_en:
…as distinct as black and white—would that not be admirable?

Among the tendencies in the realm that must least of all be allowed to grow is that soldiers do not fear the law and are easily stirred to unrest. Ever since the Zhenwu Camp (Zhenwu ying 振武營) mutinied and its ringleaders were not all exterminated, troops have from time to time again grown arrogant and unruly, and the four quarters have followed their bad example. Recently, guard soldiers raised a tumult in Anqing, and grain-transport troops murdered an attending official; incidents such as these have been repeatedly reported. In ordinary times they are coddled like spoiled children; if in an emergency we demand that they lay down their lives on command, will they be capable of doing so? The best plan is to clarify regulations so as to cut off incitement, rectify command and control so as to revive declining authority, tighten discipline so as to warn against lax indulgence, and carefully manage transfers and replacements so as to break up cliques and factions. When grace and awe complement each other and laws and orders are unfailingly enforced, never has it happened that military administration was not brought to order under such conditions.

Among the accumulated abuses that urgently require revitalization is that military farms (yingtian 營田) have long been neglected and left unmanaged. In the past, when the northern nomads were rampant, soldiers could hardly take off their armor to go plow; and even if they seized a lull to plow, it merely served to feed the nomads' horses. Recently, now that the nomad hordes have shown remorse [?] and soldiers have just rested their shoulders, the frontier state farms (biantun 邊屯) have gradually been brought under cultivation again. If even the farthest frontiers can be opened up and cultivated, is it not a great absurdity that the interior instead clings to negligent routine? The best plan is to enforce strictly the laws against land engrossment, punish the crimes of encroachment and concealment, distinguish the grades of fertile and barren land, press the collection of tax arrears, entrust the task to the right men, and hold them unswervingly to results. Under such conditions, never has it happened that state-farm administration (tunzheng 屯政) was not put in order.

Success and failure belong to a single reign, yet honor and disgrace last a thousand years: what is weightier than history? Yet in the history-writing of antiquity, there were dedicated officials in charge of recording, and diaries of activity and repose for words and deeds; therefore it verified the facts and transmitted trustworthy accounts. In the history-writing of today, at the…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
終而追筆乎數十年之事見聞鮮覈奏疏
是憑職不可謂舉矣請復
祖制特簡史官俾領其任凡
九重之起居臣工之論列大政事之因革弛張
大臣僚之陞降拜罷皆隨時紀錄據事直
書將必有如董狐之書法不隱南史之執
簡以往者矣今之史非古之史哉平心宣
化崇德象功孰大于樂乎然古之樂也八
音諧其節律呂和其聲故召和而鳴盛今
===
之樂也器數既已久亡而神理因之弗著
太常樂部尚襲舊物制不可謂備矣請設
樂學擇審音文臣專掌其事按元定之書
求后夔之意習節奏之變審聲氣之元且
假以歲年俟其自得將必有如師曠州鳩
之神解寶常令言之妙悟者矣今之樂非
古之樂哉
國家所以廢海運者以會通河也然自河漕
沮而復求海運以濟飛輓蓋一險一勞等
punctuated:
終，而追筆乎數十年之事，見聞鮮覈，奏疏是憑，職不可謂舉矣。請復祖制，特簡史官，俾領其任。凡九重之起居、臣工之論列、大政事之因革弛張、大臣僚之陞降拜罷，皆隨時紀錄，據事直書，將必有如董狐之書法不隱、南史之執簡以往者矣。今之史非古之史哉！

平心宣化，崇德象功，孰大于樂乎？然古之樂也，八音諧其節，律呂和其聲，故召和而鳴盛；今之樂也，器數既已久亡，而神理因之弗著，太常樂部尚襲舊物，制不可謂備矣。請設樂學，擇審音文臣專掌其事，按元定之書，求后夔之意，習節奏之變，審聲氣之元，且假以歲年，俟其自得，將必有如師曠、州鳩之神解，寶常、令言之妙悟者矣。今之樂非古之樂哉！

國家所以廢海運者，以會通河也。然自河漕沮而復求海運以濟飛輓，蓋一險一勞，等…
translation_en:
… end of a reign, writing retrospectively about the events of several decades; what is seen and heard is rarely verified, and memorials alone are relied upon—their duties cannot be said to be fulfilled! I beg that we restore the Ancestral System, specially selecting Historiographers and having them take charge of this responsibility. All the daily activities and utterances of the Sovereign, the deliberations and remonstrances of the officials, the continuities, reforms, relaxations, and tightenings of major state policies, and the promotions, demotions, appointments, and dismissals of grand ministers and officials should all be recorded as they occur and written down straightforwardly according to the facts. Then there will surely be men like Dong Hu 董狐, whose historiographical principles concealed nothing, and Master Nan (Nanshi 南史), who took up his bamboo slips and went forth. Would the histories of today not be the histories of antiquity?

For calming the mind and spreading moral transformation, exalting virtue and symbolizing merit, what is greater than music? Yet in the music of antiquity, the eight timbres harmonized its rhythms and the twelve pitch-pipes blended its tones, thereby summoning harmony and sounding forth prosperity. In the music of today, the instruments and numerical proportions have already long been lost, and the spiritual principles behind them have consequently become obscure; the Music Boards of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices still follow old conventions, and the institution cannot be said to be complete! I beg that we establish a School of Music and select civil officials who understand sound to take sole charge of the matter—consulting the books of Cai Yuanding 蔡元定, seeking the intent of Minister Kui 后夔, practicing the variations of rhythm and tempo, and examining the primal origins of sound and vital breath. Moreover, if they are granted sufficient years until they attain comprehension for themselves, there will surely be men with the divine understanding of Music Master Kuang (Shi Kuang 師曠) and Ling Zhoujiu 泠州鳩, or the marvelous enlightenment of Wan Baochang 萬寶常 and Liu Lingyan 劉令言. Would the music of today not be the music of antiquity?

The reason the State abolished maritime grain transport was because of the Huitong Canal (會通河). Yet ever since canal transport was obstructed and maritime transport was once again sought to aid rapid conveyance—for one is perilous and the other laborious, they are equal …

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
耳今捷而效矣乃不兩利俱存而屢章請
罷何以說也愚以爲河雖安矣而勢難永
利海雖險矣而道實常通要于未事之先
爲意外之慮則方其無事也河爲常而海
亦暫脫其有事也彼不至而此必來矣如
是則其罷也奚便
國家所以懷熟夷者以屛蔽虜也然每市外
交而恐喝疆埸之臣以要賞益貨在虜方
不靖可耳今虜輸款矣乃不俛服于我而
撓邊如故何以說也愚以爲戒之不悛則
固求其人罪之罪之不得則潛出銳師剿
===
之要以不傷
國重不起禍階則三衛常爲我司門之衕而
不至爲我附頸之癭矣如是則其戢也奚
難夫執事所詢類皆
朝廷之大制作大機宜大經濟草莽之士有
當年不能窮累世不能殫者而師心質言
若是蓋方用經術世務進即意僂僂希古
punctuated:
耳。今捷而效矣，乃不兩利俱存，而屢章請罷，何以說也？愚以爲河雖安矣，而勢難永利；海雖險矣，而道實常通。要于未事之先，爲意外之慮。則方其無事也，河爲常而海亦暫；脫其有事也，彼不至而此必來矣。如是，則其罷也奚便？
國家所以懷熟夷者，以屛蔽虜也。然每市外交而恐喝疆埸之臣，以要賞益貨。在虜方不靖，可耳。今虜輸款矣，乃不俛服于我，而撓邊如故，何以說也？愚以爲戒之不悛，則固求其人罪之；罪之不得，則潛出銳師剿之。要以不傷國重，不起禍階，則三衛常爲我司門之衕，而不至爲我附頸之癭矣。如是，則其戢也奚難？
夫執事所詢，類皆朝廷之大制作、大機宜、大經濟，草莽之士有當年不能窮、累世不能殫者，而師心質言若是，蓋方用經術世務進，即意僂僂希古
translation_en:
… equal. Now that [sea transport] has proved swift and effective, why do they not preserve the benefits of both, instead submitting repeated memorials requesting its abolition? How is this to be explained? In my humble opinion, although the Grand Canal is safe, its circumstances make it difficult to rely on as a permanent advantage; although the sea route is perilous, the passage is in fact always open. The key is to prepare for the unexpected before trouble arises. Thus, in times of peace, the canal serves as the regular route while the sea route is used provisionally; should an emergency occur, if grain cannot arrive by the former, it will surely come by the latter. If this is so, what advantage is there in abolishing it?

The reason the State cherishes the assimilated Yi barbarians is to use them as a screen against the northern caitiffs. Yet they constantly trade on their external connections to intimidate our frontier officials, demanding rewards and increased goods. When the caitiffs were still unpacified, this was perhaps tolerable. Now that the caitiffs have submitted in allegiance, why do [the assimilated Yi] not bow in submission to us, instead disturbing the frontier just as before? How is this to be explained? In my humble opinion, if we warn them and they do not repent, we should firmly demand the culprits and punish them; if we cannot obtain and punish them, we should secretly dispatch elite troops to suppress them. The essential point is neither to impair the dignity of the State nor to provoke the beginnings of disaster. Then the Three Guards (Sanwei) will always serve as a protective watch at our gates, rather than becoming a goiter attached to our neck. If we act in this way, what difficulty will there be in restraining them?

Now, the matters about which you, the examiners, have inquired are all great institutions, great strategic affairs, and great statecraft of the court—matters which a rustic scholar could not exhaust in a lifetime nor fully master across generations. Yet I have followed my own judgment and spoken plainly like this because, at a time when candidates are advanced on the basis of classical learning and practical statecraft, even as my humble aspiration is to emulate the…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
人亦願爲董江都不願爲鼂大夫公孫丞
相何也哆口無驗而詭道以阿世亦執事
之所羞耳若擘畫未審而研究弗精則經
生之陋也雖然猶有說焉自我
祖宗以來立國規模綱目不啻備矣非有極重
不可反大壞不可捄者特恢弘治理潤色
鴻業存乎其人焉耳若講求靡至是未操刀
之割也議論徒多是築道旁之舍也更張
罔漸是攺已調之瑟也皆不如其已者也
===
今
明良合德千載一時誠
上下勤恤煥然勵精則一爲而一成百爲而百
成無弗奏功者苟爲不然將朝作而莫隳
昔行而今罷何以爲屈羣策之本哉執事
倘與其進願執此以往
punctuated: 人，亦願爲董江都，不願爲鼂大夫、公孫丞相。何也？哆口無驗，而詭道以阿世，亦執事之所羞耳；若擘畫未審而研究弗精，則經生之陋也。雖然，猶有說焉。自我祖宗以來，立國規模，綱目不啻備矣，非有極重不可反、大壞不可捄者，特恢弘治理、潤色鴻業，存乎其人焉耳。若講求靡至，是未操刀之割也；議論徒多，是築道旁之舍也；更張罔漸，是攺已調之瑟也，皆不如其已者也。今明良合德，千載一時，誠上下勤恤，煥然勵精，則一爲而一成，百爲而百成，無弗奏功者。苟爲不然，將朝作而莫隳，昔行而今罷，何以爲屈羣策之本哉？執事倘與其進，願執此以往。
translation_en: … the ancients, I too would rather be Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 of Jiangdu than Grand Master Chao Cuo 鼂錯 or Counselor-in-Chief Gongsun Hong 公孫弘. Why is this? Boasting widely without practical verification, or twisting the Way to flatter the age, are things of which you, Sir, would also be ashamed; yet if my planning is not thorough and my investigation not precise, that is simply the narrow-mindedness of a mere student of the Classics. Even so, there is still more to say. Ever since our Imperial Ancestors founded the dynasty, the overall framework of the state, in both its main principles and detailed provisions, has been more than complete. There is nothing so entrenched in decline that it cannot be reversed, nor so gravely ruined that it cannot be rescued; rather, expanding the reach of good governance and adding luster to the great enterprise depend solely upon having the right men. If deliberation and investigation are not thorough, it is like trying to cut before one knows how to wield a knife; if discussions are merely numerous in vain, it is like building a house by the roadside; if reforms are made without gradual progression, it is like re-stringing a zither that is already in tune—in all these cases, it would be better simply to desist. Now an enlightened sovereign and worthy ministers are united in virtue, an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years. If superior and inferior truly show diligent solicitude and brilliantly rouse their spirits to govern, then every single undertaking will succeed and a hundred undertakings will succeed a hundredfold, with nothing failing to achieve results. Should it not be so, then what is initiated in the morning will be ruined by evening, and what was practiced in the past will be abandoned today—how then could one establish the foundation for harnessing the combined counsels of all? Should you, Sir, approve of my advancement, I wish to hold fast to these principles as I go forward.

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄後序
聖天子萬曆初元天下適當賓興
士於鄉應天府臣以請
上命臣應期臣洛文往典試事錄
成臣洛文宜序諸末簡臣竊
自惟學術行能淺鮮無異荷
先帝簡掄侍
===
上青宮繼値
上位宸極臣復日奉
講讀兩蒙
拔擢以至今官方竭誠効愚罔
裨萬一乃茲被
命校士遣自
經幄
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄後序

聖天子萬曆初元，天下適當賓興士於鄉。應天府臣以請，上命臣應期、臣洛文往典試事。錄成，臣洛文宜序諸末簡。臣竊自惟學術行能淺鮮無異，荷先帝簡掄，侍上青宮。繼値上位宸極，臣復日奉講讀，兩蒙拔擢以至今官。方竭誠効愚，罔裨萬一，乃茲被命校士，遣自經幄，
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination

In the first year of the Wanli era (1573) of the Sacred Son of Heaven, it was just the time throughout the realm to fete and recommend scholars for the provincial examinations. Upon the request of the officials of Yingtian Prefecture (Nanjing), His Majesty commanded Your Servant [Wang] Yingqi 王應期 and Your Servant [Dai] Luowen 戴洵 (zi Luowen 洛文) to go and preside over the examination affairs. Now that the examination record has been completed, it is fitting for Your Servant Luowen to write a postface at the end of the volume.

Reflecting privately upon myself, Your Servant possesses shallow and meager learning and ability, with nothing out of the ordinary. Yet I was favored with selection by the Late Emperor to attend upon His Majesty in the Heir Apparent's Palace (Qinggong). Subsequently, when His Majesty ascended the imperial throne, Your Servant again served daily as Lecturer and Reader, and twice received promotion to reach my present office. Just as I was exhausting my sincerity and offering my humble efforts without contributing even one part in ten thousand, I have now received the command to examine the scholars, dispatched directly from the Classics Mat…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
任使過隆豈非
殊常遘遇哉已復思
留都寔
聖世鎬京士生且游其間有山川
之秀發而
豐芑詒育所從來久蓋已幸矣
矧
===
今天子龍飛伊始
聖神立極文教聿新且外賔內寧
士得一意被服儒術湛涵道
德人文興起愈斌斌焉不尤
幸歟夫士幸會
昌期乃無名世者應
運嚮臻士之耻也誠有之而臣
punctuated: 任使過隆，豈非殊常遘遇哉！已復思留都寔聖世鎬京，士生且游其間，有山川之秀發，而豐芑詒育，所從來久，蓋已幸矣。矧今天子龍飛伊始，聖神立極，文教聿新，且外賔內寧，士得一意被服儒術，湛涵道德，人文興起，愈斌斌焉，不尤幸歟！夫士幸會昌期，乃無名世者應運嚮臻，士之耻也；誠有之，而臣
translation_en: …The responsibilities entrusted to me are surpassingly generous; is this not an extraordinary encounter of imperial favor? Yet when I reflect further, the Auxiliary Capital is truly the Haojing of our sacred age. Scholars born or studying within its precincts enjoy the flourishing beauty of its mountains and rivers, and the nurturing legacy of Feng and Qi has endured here from of old—this is already fortunate indeed. How much more so now, at the very beginning of the Reigning Son of Heaven's dragon flight to the throne, when sage and divine, He establishes the supreme standard, cultural teachings are newly revitalized, and with foreign peoples submitting as guests and the interior at peace, scholars are able to devote themselves single-mindedly to embracing Confucian arts and immersing themselves in morality and virtue, so that literary and moral culture rises up ever more harmoniously refined—is this not even more fortunate? Now, when scholars are fortunate enough to meet with a flourishing era, if there are no men of world-renowned eminence who step forward in response to theTurning of Destiny, that is the shame of the scholars; yet if such men truly exist, and Your Servant…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
弗克知遺諸所舉之外
殊遇之謂何故自受
命以來夙夜祇惕比入院偕諸執
事矢公盡慎已而閱諸士文
蒿目焦思程以尺度而準諸
理奧若辨淄澠窮濊汲必彬
彬質有其文者乃收之念且
===
獻諸
天府輒竦然曰才誠在是庶幾哉
其惟吉士進而在列斯足光
輔
帝德在宥而理萬方矣乎雖然是
曷敢知昔孔子卜而不取于
賁惡離真也士苟修詞措躬
punctuated: 弗克知，遺諸所舉之外，殊遇之謂何？故自受命以來，夙夜祇惕。比入院，偕諸執事矢公盡慎；已而閱諸士文，蒿目焦思，程以尺度，而準諸理奧，若辨淄澠、窮濊汲，必彬彬質有其文者乃收之。念且獻諸天府，輒竦然曰：「才誠在是！庶幾哉，其惟吉士，進而在列，斯足光輔帝德，在宥而理萬方矣乎！」雖然，是曷敢知？昔孔子卜而不取于賁，惡離真也。士苟修詞措躬，
translation_en: …am unable to recognize them, leaving them outside the ranks of those selected, what then could be said of the extraordinary favor I have received? Therefore, ever since receiving my commission, I have been reverently fearful day and night. When I entered the examination compound, together with all the officiating functionaries I swore to be impartial and exercised the utmost caution. Afterward, in reviewing the essays of the scholars, I strained my eyes and racked my brains, measuring them against the standards and gauging them by the profundities of principle. As if distinguishing the waters of the Zi and Sheng rivers or fathoming the depths of drawing from a well [? 窮濊汲], only those in whom substance and refinement were in due proportion did we accept. Thinking of how their names were soon to be presented to the Imperial Treasury, I was repeatedly struck with awe, saying to myself: "True talent lies herein! May it be that these worthy scholars, advancing to take their places in the official ranks, will suffice to gloriously assist the Imperial virtue, governing the myriad regions in tolerant forbearance!" Even so, how dare I claim to know this for certain? In antiquity, when Confucius divined and drew the hexagram Bi (Grace), he was displeased with it because he disliked that which departs from genuine substance. If a scholar cultivates his words and conducts himself…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
較若左劵璚而璚珉而珉朱
而朱紫而紫雅音而連謱郎
雅音而連謱無或爽者則臣
竊可信得士異時徵諸實用
足圖萬一之報矣脫或本末
謬盭初終岐判雖言澤道德
十不一鑣徒枝經術以爲取
===
世之資直優孟之抵掌耳是
安所貴才矣郎㑹文者覃精
品鏡處且儀毛而失牆儀髮
而易貌殆實鄭璞而瑞昭明
等耳人亦有言試而得人若
博之中呼也試而失人若博
之遺質也何也非有參驗之
punctuated: 較若左劵，璚而璚、珉而珉，朱而朱、紫而紫，雅音而連謱郎〔？〕雅音而連謱，無或爽者，則臣竊可信得士，異時徵諸實用，足圖萬一之報矣。脫或本末謬盭，初終岐判，雖言澤道德，十不一鑣，徒枝經術以爲取世之資，直優孟之抵掌耳，是安所貴才矣？郎㑹文者覃精品鏡，處且儀毛而失牆、儀髮而易貌，殆實鄭璞而瑞昭明等耳。人亦有言：「試而得人，若博之中呼也；試而失人，若博之遺質也。」何也？非有參驗之
translation_en:
…tally like the left half of a contract: if fine jade is truly fine jade and common stone is truly common stone, if vermilion is truly vermilion and purple is truly purple, if refined music is refined music and rambling ditties [連謱, reading 郎 as 即] are rambling ditties, without the slightest discrepancy—then I, your servant, may venture to believe that we have obtained true scholars, and when they are later tested in practical application, it will suffice as a one-in-ten-thousandth repayment to Your Majesty.

Should it happen that root and branch are at odds, or beginning and end diverge—even if their words are steeped in morality, yet not one in ten keeps pace in action, merely embellishing classical learning as a means to win worldly advancement—that would be nothing more than the actor Meng clapping his hands in impersonation! Where then would be the value of talent? Even if [reading 郎 as 即] those who evaluate the essays exhaust their minds in critical appraisal, they would still be judging a horse by its coat while missing its frame, or judging a person by his hair while mistaking his features; it would be virtually no different from treating a rat-carcass from Zheng as uncut jade or mistaking it for an auspicious luminous gem [?].

As people also have a saying: "Testing and obtaining the right men is like calling the winning throw in a game of dice; testing and missing the right men is like losing one's stake in the game [?]." Why is this so? Is it not because there is no means of cross-verifying…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
首善者邪抑昔之謂不朽者雖
左言而右功然虞以言揚周
用藝興庸可廢諸千載而下
窺尹旦經綸之心者以尹旦
之文遡尼軻計道之心者以
尼軻之文慕賈董康濟之心
者以賈董之文諸士蓋謂法
===
伊周孔孟不第以賈董自許
者臣方選才
盛世匪言是徵先資其奚以焉
顧臣所能者校士以經術世
務中程而後取之如是止耳
脫猶不副所舉卽臣無所逃
責然可若何矣乃士既錄行
punctuated: 首善者邪？抑昔之謂不朽者，雖左言而右功，然虞以言揚，周用藝興，庸可廢諸？千載而下，窺尹、旦經綸之心者，以尹、旦之文；遡尼、軻計道之心者，以尼、軻之文；慕賈、董康濟之心者，以賈、董之文。諸士蓋謂法伊、周、孔、孟，不第以賈、董自許者。臣方選才盛世，匪言是徵，先資其奚以焉？顧臣所能者，校士以經術、世務，中程而後取之，如是止耳。脫猶不副所舉，卽臣無所逃責，然可若何矣！乃士既錄，行
translation_en: …model of excellence [in the capital]? Or again, in what the ancients called "immortality," although establishing words was ranked below establishing meritorious deeds, nevertheless under Yu [Shun] men were promoted on the basis of their words, and under the Zhou they were raised up by means of the six arts—how could literary expression be dispensed with? A thousand years later, those who peer into the minds of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou (Dan) regarding statecraft do so through the writings of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; those who trace back the minds of Confucius (Zhongni) and Mencius (Meng Ke) in taking the measure of the Way do so through the writings of Confucius and Mencius; and those who admire the minds of Jia Yi and Dong Zhongshu in bringing peace and relief to the world do so through the writings of Jia Yi and Dong Zhongshu. The scholars here presumably claim to model themselves on Yi Yin, the Duke of Zhou, Confucius, and Mencius, and do not merely set Jia Yi and Dong Zhongshu as their standard. As your servant is right now selecting talent for a flourishing age, if I do not take their words as evidence, by what means can they present their initial pledge of service? Yet all your servant is capable of doing is examining the scholars in classical scholarship and practical statecraft, and selecting them only after they meet the standard—nothing more than this. Should they still fail to live up to their recommendation, even though your servant cannot escape responsibility, what more could I have done! Now that the scholars have been recorded, they are about to…

title: 萬曆元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
詳而觀察之可賴也是故錄
成而〔臣〕滋竊竊焉以懼然竊
聞之求玉于崑岡不乏瓌寶
求驥于冀野不乏逸足夫
南都亦士之崑岡冀野也而患
無連城與千里者是〔臣〕之計
過也且夫世平
主聖俊乂將自至雲從物覩機有
固然今
===
堯舜在上
典學
勤政進賢興理
德意所嚮郎遐陬殊類當靡然顧
化矧都人士感會
punctuated: 詳，而觀察之可賴也。是故錄成而〔臣〕滋竊竊焉以懼。然竊聞之：求玉于崑岡，不乏瓌寶；求驥于冀野，不乏逸足。夫南都亦士之崑岡、冀野也，而患無連城與千里者，是〔臣〕之計過也。且夫世平主聖，俊乂將自至，雲從物覩，機有固然。今堯舜在上，典學勤政，進賢興理，德意所嚮，郎遐陬殊類，當靡然顧化，矧都人士感會
translation_en: … become manifest in detail, and our observation of them can be relied upon. Therefore, as this record is completed, I am all the more filled with private trepidation. Yet I have heard it said that when one seeks jade on Mount Kun, there is no lack of rare treasures; when one seeks fine steeds in the wilds of Ji, there is no lack of fleet-footed horses. Now the Southern Capital is likewise the Mount Kun and the wilds of Ji for scholars; to worry that there are none worth a string of cities or capable of running a thousand li would be a miscalculation on my part. Moveover, when the age is at peace and the Sovereign is sage, men of outstanding talent will come forward of their own accord; like clouds following the dragon and all creatures beholding the sage, such is the natural working of things. Now that a Yao or Shun reigns above, devoted to learning and diligent in governance, advancing the worthy and promoting order, wherever His virtuous intentions are directed, even [reading 郎 as 即] those in distant corners and of different kinds will bow like grass before the wind and turn toward transformation—how much more so when the scholars of the capital are moved by and meet with…
